| | | This is State Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA). But _it's not too late to believe in Louisiana_ and pull off the unthinkable. In one of our reddest seats, LA-05, we lead by less than 1% and have forced a December 12 runoff where we can flip this seat. Clawing out this narrow lead took everything; **our bank account now shows a 3 digit balance**. And our GOP opponent has outraised us 20-1 with just mere weeks left to catch up. clean_body: Hard-fought victories right here in Wisconsin | | | | Last week, Rebecca Cooke and Mitchell Berman flipped two crucial House seats in battleground districts right here in Wisconsin! Today, we’re asking supporters to endorse Rebecca and Mitchell. | | Democrats won hard-fought victories in WI-01 and WI-03 because of the hard work of grassroots supporters like you. Here’s a recap of the Republican spending we were up against: | 🔴 Donald Trump committed $90,000 to Mitchell’s opponent, Bryan Steil. 🔴 Elon Musk funneled thousands of dollars to Rebecca’s opponent, Derrick Van Orden, helping fund multiple seven-figure attack ads against her. 🔴 MAGA billionaires like the Uihlein family and Diane Hendricks poured millions into the Wisconsin GOP, funding both Van Orden’s and Steil’s campaigns. Rebecca and Mitch ran tough campaigns against staggering Republican spending, and they won! Now we’re asking supporters in your community to show just how many people are standing behind them. | Thank you, Battleground Wisconsin * | | | | ---|---|---|--- | AS GOES WISCONSIN, SO GOES THE NATION Our party is committed to advancing progressive values and ensuring Democratic victories up and down the ballot. | | I promised you that I would hold Donald Trump and his cronies accountable. **That means standing up when this administration abuses its power, demanding answers when it fails the American people, and making sure no one is above the law.** This week, I have been doing just that. **After more than 100 days in an ICE detention center in Tacoma over a paperwork problem, Conway resident Juan Martinez is finally home.** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143304903/659775353/-351759073?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMDdkZDAxNi0yZmRlLWYxMTEtOTFmNS0wMDIyNDgyNGQ5ZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=92TJWtVTJom2Ub_h1lKvG94HC66SWNPRoDkhfJpFFiQ=&emci=571104a3-13de-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&emdi=f07dd016-2fde-f111-91f5-00224824d9f7&ceid=9494239)** I am glad I could help Juan return to his family and community. **But let us be clear: No one should spend more than three months in detention because of a paperwork issue.** The Trump administration's reckless deportation agenda is causing real harm to people in our communities. I will keep fighting to ensure ICE follows the same rules as every other law enforcement agency and that families like Juan's get the answers and treatment they deserve. **I also continue to believe Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is unfit to lead the Pentagon. In March 2025, I called for his immediate resignation or firing. Tuesday, I supported impeaching him for his incompetent leadership.** But instead of allowing the House to debate and vote on impeachment, House Republicans voted 211 to 204 to block consideration of the resolution on procedural grounds. Once again, Republicans chose to protect this administration rather than hold it accountable. That will not stop me. I will continue looking for every opportunity to hold Secretary Hegseth accountable for his failures. This fight is not over. **With a new Democratic majority in the House, we will have the opportunity to turn accountability into action. We will conduct meaningful oversight, demand answers, investigate abuses of power, and make clear that this administration is not above the law.** I promised you that I would stand up to Trump and his cronies. I intend to keep that promise. **Juan Martinez is home. The fight for accountability at the Pentagon continues. And when Democrats take the majority, we will have even more tools to make this administration answer for its actions.** This is what accountability looks like. _Rick_ | Express Donate: If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution to Rick Larsen instantly:

clean_body: When Democrats take the majority, we will have even more tools to make this administration answer for its actions. | | | | I promised you that I would hold Donald Trump and his cronies accountable. That means standing up when this administration abuses its power, demanding answers when it fails the American people, and making sure no one is above the law. This week, I have been doing just that. After more than 100 days in an ICE detention center in Tacoma over a paperwork problem, Conway resident Juan Martinez is finally home. I am glad I could help Juan return to his family and community. But let us be clear: No one should spend more than three months in detention because of a paperwork issue. The Trump administration's reckless deportation agenda is causing real harm to people in our communities. I will keep fighting to ensure ICE follows the same rules as every other law enforcement agency and that families like Juan's get the answers and treatment they deserve. I also continue to believe Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is unfit to lead the Pentagon. In March 2025, I called for his immediate resignation or firing. Tuesday, I supported impeaching him for his incompetent leadership. But instead of allowing the House to debate and vote on impeachment, House Republicans voted 211 to 204 to block consideration of the resolution on procedural grounds. Once again, Republicans chose to protect this administration rather than hold it accountable. That will not stop me. I will continue looking for every opportunity to hold Secretary Hegseth accountable for his failures. This fight is not over. With a new Democratic majority in the House, we will have the opportunity to turn accountability into action. We will conduct meaningful oversight, demand answers, investigate abuses of power, and make clear that this administration is not above the law. I promised you that I would stand up to Trump and his cronies. I intend to keep that promise. Juan Martinez is home. The fight for accountability at the Pentagon continues. And when Democrats take the majority, we will have even more tools to make this administration answer for its actions. This is what accountability looks like. Today is Veterans Day, and I want to take a moment to recognize the service of thousands of Americans in our armed forces, and their children and families.

These brave men and women put their lives on the line and sacrificed to protect our country’s freedom and democracy both at home and abroad.

It is our veterans who are putting their lives at risk so we can continue to better our lives, communities, and nation.

As your Congressmember, I promise to always advocate for the best interests of our veterans and current service members. Our government has a responsibility to ensure our veterans receive the quality care and benefits they deserve.

So today, I hope you will take a minute out of your day to honor these heroes.

And to our veterans in Ohio’s first Congressional District and beyond — I deeply thank you for your service to our country. From the bottom of my heart, thank you for your service and your sacrifice.

Peace and Love 🙏💙,

Greg Landsman

body:
The race for my old House seat is one of the closest elections of 2026.
#
Peter,
Though the midterm elections happened over a week ago, the race for my old U.S. House seat in Minnesota’s 1st district still hasn’t officially been called.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261112-jj.fDfg32&amount=5&refcode=em20261112-1338&t=1&akid=1338%2E34582%2EtTWifr)
**With 99 percent of votes counted, it looks like Small Town PAC-endorsed Democrat Jake Johnson won. But since he’s only up by a razor-thin margin of about 300 votes, less than 0.1 percent, his Republican opponent has requested a recount.**

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Some questions I’ve been asked
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Earlier this week, I did an Instagram Live where I talked about a number of topics and answered a few questions from folks.
Here are some of the questions I am getting most frequently since last week's election -- I thought maybe you'd be interested in the answers.
**What do you make of Stephen Miller as the next White House Chief of Staff?**
Donald Trump made a decision, after a historic midterm election that was at least in part a rebuke of his immigration policy, to appoint Stephen Miller, to affirm and uplift the worst and most cruel ICE policy that they have to offer.
I think it’s actually a very dangerous point that we’re at in our country, because the president is so unstable. And for Stephen Miller to be the primary advisor to the president, I think, actually puts our entire nation in a very risky and volatile place.
So the fact of the matter is, I think that Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff is completely untenable and unacceptable to the American people -- And it is certainly in direct contradiction to what the American people voted for a week ago.
**Thoughts on the grip of AIPAC after the last election?**
It is still large, but this election dealt a historic blow to AIPAC. Their whole premise was that they will do everything they can to guarantee your election if you're with them, and will find and fund a successful primary against you if you go against them.
Tragically, they've engaged in a horrific amount of bullying, racist campaigning and intimidation that worked for a long time. But that blew up this cycle. This year, many members gave up AIPAC money and others like Abdul El-Sayed beat AIPAC despite their tens of millions of dollars spent against him and other Democrats in primaries.
AIPAC is no longer seen as the omnipotent power they once marketed themselves as and that will give people the courage to walk a different path. However, they do remain very powerful, and a majority of Congress is still affiliated with them.
**Are you going to run for re-election, for the Senate or for president?**
The last thing that people want to hear about from me or any other politician today is the next election. We have a responsibility to the American people to lay out what we plan to do with the power they just gave us last Tuesday - that includes everything from halting Trump’s Medicaid cliff and ending the war in Iran, to getting big money out of politics and taking on corporate oligopolies gouging prices on working people. They want to know about the legislation and investigations that are going to be happening. What are we going to do about health care, affordability, the war in Iran and more. There will be time for the rest of that.
**How often do you do these Instagram Lives and how can I ask questions?**
I try to do them from time to time because there's no substitute for being able to speak directly to people without a filter. The conversations we had earlier this week lasted almost two hours. You can follow me on Instagram and see the conversations there.
**[But if there's a message you'd like to share with me or a question you want to ask, you can do it here.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/send_a_message_to_aoc/?source=em-261112&t=3&akid=12500%2E2526796%2ElsdBbk)**
**[https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/message-aoc](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/send_a_message_to_aoc/?source=em-261112&t=4&akid=12500%2E2526796%2ElsdBbk)**
**[SHARE SOMETHING WITH AOC](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/send_a_message_to_aoc/?source=em-261112&t=5&akid=12500%2E2526796%2ElsdBbk)**
I won't be able to look at every comment, just like I can't look at them all while on a Live, but someone on my team will read them and get stuff up to me.
Talk soon.
In solidarity,
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

name: Jane Fonda
subject: Three historic wins
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee
body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=24%2E6803%2EBNyyk4)
I've spent most of my life fighting for a better future. On Election Day, I watched history unfold in ways that reminded me exactly why I never stopped.
**Three remarkable women shattered barriers that had stood for generations. I couldn't be prouder that JanePAC stood behind each of them. Let me introduce you:**
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261112-ak.abAXI3&refcode=em20261112-24&t=3&akid=24%2E6803%2EBNyyk4)
**Senator-Elect Peggy Flanagan:** Peggy is making history as the nation’s first Native American woman to serve in the U.S. Senate. As Minnesota’s Lieutenant Governor, she helped establish a 100% carbon-free energy standard by 2040 and secured over $1 billion for climate resilience and clean energy. In the Senate, she will stand up to Trump’s cruel agenda, block ICE raids in schools, and fight for an immigration system rooted in human dignity and safety for all of us.
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261112-ak.abAXI3&refcode=em20261112-24&t=4&akid=24%2E6803%2EBNyyk4)
**Governor-Elect Deb Haaland:** Deb is officially the country's first Native American woman governor. Deb and I have been in the trenches together for years. She is the exact leader I had in mind when founding the Jane Fonda Climate PAC: someone who listens to community voices, stands up to polluters, and never hesitates to put people over corporate profits. As governor of New Mexico, she is ready to protect our drying Rio Grande, lower energy costs, and treat the climate crisis with the urgency it demands.
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261112-ak.abAXI3&refcode=em20261112-24&t=5&akid=24%2E6803%2EBNyyk4)
**Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa:** Gina had the moral courage to take on a three-term incumbent and the oil money backing him — all while refusing a single cent of corporate PAC money. She is the first Democrat elected governor of Texas in more than 30 years, and the first ever Latina Governor of the Lone Star State. In office, she’ll stop AI data centers from draining local water supplies and has already pledged to end Greg Abbott’s school voucher schemes.
**I am honored to have played a tiny part in these historic wins. It’s why I started JanePAC to begin with. But winning the election is only step one.**
We need leaders who hit the ground running on day one. That’s exactly what Peggy, Deb, and Gina are already doing.
We’re not here to just elect Democrats — we’re here to elect climate champions with the courage to take on the hardest fights.
**[This work takes immense grassroots resources. We don’t take a single dime from oily billionaires to fund this movement. We rely entirely on people like you.](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261112-ak.abAXI3&amount=5&refcode=em20261112-24&t=6&akid=24%2E6803%2EBNyyk4)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261112-ak.abAXI3&amount=5&refcode=20261112-24&t=25&akid=24%2E6803%2EBNyyk4)**
Thank you for being in this fight with me.
xx Jane

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: Today’s tragedy in Washington, D.C.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
At around 8:30 this morning, a shooter entered Vida Fitness near Logan Circle in our nation’s capital.
#

Friend -
At around 8:30 this morning, a shooter entered Vida Fitness near Logan Circle in our nation’s capital. Five people were shot, one was killed, and the suspect barricaded themselves in an apartment complex above the gym before they took their own life.
Vida is an LGBTQ+-owned chain of gyms, and a place the community comes to as a safe and inclusive space. This location is in a densely populated area that includes a church, homes, apartment buildings, grocery stores, restaurants, and bars.
Instead of an early morning workout, families in that neighborhood were locked down with a shelter-in-place order. Helicopters flew over the area, armed law enforcement officers took positions on the rooftops, while the smell of gunpowder lingered in the air.
A place of joy and community was shattered today, and that is the horrifying reality of gun violence in the United States of America. This is not freedom.
My heart goes out to those injured and killed today, their families, and the entire neighborhood that will feel the impact and trauma of this shooting for years to come.
I am devastated and angered by this tragedy. But I also feel determined because I know it doesn't have to be this way. Just days ago we elected a gun safety majority in Congress that will go to Washington and build on our progress. But we must work together to make this happen. Our leaders can choose to act and pass commonsense gun safety legislation that can prevent shootings like these from happening.
Every American deserves the freedom to live safe from gun violence. I will not rest until that vision for our country becomes a reality. Please, keep standing with me in this fight.
Sincerely,
Gabby Giffords

Dear Patriot,
Nearly twenty years in this work has taught me one rule about Washington: **When a door opens, someone is already pushing it shut.** Senator Rand Paul opened one for us. Send subpoena requests to his office . . . the one office in the Senate with sole power to issue them. **No reporter has ever held a key like this.** Since then, you and I have a responsibility to build something fast: A small team of researchers and professionals must be funded and put to work right now. Threads picked: the ballot cash. The border money. The Pfizer papers. And one twenty-year theory, at last ready for its test. Now for the truth about doors . . . Gavels change hands. Sessions end. And the first time a return comes back with a big name on it, they will push hard to shut this down. Harder than we have ever felt. **Senator Paul 's offer has no closing date printed on it. Washington will print one for us if we move slow.** So we will not move slow. If you have been waiting, **this is the moment.** [**Every gift, big or small, goes through that open door with us.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTgsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBO1GS_bVwl5fIWUwCLfw3Ner6Get2lMEJng0X2TD8fZPQArtsiERneX7ypH8MWeSHVd6MkmUbQ1aKfWZZIb9tCfagGmTnesjdEH) [**Give before the door closes.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTgsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBO1GS_cPiipcScXZ8DlEaHV5yzfxdjACt8Cc-IYzREuQq1-AZmDTM68soeLFyE-jr5obWS4RiZoZfdgRTj9-txeTDFFNhSlJ_vx) **[GIVE BEFORE THE DOOR CLOSES](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTgsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABBO1GS_dzBB97BDWBu_qYNHUKi6RhmtuHLIyqMs1Vaccte4UQNjaS9ykEjxJ2YWfXwJWDk_SNKXJsc85tI7Np4WDAiVUKvWFfZ4a)** Thank you for all that you do. I mean that more than you know.
In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group

## SS United States Heads to Seafloor
Crews [began sinking](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0DFu4zAQheHTUN0Y5Iik5ELFNuqy7ZbCSBzak9CiQTIScvuFFwH2AKkf8PDj-_O2vJEk2W-_6cFTzHHZ-ayJW-OyJCo3ro1KkyibUCrMsT6ZF9TowRgwuNDW5ODFUhemwY6k144nM1ytHfX16rr75LwzG4d1MMYFP6yBMIwWbR-vkUeDnUyvP2MMGu1831-88457bWjzjNahspqDtFwu71n2mL7ywSWmXCTQZcuPLk331p5V9b8UzgpnT-v2GhTOz1ybwvmeTzipbXeoFT53aRygNmpcocr-IfsNDq6VEzT64ApRdkrwnj_Lzl-w8pYfDGcuKVT4doH_MPCSge8ihTNqjaNDq3DuyhSep6Qk1Q_K6tuDJP2Lbj_0Pib8GwAA___pc5cB) the _SS United States_ on Wednesday about 25 miles southwest of Destin, slowly flooding the 990-foot ocean liner to create the world's largest artificial reef. Okaloosa County [moved the $13.5 million](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL2SpCAUhZ9GMyxARDsg2MSsN93QusKl--6idHFZnX77KafmDSY7wanz8_25L3egRPvjN2zoYo7LjicnrBXLkqA8kCuUSpE8QSqIkV-Ii5baCqWE0gv4SgcuBtrgRjOBXFt0arwZM8nbbWifDtdgh1VOazCAWsXeRL_iZMyoex2MacldeUopreRg-76zgx2wlwq8RW0G3RiJgWou3d9Me0zvfGCJKRcK0Pm8tck9a31x0_9q9Nzo-TzPLuYP1V9vLkej50s2en4S11zIC2bxf6eKQXCFiiyY9n_ixLAjB3iLHKP47hA-A1exos8big2Y6UBx0WiLC6-TUiK2Y2PkYwNKX5PqD2keTn8GAAD__5SzjNs) project up a day over weather concerns, canceling a public sendoff but placing the sinking on Veterans Day. Federal rules barred explosives, so workers cut deck holes and removed more than 400 portholes. The ship should settle in 180 feet of water, with its top deck about 60 feet below the surface, near the sunken aircraft carrier _USS Oriska_ _ny_. On its 1952 maiden voyage, the liner [set a trans-Atlantic record](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkDFuxCAQRU-DOywYY3spKNK427QpLQyDd1bYrICsldtHjjbKAdJMM9L7__2P63y1FGlf3-2GJqQw73iUiLVinqPNK5Zqc6VAjmzMiKE8EGcQMHApuYTZukpPnJVtvBnVxYqlQSNHrdRFaN03NyO0AKEcLqDlCFZ7HZxbRuExBK_H0JA5eVJKkKIfuq4d-qHHTkjrBgTVA1MCPdWU23uiPcSv9MQcYsrkbevS1kRzq_VRWPfGYGIwHcfRHvfbej4ZTCeewSTl7ymFf-5U0fNSbcXCF3RpQ36kHH3hL3H-Z85PdZ5C4K9Y7pItlcHUZOMfB8VIZRiZEutmKf6Uqv_c82ngOwAA___Yboqm) for ocean liners that still stands. Marilyn Monroe, Walt Disney, four presidents, and the _Mona Lisa_ all sailed aboard. The ship's 65-foot smokestacks will anchor a planned Destin museum.
## Salazar Survives Recount by 1,086 Votes
Republican U.S. Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar narrowly won a fourth term [by 1,086 votes](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0D1u6zAQBODTUJ0E_osqWLxGnV-bUliTS3sDSjRI2kJuHzjIDdJ_MwPMx2W7AGU6bv9hR59K2g48W8besW4Z6g1bh9opUSDIFTG1B-ImubSjEKOQG4ROL9w0DNHP2gG_DujFvGjt-LKY4e5hQSEXZ6M1LnGxgOJxBlBJGQXRmYH8u08IIQU3VqnJGmtQcQHBotRGMs0xUi91-ix0pPxVXlhTLpUiTKHsQ_b33h-NqX9Mrkyu53lOxzXsBDu9AZMrZgydytGYXH-jY6TWK4U-ynmsEHCsGMrz6GPF9sz9TZVzluuZyXWoPj5OypmanZnmtx0o_6z3Px738vI7AAD__7ORghQ) after a machine recount in Florida's 27th Congressional District. Workers recounted nearly 250,000 ballots, finishing on Tuesday with Salazar at 124,519 to Democrat Eliott Rodriguez's 123,433. Salazar thanked voters across party lines. Rodriguez had [sought to remove](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMiO7MQYCB5uQzaYbosY0TK-MPbI9g_b2K77-DX5apSpVvT-P5YEcOB6_8SS3p32JdJVAtVJeAuaDSsVceWfPGDLRXl5ECyiwUmupYUFf-UOLwWZzgxlRrQ05PUzGjGqa-ubpsB9xXP1AAJuxajMTrNrCMIzUwbraht3dp7UGrXrbda3tbU-d0ugtgelBGEUb15Tbv4njHv6lD-U9pMwbtj6dTXDPWl9FdL8EzALm67pav5b7y-0LmE_GkwXMtyRg_g5LGOpT-hSPTKVwihjkxqVm9lVm9CQvjpGyzFTeoRaZyad3rALmJrvtdXEIXOwgjDpO5PA1pv6Q48fB_wAAAP__YhaJlA) Supervisor of Elections Alina Garcia, a Republican, from the canvassing board over her election-night remark that Salazar had won no matter what a recount showed. A federal judge sharply criticized the remark but allowed Garcia to remain on the board. The canvassing board [reconvenes Friday](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL2u2zAMRp9G3hRYtC07g4Yu3m7XjgYjUQkLWjIkNcbt0xfuzxN0IQiQIM_5vn1sH8jC6fkVd3Ixxy3RWYVao7IJlifVhqVxZM8ohSjWg2iDHqw2RhvY0Dd-0zZiF9w8Ltg_OnJmvo_j0t_vU_dyQ4z-McUJ8D5gWKbHQpZohsWOPQXwHbvrnjEGTD_ZYbjZyU409Aa9JRgnUNcit1xu3zOnKJ_5TSVKLhzw5vPeiXu1dlQ1fFGwKljP87xJ9iimv-YK1ktLwXpk4cb-aq-fClZj_pWdcWcdMJBuWef4x1k-NaaUfyRPuqLgTywaqz45JSo6R_2Xo2qY20v7nJ6FauWcUHTg2gr7pmDtigvHySJc7azG_rkjy2_49p-5vx38CgAA__-C05jK) to declare Salazar the winner, with state certification Nov. 17.
## Goodwill Trade Program Graduates 277
In its first year, Goodwill of North Florida’s tuition-free GoodTrades program in Jacksonville [graduated 277 students](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkDGu5CAMhk9DOiIgJDMpKLZJN9tuGTlgEkYkRIaZ7N5-xei9E7zGki3r_z77z2N-QIjhWH_DjsYnPx945YilIM0RaMVcgErwwQaIhOjziTgroQYuJZdqBlvCG2cNjTM3fQexNGjkbdT6LsaxbzaD9r64rhMj6MHrxS0SR6E0LBpG7LRtgql5UkolRT90XTv0Q4-dkGAHVLpXTAt0oSRqnykcPv5LbyQfEwUHrU17E81WyplZ94upianpuq62HqKf8LcuMDXVlqkpJguRqakSmZqk_C6FwCF_nXxNyV0hxsw9IfLPPPOT0kqw8w3jmfmRqGz8y4Dn8nJ4lMyXV4iOH3hxC4RIFdiQcWfNC3m4MS3WHUL8SJcf_vtt1P8AAAD__wcbllA) who learned by installing sinks and tubs in a replica home. HVAC, electrical, and heavy-equipment courses are planned. Plumbing graduate Bruce Lee, who ran an agriculture business before enrolling, said cost was a major hurdle at other trade schools. He’s already fixed a clogged sink and a leak at home, and plans to take [Goodwill’s carpentry course](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0L1uKjEQxfGn2e1YecYf4MLFbei4bUprWI-Xicwa2RYobx8R5Q3SHh39iv_HJV5Iiuzbf7pzyDXHnV-98BjcYqG2cR_UhmRZhUpjzv3BHFGhOwAcACOtQ54cDc0pHM2J1HXmAEdvzEl5b-dbgMRX77QHQpvIEFrSyV85WwJnk50lvD0AQFDWab046yxrBbQ6RmNxMoqTjNqWzyp7Ll_1yS2X2iTRstb7XMJtjEef9L8JzxOet1rTS0rZaxu3XJbatt91NErcJzzPLaTH-yPdHSejtjtJ-cHGHzs8A34HAAD__0hfcqU) before seeking an apprenticeship. Open to Florida residents legally able to work, the program has a wait list. Jacksonville provided $785,000 in startup money, joined by the Jaguars Foundation and Lowe’s. A trade group estimates the construction industry must [hire about 723,000 workers](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGupDAMRb8mdBkRE2AoUmxD97bdEoXEAa9CghLPoP37FU_zB6-9ts-x7p-v5ctSpLT9tgeakMOS8KoRmbEs0ZYNK9vCFMiRjQUx1BNxgRYGqZRUsFjH9MZF28abUT9tuzZo1Dhp_WynqW928-xtt679FDocB9AO1m51oK3H8c5dQ-bmKaVAtf3QdY-hH3rsWmXdgKB7ELpFT5zL42-mFOK__MYSYi7k7cPlo4lmZz6r6H4JmAXM13U91hdFjyWnSAnvLQHzd0ZpEzBzsR6rrK_V5cTFOs6lCpi3nP1FMcocZMqFd_kRyXxiqvKef24dJsYiL-Jd7vlA-VFWSaky8YtRwNwU48-bSHUYhW63w1L8_pp_WPjbwP8AAAD__8jlmvI) a year.

## Spanberger, Democrats Pitch 2027 Agenda
Gov. Abigail Spanberger and Virginia Democrats [unveiled their 2027 legislative agenda](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0UHLnjAMB_BPU295sGm1evCwi7d31x0l2tQn0MdK2yn79sPB2AfYIRDCn5Af-fG1fJFEOfbv9OGpXmE5-C6Ra-W8lJOOlfPOudDOhyfKT7SmBVvsQWvQuNBW5eLFUuOnQJZpbHjSbrR20GNvmvc0rCtp9P22bs560xlnuENiZ3vvDQ6NTM8-rTU-ZfVr7XutcejRhQFDq5Vt2UtN-VXffEne5RAK8Ve6OL-29Gni9K71LMp8UzgrnO_7fmnzUI50PwmFM-UqW2SF8zNXOJ8pSpXtaf9J4edxscQCkXcpkR4cnFlSlipcIKQMfy8Az5-0ZaoF6M3kIQXAFh0ULkXSoXDGUYMPnXbGIjC3AaztPIydIwjB4DiuJrRr2-TJn7fEKKV3yrb7hyT-odX__Mo14e8AAAD__wnvokQ) Tuesday, built around medical debt relief, classroom screen-time limits, and tighter oversight of data centers. The "Moving Virginia Forward" plan, announced at the Capitol in Richmond, leans on affordability. The [data-center proposals](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkbEOnTAMRb8GtiBiIAkDQxe217UjMokDlgI8JRaof1_RoT_QwfIdjq50dH99lg9y4nP7iQdNcsflpKckEqG8lC-eK-WNcsGNzoCYX1SuBVowSmulYUEvfNPSYx2miD3hWNOk7dj3To-mq_cJLdAQjR2CG1pnIhrqQWu0rgMwgDVPb5_WGt7rdbMaozU4AzY6iK2u-pYCy5Ub2enmvPHJGNPv66bc-Ouo07SLfEvV_ahgrmB-nqfxa9Hja_MSFcxvrGAugkLv_yenblSBjstnlKK-LH5XBwX2mFSgVVSmxBRVQEHl6RTKKvHBUlS8soIWbAUzZmGfaHEdgVmdVb0LoIYWjcJx6FSnx9VZb0fysdnlSHWewvfhlLgYW_XtdiCnvzbyn0PcE_wJAAD__xX4nFw) would end by-right approval for facilities drawing more than 25 megawatts, ban nondisclosure agreements between developers and local officials, and regulate cooling-water use. A separate measure targets AI-generated child sexual abuse material. House Minority Leader Terry Kilgore, R-Scott, [dismissed the pitch](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtDAMhJ8mdEGxNwQoUvwN3f7tlciAw0YKASURaN_-xOlO9wBXuLDsGc03H8_xST74uP6njW053Rj5yoFL4TTmg-LEaeWUaeW4EKX7tewjKjQSQAKONBd_8qipWqwjzdRXbKHtte6gN4_qZakHp0DNWj-6RndL32A7NT26CU3TNU3l7e0HAHiPhnoyBgA7g63r0CkQWvHiy57q8uLTp9VHTy6895NTPe9bFeyrlCOLxz-Bg8Dhuq76Sn6-jwKHm0ng8KOU3_svn1w5cqIgKWfepvCWR-Kc5bxHx4njzDLupwQlcKiSXY7Lh-CzaYVW60Y-fKUofyzwtPgZAAD__ythhis). _" There was nothing that will bring down power bills, nothing that will end the car tax, nothing that will end the grocery tax, nothing that will help young people get started in life,"_ he said, promising Republican tax-cut bills instead. Democrats hold a 64-36 House majority. The full General Assembly convenes Jan. 13.
## Virginia Beach Weighs 27 Safety Steps
A Virginia Beach task force handed the City Council [27 recommendations](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkTHP3CAMhn8N2Thhh48kQ4Yu2a5rx8gQk0MlcCIo0f37ikqdOn6Dl1evHuuxfz3XJ4UY0v6TDp7r5dfE9xm5Vi7r-aZkuexcTto5bUSlVWteUaGRABJwJVfDxaumbps9aaap4xmGSesRJtN3r1lp6xwiD96jtZs1E4zW9iPQ5vWoVBfmxgMAbKPhYY0BwNHg4Ef0CoRWvIWay6O--AplDymQj598cXm4fHRxftX6PkX_Q-AicLnv-wF9U0n5bg2BC5UaXGSBS8sFLjE7igKX4-NC_Qhc_pGlZXKv_wJ5kuf6kZXO39Ln4lgWdvk42mlqyOmU2TElX3Kq8go5cnJtH04giWCwZiDp-i8lNWMvJ-176byxX6iwN053Zd7ed4gxnGYQWu0HhfjXr37zNdeMfwIAAP__Va2kHw) Tuesday to curb violence and reshape the Oceanfront after three violent incidents this past spring. The headline idea is a violence interruption program that would deploy trained civilians, not police, to defuse confrontations among the young crowds that pack the resort strip each spring. Other proposals: brighter street lighting, cleaned-up storefronts, more entertainment, expanded mental health crisis teams, and a possible pedestrian-friendly stretch of Atlantic Avenue on weekend nights. Councilman Michael Berlucchi [_pressed the need to move fast_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAMhp8mbDkiJhc4Q4YubLdrR-STGLAakqPEBfH2FVfq1PEOXmzr0_9_vz7nT-TIaf2JOzk5ljnRWSOJUJnrG9OLykql4kopIJb7VfIMLfTaGG1gRi980GyxCW5BS_hsyJnhae1onn3XbM7S0H2MHfi2H59jCAY_Omtasn5AMGAbdjfPGAP3WPN49b0xMPYwLCMsrVG2pcCSy0M2OrisnBiXeOWDysPnvYluE3lX1f1QMCmYzvN8nPL766hgujspmDhp2Uj7vO9_EsulYPoH0y9Cv_230JEwUKna51Q5UNEw6EI34fYhnFPVkjXv75IP0p7l0piCzp4wLSUn0RUXkqspLrxPjpFrPyjbrjty_Mou39R-OPgbAAD__0sJmyo). _" We cannot afford not to try the violence interruption program,"_ he said. City Manager Patrick Duhaney said the program could be piloted at the Oceanfront next spring, and city staff expects to update the council in December or January.

subject: URGENT: Your Senator voted YES. Wildlife could pay the price.
body:
They want to ram through this anti-wildlife legislation. Tell your Senator to vote NO!
They want to ram through this anti-wildlife legislation. Tell your Senator to vote NO!

#
|
---
[SIGN NOW: Keep Threatened and Endangered Animals Protected!](https://support.defenders.org/s/6289810/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
Defender,
#
[**Your chance to speak up in defense of America’s imperiled wildlife is almost gone!**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6289811/38SyG9Xl)
#
**Did you know your PA Senator voted to advance a bill that could bulldoze the Endangered Species Act (ESA)?**
#
Unless we act NOW, wolves, grizzly bears, sea turtles and countless other imperiled species could pay the price.
#
Earlier this week, the Senate voted to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA). Despite its name, this legislation is one of the worst attacks on wildlife we’ve ever seen.
#
**If passed, it will make profound and dangerous changes to the ESA, our country’s strongest tool for protecting wildlife and preventing extinction.**
#
**The good news –Your Senator still has a chance to change course and vote NO on final passage of BAAJA.**
#
[**With more votes on this bill that could take place at any time, we have no time to waste! Send an urgent message and demand your Senator protect endangered wildlife by voting NO.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6289812/38SyG9Xl)
#
|
---
[TELL YOUR SENATOR: VOTE NO!](https://support.defenders.org/s/6289813/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
**What's so bad about BAAJA? A lot.**
#
* It will **cut federal wildlife scientists out of decisions** about projects that threaten endangered animals, removing a critical safeguard against extinction.
* It will **leave endangered animals extremely vulnerable** by shifting conservation responsibilities to underfunded and understaffed state agencies.
* It will **weaken protections across the country** by gutting the national system for protecting endangered species, replacing it with a patchwork of **_up to 50 different state processes,_** leaving wildlife with dangerously inconsistent protections.
* It will completely **exempt some highway and water projects from endangered species requirements** and never even ask the question whether the project might jeopardize the existence of the threatened or endangered species. This effectively creates a **God Squad without the squad!**

#
**And now, during a lame-duck session of Congress, lawmakers are trying to ram through these sweeping and deadly changes before newly elected members have a chance to weigh in.**
#
|
---
[TELL YOUR SENATOR: VOTE NO!](https://support.defenders.org/s/6289814/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
There is clear evidence that the ESA is not the obstacle to development that opponents claim it is. BAAJA would weaken fundamental wildlife protections without addressing the problems that actually slow development.
#
The ESA has helped save more than 99% of listed species from extinction. We will not let it be gutted by a rushed vote.
#
[**Your Senator still has the chance to do the right thing for wildlife. They need to hear from YOU – tell them to vote NO on BAAJA.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6289815/38SyG9Xl)
#
Thank you for taking this important step on behalf of threatened and endangered animals.
#
Sincerely,
#
|
---

---
| **Chris Westfall** Sr. Government Relations Legislative Counsel
Defenders of Wildlife

subject: Are you upset about 2026?
body:
Non-citizens on the rolls, ballots counted days late, machines that won't work. We can fix this

| | | |

I'll be honest with you. I'm frustrated with how the 2026 midterms turned out, and if you're reading this, I'd guess you are too.Look at what we watched happen this cycle. On Election Day, ballot scanners failed across Westchester County, **New York** , in one of the closest House races in the country, held by a Republican incumbent, and poll workers stuffed completed ballots into emergency bags saying they would just be counted later. In **California** , federal officials flagged roughly 20,000 likely non-citizens who had been mailed ballots, and an appeals court let the state count them anyway.**New Jersey** admitted it found 6,600 non-citizens on its own voter rolls. And in one **California** county, election staff opened a locked drop box and found nearly 600 sealed ballots that had sat there uncounted for five months after the election was certified.On top of all that, the Supreme Court ruled this summer that 14 states and D.C. can keep counting mail ballots that arrive after Election Day. **_Election Day is supposed to mean one day._** After a night like this, it's tempting to tune out and wait for things to cool down. I _understand that feeling._ But these problems don't fix themselves between elections. If we look away now, every one of them will be bigger in 2028, and liberals will do everything they can to steal the presidential election. _**[If you're upset about how 2026 turned out and you want to make sure 2028 is decided by honest votes, I need your help right now.](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkTmP2zAQhX8N1cnQkJRkFyoCGOo2RRAgJTEajm1iKVLh4cX--4DO0aeZ4r0Pb64fb-YNnXfh_hV3XlK5mZQNJv6MtR6ZC26xFjnIybTSA_QgDVJxTzYaO7tYsgjU8QLzReuzGkB2j-V2HkETzzTc2EpJ2wiD5nnSKJk1TZ1bWh4ASAA1AJzGcZ4ukmmct4ueNxB6QM-pnBIfdfOOMBTM77eYiE8U984vj1KOLNQXIVch18xUE58-XEhsG9E0fHLPnqm4GHqLn0KuyP0Rc_mnIv0Uaq1lNztbV3ehrryj80JOTcyxJmKhrg9MFvO7afxvi3A_0N2DUNfM1oT4bGZ12bXg18H-kjEUDkWo67fvK4zn86D-OIVT69ilxR4fznuXp1no4d4meK1Z_v8pz0X-CgAA__9XpZzc)**_

subject: We will keep fighting until every ballot is counted
body:
I wanted you to get this update from me: Ballots are still being counted,
and right now, it’s still too close to call.

We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is
counted in this race.

But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources
that we don’t currently have.

As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain
the top target of the DC establishment.

We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your
help to fight back against their attacks.

It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to
sustain our fight until every vote is counted.

From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots
donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s
going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days.

_" Hope is believing in spite of the evidence, and then watching the evidence change."_
_- Jim Wallis_
I fell in love with hiking as a kid at church camp in West Virginia. A farm girl from Ohio, I was used to a landscape that didn't change based on how far you walked. How different that was from scaling a mountain. After hours of pushing your body away from the earth, one step of increasing difficulty at a time, you reach a bald patch of rock . . . and you've earned some spectacular perspective.
After pouring everything into this movement, I didn't know how I would feel last week if we lost. I was prepared to have my heart broken.
I was not prepared for this loss to feel like such a win. As I shared in my speech last week, we thought this was a mountain, but it turns out that it's a mountain range.
_**And now, we know how to climb.**_
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/131a5a25-892c-42d4-b196-17dd14752212?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Photo credit: Emery Ball. Election Night 2026.
On election night after we lost, one young man who has been volunteering with the campaign for the past year came up to me. "For a long time, I've been consumed by anger. But this campaign has created space for something else to rattle around inside of me - and that's been hope."
Another dedicated volunteer approached in tears. "I didn't know how much I needed a vehicle for all of my feelings. Working on this campaign gave me a place to pour my hope into."
While so many of you joined me in the audacity of hope over the past year, I've also spoken with many people flirting with nihilism. People who believe that their votes don't matter, that their actions don't matter, and that we - either our world, our country, or our region - are a lost cause. Rather than turning toward the hard climb, they've opted out of walking forward altogether.
**You and I know that just like there is no such thing as false hope, there 's no such thing as a lost cause.**
Part of our work going forward will be reminding everyone the power they hold, and how to wield it. We'll be doing a full campaign debrief virtually on Sunday, November 22nd ([sign up here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6e8d505a-58bb-49af-8f11-5f2ab2086b68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)), but I want to share just some of the progress that we achieved.
You might have seen this meme circulating, or people online talking about how Tennessee was the one state that "didn't understand the assignment."
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/db2c6a14-a990-4f20-b617-7c96ca192dde?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As much as I am dreading four years of a Blackburn governorship and a continued Republican supermajority in the state assembly and am disappointed we didn't flip more Congressional seats . . . as someone who poured _everything_ into our state this cycle, I actually see this as momentum, not as failure at all.
Georgia turning blue didn't happen overnight. Stacey Abrams and thousands of other organizers have been putting in the work for _years_ , fighting against disenfranchisement in their state. This is a good time to remind everyone that the first time Jon Ossoff ran for office, he ran for the House of Representatives in a special election in 2017 in a heavily Republican district that no one thought was competitive.
He organized, fundraised, and mobilized incredible turnout . . . but according to one local population, "surging Democratic turnout wasn't enough to overcome heavy GOP voting in a district where Republicans far outnumber Democrats." Sound familiar? He lost. But a Democrat won it the next year, and three years later Ossoff flipped the decisive seat in the US Senate, and won re-election handily this year.
Let's not forget Texas. How many times did Democrats, especially those blue dots in red states, hold our collective breath while hoping that Beto would pull it off? He lost the Senate in 2018, withdrew from the presidential race in 2020, and lost the governor's race in 2022. Now, Ted Cruz is the only Republican who holds statewide office in Texas.
Annie Andrews. Did you know she ran for Congress in 2022 against Nancy Mace, and lost after receiving just 42.5% of the vote? Four years later, she became the first woman elected to the Senate in South Carolina.
We out-worked and out-hoped our opponents at every step. And like so many of you told me on election night before the results even started to roll in, **this is a beginning**.
Let's look at how East Tennessee, despite online narratives, understood the assignment.
We received 41.6% of the vote. Crossing the 40% threshold has only happened one other time for Democrats since 1965. Over 103,000 people voted for this movement. That's the most a Democrat has gotten during a midterm _ever_.
**We shifted our entire district by double digits,**_**and actually outperformed the blue tsunami in the rest of the country.**_
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ca72b07e-8ee8-453d-a0ff-58e7fefa3e3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Image source: NY Times._
Trump and Vance won Knox county handily in 2024. In 2026, Burchett won Knox county - the county he served as mayor for 8 years - _by less than 1%_. At the precinct level in Knox county (the only one with clear precinct data so far), we made huge gains, shifting the margin in _**every single precinct**_ in Knox on average over 20 points compared to 2022 and 2024.
And we built on the momentum of the local races, shifting the margin in Knox county by 4.7 points over the August Mayoral race.
We've climbed one mountain. I don't know about you, but I'm ready to lace up my boots and see what else this range has in store for us.
[Join us on Sunday, November 22nd at 4 pm ](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6e8d505a-58bb-49af-8f11-5f2ab2086b68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)where we'll fully break down the election results and share what comes next - _**and how you can be part of it**_.
-Michaela

You might have seen this meme circulating, or people online talking about how Tennessee was the one state that "didn't understand the assignment." | | ---|---|--- As much as I am dreading four years of a Blackburn governorship and a continued Republican supermajority in the state assembly and am disappointed we didn't flip more Congressional seats . . . as someone who poured everything into our state this cycle, I actually see this as momentum, not as failure at all. Georgia turning blue didn't happen overnight. Stacey Abrams and thousands of other organizers have been putting in the work for years , fighting against disenfranchisement in their state. This is a good time to remind everyone that the first time Jon Ossoff ran for office, he ran for the House of Representatives in a special election in 2017 in a heavily Republican district that no one thought was competitive. He organized, fundraised, and mobilized incredible turnout . . . but according to one local population, "surging Democratic turnout wasn't enough to overcome heavy GOP voting in a district where Republicans far outnumber Democrats." Sound familiar? He lost. But a Democrat won it the next year, and three years later Ossoff flipped the decisive seat in the US Senate, and won re-election handily this year. Let's not forget Texas. How many times did Democrats, especially those blue dots in red states, hold our collective breath while hoping that Beto would pull it off? He lost the Senate in 2018, withdrew from the presidential race in 2020, and lost the governor's race in 2022. Now, Ted Cruz is the only Republican who holds statewide office in Texas. Annie Andrews. Did you know she ran for Congress in 2022 against Nancy Mace, and lost after receiving just 42.5% of the vote? Four years later, she became the first woman elected to the Senate in South Carolina. We out-worked and out-hoped our opponents at every step. And like so many of you told me on election night before the results even started to roll in, this is a beginning. Let's look at how East Tennessee, despite online narratives, understood the assignment. We received 41.6% of the vote. Crossing the 40% threshold has only happened one other time for Democrats since 1965. Over 103,000 people voted for this movement. That's the most a Democrat has gotten during a midterm ever. We shifted our entire district by double digits,and actually outperformed the blue tsunami in the rest of the country. | | ---|---|--- Image source: NY Times. Trump and Vance won Knox county handily in 2024. In 2026, Burchett won Knox county - the county he served as mayor for 8 years - by less than 1%. At the precinct level in Knox county (the only one with clear precinct data so far), we made huge gains, shifting the margin in every single precinct in Knox on average over 20 points compared to 2022 and 2024. And we built on the momentum of the local races, shifting the margin in Knox county by 4.7 points over the August Mayoral race. We've climbed one mountain. I don't know about you, but I'm ready to lace up my boots and see what else this range has in store for us. we'll fully break down the election results and share what comes next - and how you can be part of it. -Michaela Paid for by Michaela for Tennessee Michaela for Tennessee P.O. body:
It is heartbreaking

It is heartbreaking
| Do you trust your neighbors, Peter?This would've been an easy question for me back when I knew my neighbors and could count on them. I would always see most of my neighbors at church, and there was a collective will among us to do something for our people and community.We used to belong to a community where everyone looked out for each other, and that's what made America great in the first place.It is heartbreaking to tell you that this is all going away.As our communities have been invaded by people from the Third World, we've lost our sense of who we are. They came here and took advantage of us.[How can you trust your neighbors when all they do is take from you while sharing none of your values, heritage, or faith?](https://trk.email.exclusive-update.)This is outrageous, and the fact that the Federal Government knowingly let this happen to your community and our society is beyond shameful.

I will never take your support for granted.

It takes a thoughtful look at the ideas, events, and debates surrounding the Declaration of Independence and the American Revolution. **You can receive instant access to this free video series about 1776 today using this secure link:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/1776-cca-video-series](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcGK2zAQhp9GvtlII9myDz4sddLuIVvaLCw9GVWaOAOyJCw57eMXw-YFev1m-H74_4_LfDHkKSxvZsWRcp5ddDP-TT5uWO54i3twFJa0UbCUZuDQ1ULUAmZjCz1wVqZyYwuiv_UVjkIPSvV9O_TVfZTQt9KClg57q4TgZtBcoTCopeskVjQePiEECMmlaBt0Vg8t_w0SrdJtxxTfkzMFGwqZHGYbY0rRUyGbm7gtlR_vpaTM5AuDM4MzhVts7uR9dsZjg25ncBZad7W1pn6Qw1hn3Agzk-eMy4qhfIkOmZw4FxzeOCh4_TpM36fT6cqg28s657hv9nhJW8wJbaGwfJ5WdLSvTE64GvKf0Jo1GVoCk9MR_aQxFAyFyenj26_Ly_v76ef8Q9ev12v9rKHaRpf-kPeUO80UXw5pY-Nalf8d5zHCvwAAAP__9a6diQ) In six engaging lectures, scholars walk through the principles and turning points that shaped our nation’s founding—along with the military, economic, and moral dimensions of the Revolution. **These are the topics you’ll explore:**
* The story of the Declaration of Independence
* Lexington and Concord
* The economics of the Revolution
* Keys to American victory

* The ongoing debate over 1619 and 1776

For more than 50 years, Hillsdale has hosted a lecture series aimed at encouraging serious, civil discussion about the most important questions facing our country. | | [Congressman Wiley Nickel](https://substack.com/@wileynickel)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6efbce72-7562-43b4-a1eb-348ed5597646?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I've been smiling a lot this week.
Democrats won back the U.S. Senate, and it looks like we'll have 56 Democrats in the Senate when the new Congress starts in January. A lot of people said it couldn't be done. The map was tough and the money was against us. But folks showed up anyway, in places nobody expected, and they sent a clear message. They're tired of paying more for groceries, rent and health care. They're tired of politicians who work for the people at the top. They want a government that actually gets something done.
Here in North Carolina, sending Roy Cooper to the Senate was about saving our democracy. People across this state voted to protect their freedoms and push back against leaders who'd rather rig the rules than win a fair fight.
Now Senate Democrats have to deliver. And I'll tell you what I think comes first.
**They have to nuke the filibuster.**
I know that sounds like inside-baseball Senate stuff. It's not. It's the reason so many good ideas die in Washington before they ever get a vote. Under the rules today, almost nothing passes the Senate without 60 votes. Not 51. Sixty. So a minority of senators can block what most Americans want, and they don't even have to break a sweat doing it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6efbce72-7562-43b4-a1eb-348ed5597646?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Even with 56 seats, Democrats are four short. And even if they got to 60, I'm not sure they'd get 60 votes. John Fetterman has already said he wants to keep the filibuster, and he keeps breaking with our party on big votes. He won't be the only one. If we wait for a magic number, we'll be waiting forever, and working families can't afford it.
Let's be honest about who that rule protects. It protects the billionaires and the big corporations who've spent years buying influence in Washington. They don't need to win a majority. They just need to keep 41 senators happy. That's a lot cheaper than earning the support of the American people, and they know it.
So here's how I see it.
If you care about protecting voting rights, nuke the filibuster.
If you care about restoring women's reproductive freedom, nuke the filibuster.
If you care about lowering costs for working families, nuke the filibuster.
If you want to get rid of unlimited dark money in our politics, nuke the filibuster.
If you want to end gerrymandering and clean up corruption in Washington, nuke the filibuster.
I'm sick of a system where billionaires can pour unlimited dark money into our elections. I'm sick of members of Congress trading stocks in the same companies they're supposed to be regulating. Ban stock trading by members of Congress. Shine a light on dark money. Make public service about serving the public again. None of that happens as long as a minority of senators can quietly block it with the filibuster.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6efbce72-7562-43b4-a1eb-348ed5597646?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Nowhere in the Constitution does it say you need 60 votes to pass a bill in the Senate. The founders let each chamber write its own rules. The 60-vote threshold is one of those rules, and the Senate can change it any time it wants to.
It's also a rule with a painful history. For decades, Southern senators used the filibuster to block civil rights bills, including bills to make lynching a federal crime. The Senate didn't break a civil rights filibuster until 1964. That's not a tradition worth protecting.
I'm not saying senators shouldn't be able to fight hard for what they believe in. I'm fine with a talking filibuster. If a senator feels that strongly, let them stand up on the floor and talk as long as they can. Make the case in front of the American people. What I'm against is killing a bill by quietly objecting and going home for the weekend.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6efbce72-7562-43b4-a1eb-348ed5597646?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I know a little about rules that get rigged against voters. Gerrymandering cut my time short in Congress. I wrote a bill to create independent redistricting commissions, and I'm still fighting for it. I guarantee you we'll never get four Republican senators to join 56 Democrats to end partisan gerrymandering in the next Congress. The only way it happens is if it takes 51 votes.
So here's what I'm asking for. Put every member of the Senate on record. Every single one. Bring it to the floor and hold a vote. Let each senator tell the country, out loud, whether they're with the people who just voted for change or with the billionaire donors who like things just the way they are. No hiding behind procedure. No "it's complicated." Yes or no.
Then get it done.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6efbce72-7562-43b4-a1eb-348ed5597646?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And this fight doesn't end in January. In 2028, Republican Senator Ted Budd is up for reelection. North Carolina needs to send someone to Washington who will actually get it done. Someone who'll fight for lower costs, honest government and fair maps. Someone who answers to the people of this state, not to billionaires and their super PACs. It'll be one of the most important races in the country.
I'm hopeful. I really am. We just proved that when people show up, things change. Democrats have the majority. We've got the momentum. Let's not waste a minute of it.
Talk soon,
Wiley
P.S. Billionaires write big checks to keep the system the way it is. We win by doing it the other way: lots of regular people, each pitching in what they can. If you care about restoring women's reproductive freedom, nuke the filibuster. If you care about lowering costs for working families, nuke the filibuster. If you want to get rid of unlimited dark money in our politics, nuke the filibuster. If you want to end gerrymandering and clean up corruption in Washington, nuke the filibuster. I'm sick of a system where billionaires can pour unlimited dark money into our elections. I'm sick of members of Congress trading stocks in the same companies they're supposed to be regulating. Ban stock trading by members of Congress. Shine a light on dark money. Make public service about serving the public again. None of that happens as long as a minority of senators can quietly block it with the filibuster. | | ---|---|--- Nowhere in the Constitution does it say you need 60 votes to pass a bill in the Senate. The founders let each chamber write its own rules. The 60-vote threshold is one of those rules, and the Senate can change it any time it wants to. It's also a rule with a painful history. For decades, Southern senators used the filibuster to block civil rights bills, including bills to make lynching a federal crime. The Senate didn't break a civil rights filibuster until 1964. That's not a tradition worth protecting. I'm not saying senators shouldn't be able to fight hard for what they believe in. I'm fine with a talking filibuster. If a senator feels that strongly, let them stand up on the floor and talk as long as they can. Make the case in front of the American people. What I'm against is killing a bill by quietly objecting and going home for the weekend. | | ---|---|--- I know a little about rules that get rigged against voters. Gerrymandering cut my time short in Congress. I wrote a bill to create independent redistricting commissions, and I'm still fighting for it. I guarantee you we'll never get four Republican senators to join 56 Democrats to end partisan gerrymandering in the next Congress. The only way it happens is if it takes 51 votes. So here's what I'm asking for. Put every member of the Senate on record. Every single one. Bring it to the floor and hold a vote. Let each senator tell the country, out loud, whether they're with the people who just voted for change or with the billionaire donors who like things just the way they are. No hiding behind procedure. No "it's complicated." Yes or no. Then get it done. | | ---|---|--- And this fight doesn't end in January. In 2028, Republican Senator Ted Budd is up for reelection. North Carolina needs to send someone to Washington who will actually get it done. Someone who'll fight for lower costs, honest government and fair maps. Someone who answers to the people of this state, not to billionaires and their super PACs. It'll be one of the most important races in the country. I'm hopeful. I really am. We just proved that when people show up, things change. Democrats have the majority. We've got the momentum. Let's not waste a minute of it. Talk soon, Wiley P.S. Billionaires write big checks to keep the system the way it is. We win by doing it the other way: lots of regular people, each pitching in what they can. If this post meant something to you, can you give $10, $25 or $50 to my campaign right now? It keeps me in this fight for fair rules and honest government. P.P.S. Come see me get sworn in as Wake County's next District Attorney. It'll be Tuesday, January 5th, 2027 at 1 PM at the Wake County Justice Center in Raleigh. It's free and open to everyone, and I'd love to see you there. RSVP here so we know you're coming: | | ---|---|--- ? PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY WILEY FOR WAKE ? Democracy is on the ballot. Join the fight at . | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Wiley for Wake P.O. Box 563, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

| | | [](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckT2O4zAMhU8jdw6sf7twsdjAwBYz7ZYCI9ExEVvyWFLm-gtPcoLtCPLxPfDj3w_3AbRSvH_ChqN_kjuyg69K_rGm9IDyvUDJC-w7RopOdMK0nLdcOPCFnugUNGH0wUjR4MjtoFQ_yF43y8gHQM5Fb6SdZW8sqiHc-m6WvbrNptMNjacd51xwyY0QF62tvyE32koPAiVTXd0DFMwXn2LG4wlnJsWYzirFi09bs45LKXtm8hcTExNTRl8PvEDEkMqpYGIq9YgU7-2eKJa2ZmBisoOeb9piO-AgW4UB2gFRtjD386yRo0FgcsqpHh6dTwGZvP7-88m17RRnwtSyuQ0D1Y3JK25A67v5WmHyusARID8c-K_3yMO2A90jk9ey1wwvjJS3H7RvUcHjtGyOMezftK6UjWWqu58RPyeX__zUcxT_AgAA__8deaSb)

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.

---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.

And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward. One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you. If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now. Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school. This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it. And we don't take that lightly. I appreciate you taking the time to read this, and for everything you've already done to support this work. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. Friend, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture. But moments like this don't sustain themselves. If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple. We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. If you've already supported Turning Point USA in the past, thank you for carrying this movement forward every single day. If you haven't yet, I'm asking you to step in now. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044 Pop Acta Media | Conservative Innovation PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 | _

name: James Delos Reyes
subject: What’s really happening with ICE in our communities
body:
Stand with API PA to protect our neighbors
| |
---
| Hello Peter, 2026 is almost over. As families are gathering to celebrate the holidays, from Diwali to Thanksgiving, it’s hard for me to feel joyful knowing that more families this year are facing this holiday season apart. Too many Pennsylvanians have been detained by ICE or deported this year, leaving empty chairs at dining tables and gaps in our communities at this time of year. Pennsylvania wants a change. We overwhelmingly voted against the Trump agenda — including ICE’s violent abductions of our neighbors, inhumane detention, and rushed deportation. But until we can have real accountability for ICE, our communities are still facing down systems that keep ICE on our streets. We see [in Western PA](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/0s0baiMS9ZvSPFxokw2CcH9paQvjYMhn/click?signature=db70759b6e5cfbd427fd370c77b2606800cf1012&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wesanews.org%2Fpolitics-government%2F2026-11-10%2Fpennsylvania-immigration-enforcement-allegheny-county), ICE detentions vary wildly county-by-county. Despite Beaver County being smaller and less diverse, they face nearly three times the detentions compared to neighboring Allegheny County. The difference? Beaver County has an**active 287(g) agreement** with the local sheriff’s office — and nearly 69% of Beaver County ICE detentions resulted from collaboration with local police. This isn’t just happening in Beaver County — across the state, more and more [local police departments](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/0s0baiMS9ZvSPFxokw2CcH9paQvjYMhn/click?signature=b36da1387f49ff5de3f5428427eccda58042dfd7&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.inquirer.com%2Fnews%2Fice-arrests-pennsylvania-police-287g--20261105.html) are signing up to help ICE with the President’s anti-immigrant agenda. This isn’t right. Our local resources are already stretched thin — it’s unthinkable that we would send our taxpayer dollars and our local police to help ICE separate families and detain our neighbors. Our neighborhoods become more dangerous if we can’t trust our local police to treat us fairly, simply based on what we look like or our suspected immigration status. As we gather this year, we are not just resting, we are strengthening our relationships with each other. These bonds between family, friends, and community are what make us powerful. At API PA, we are building power for Asian communities across Pennsylvania. We showed our power this November when we stood up and elected leaders that will champion our community in the State House and in Congress. Next, we are working to end 287(g) agreements, get ICE off our streets, close down detention centers in Pennsylvania, and abolish ICE once and for all. [Will you join us by becoming a member of API PA? ](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/0s0baiMS9ZvSPFxokw2CcH9paQvjYMhn/click?signature=cdec22d07f80cc7ea4d6f3264b43193ba4e366ee&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.apipennsylvania.org%2Fmembership "Membership") In Solidarity, James Delos Reyes Co-Field Director Asian Pacific Islander Political Alliance

body:
I’m sending this again because it matters. The rebuild starts now, not in an election year.

| | | | Fellow Conservative \- Last week, I sent you the hardest message I've had to write in a long time. I'm forwarding it below because I need to know you saw it. Here's the short version: 2026 wasn't a blue wave. It was a blue tsunami. _We lost the House.__We lost the Senate._ In Texas, Republicans lost every single statewide race, and I am one of the few statewide elected Republicans left in the Lone Star State. Our voters didn't stay home. They showed up and voted against us, because too many Republicans ignored the very real pain families feel every time they buy groceries, fill up the tank, or open an electric bill. Now the radicals are in charge in Austin and in Washington. _And they will overreach._ Higher taxes. An assault on Texas energy jobs. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, and nonstop retaliation against President Trump. **_That's why we have to build a resistance,___starting today_._** Here's my plan.
1. **_We fight the madness_.** When Democrats are reasonable, I'll work with them. When they push policies that hurt American families, I will fight them with everything I have.
2. **_We rebuild_.** We win back the voters we lost: blue-collar workers, Evangelical Christians, farmers and ranchers, young people, and Hispanic voters. We do it by championing policies that make a real difference in their lives.

That rebuild doesn't start next October. It starts right now. Every month we wait is a month the Democrats spend digging in. You've stood with me before, Fellow Conservative. _**[I'm asking you to stand with me again.](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)**_ Texas is still Texas. America is still America. We will bring it back. For America, Ted Cruz
---
[ **REJOIN THE FIGHT ->** ](https://trk.email.tedcruz.-vUiks5vFHvjkw)
---
|

\---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Ted CruzDate: Thursday, November 5, 2026 Subject: History was madeTo: dpwillis67@gmail.com

---
_**FROM THE DESK OF SENATOR TED CRUZ **_
---
| | | Fellow Conservative,
---
History was made this week...

For months, we were saying that 2026 was the most consequential midterm election of our lifetimes.

Unfortunately, we were right. Sometimes history is to be celebrated; other times, it is to be mourned. Always, it must be reckoned with.

2026 was not simply a blue wave; it was a blue tsunami. It was an ass kicking. It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation. What happened, and why? What are the consequences, and where on earth do we go from here?

When all the votes were counted, the problem wasn't turnout. Instead, our voters, Republicans, Libertarians, Independents, showed up and voted, and rejected our candidates, voting Democrat instead. We've lost the House. We've lost the Senate. When all is said and done, we will have lost eight to 10 Senate seats.

We lost in historically red states, like South Carolina and North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. We lost in purple states, like Michigan, and New Hampshire, and Georgia. And we just barely won by just a single point in bright red states like Florida and Louisiana, and then there's Texas.

Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas. In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election. For weeks, I had been publicly warning on this podcast that we were in very real danger of losing everything in Texas. Far too few believed that was possible. I am very, very sorry that it came to pass. Texas has not had a Democrat governor since 1994. We haven't had a Democrat senator since 1993. Now we'll have both.

Why were the results so overwhelming? Pundits and analysts will break down the results for weeks or months or even years to come, but several things are already evident today.

Years ago, the very best political advice I ever got was from Heidi. She said, "It's not about you. It's about them. It's about their kids, their families, their hopes, their dreams, their futures." Too many politicians forget that.

Take the state of Kansas, for example, a state that has not elected a Democrat senator since 1932. It just did. Here's what exit polling showed were the top issues in Kansas.

Number one, cost of living, energy, and groceries. That was listed as number one by 30.6 percent of voters.
Corruption. Number two, 18.5%.
The cost of the Iran war, 10.1%.
The candidates are terrible, 7.9%.
The Canada trade war, 7.6%.
The GOP didn't do enough to support Trump, 6.6%.
Republicans didn't pass the Save America Act, 5.6%.
Trump's focus on monuments, 5.5%, and data centers and AI, 3.8%...

The top issue, cost of living, is very real. Too many in politics dismissed it. They didn't understand. They pointed to the macro numbers showing the stock markets soaring, median income at record highs, and poverty at record lows. Those data are true, but they don't tell all of the story.

Here are some stats that are a lot more real and personal. Spam, Hormel's processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That's double the share just two years ago.

In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm.

And here's one that's really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That's another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries.

That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn't understand or they didn't care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high.

Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars.

There's a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world's very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American's electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years.

Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn't do enough to address their very real pain.

So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people's lives, and we need to deal with the consequences.

Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That's not something I ever thought I would say.

We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk.

And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed.

Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI.

The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They'll just blame it all on Donald Trump.

In the next two years, we need to do two things.

One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they're willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas.

So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution.

And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost.

There's a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn't show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics.

For Hispanics, there's a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around.

And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record.

Too few voters were even aware of what we'd accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism.

People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else.

But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain't us. Texas is still Texas.

We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well.

When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America.

It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you.
---
Thank you,
