Here's what exit polling showed were the top issues in Kansas. Number one, cost of living, energy, and groceries. That was listed as number one by 30.6 percent of voters. Corruption. Number two, 18.5%. The cost of the Iran war, 10.1%. The candidates are terrible, 7.9%. The Canada trade war, 7.6%. The GOP didn't do enough to support Trump, 6.6%. Republicans didn't pass the Save America Act, 5.6%. Trump's focus on monuments, 5.5%, and data centers and AI, 3.8%... The top issue, cost of living, is very real. Too many in politics dismissed it. They didn't understand. They pointed to the macro numbers showing the stock markets soaring, median income at record highs, and poverty at record lows. Those data are true, but they don't tell all of the story. Here are some stats that are a lot more real and personal. Spam, Hormel's processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That's double the share just two years ago. In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm. And here's one that's really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That's another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries. That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn't understand or they didn't care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high. Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars. There's a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world's very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American's electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years. Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn't do enough to address their very real pain. So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people's lives, and we need to deal with the consequences. Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That's not something I ever thought I would say. We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk. And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed. Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI. The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They'll just blame it all on Donald Trump. In the next two years, we need to do two things. One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they're willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas. So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution. And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost. There's a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn't show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics. For Hispanics, there's a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around. And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record. Too few voters were even aware of what we'd accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism. People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else. But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain't us. Texas is still Texas. We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well. When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America. It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you. Thank you, Ted Cruz | | | | | | | | | | Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate | | PO Box 25400 Houston, TX 77265 | | | To stop receiving emails from Ted Cruz for Senate, to unsubscribe.

body:
The path forward is clear.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41644%2E3422442%2E1o4xt5)
Peter,
When I flipped a Republican seat as part of a blue wave in 2018, I was told you couldn’t win in a red district by rejecting corporate money and fighting for working families—but our campaign proved them wrong.
**On Election Day, we saw more candidates than ever run on that exact same message and _win._**
Democratic candidates across the country proved that when you reject the corrupting influence of corporate money and fight unapologetically for everyday people, voters will have your back.
People know it’s Donald Trump’s tariffs and budgets that drove up prices on nearly everything. They also haven’t forgotten that it was politicians bought off by corporate PACs who voted for those policies. When they had the opportunity to vote for candidates who will actually stand up to that corruption, they made their voices heard.
**The result was one of the most successful elections for Democrats in a generation.**
In the House, we took back the majority with at least 254 seats—with several races still too close to call. We flipped districts in California, Iowa, New York, and many places in between.
In the Senate, Democrats now hold a decisive majority with room to grow even more once the race in Alaska is called. **Not only did we finally defeat Susan Collins, but we flipped seats in Mississippi, South Carolina, North Carolina, Texas, Ohio, Kansas, and Iowa** , while holding the line in Georgia and Michigan.
The path forward is clear: run more candidates who will fight for working families. That’s the only way we will keep expanding the map, take back the presidency, and finally deliver the wins that everyday people need.
2028 might feel far away, but that work starts right now. We are already laying out our plans to protect our majorities and keep winning, and we need to know you stand with us.

Thank you,
Katie Porter

First, the ultimate battle isn't about politics or parties. It's about truth, and the freedom to speak it. ADF exists to remove the obstacles between people and the Gospel. We protect the first freedoms that keep the door open so that all might be free. With God's grace, we do that regardless of which party is in power. Second, we play the long game. The terrain changes, but the strategy does not. We anticipated this shift, though we hoped it wouldn't be this big, and that is why--with your partnership--we have pressed so hard in the courts these past few years. We will likely see more hostility toward truth in the days ahead. But we also expect new opportunities to set precedents, especially in states with leaders hostile to human flourishing. Losses at the ballot box in Nevada and Virginia, where voters enshrined a right to abortion in their state constitutions, signal what kinds of policies might soon be attempted elsewhere. We will continue to contend for the sanctity of every woman's life and that of her unborn child. But truth won on Tuesday, too. It can never be erased, only rediscovered or rejected. And in several states, voters rediscovered the truth that men and women are different. Biology isn't red or blue. Building on our major victory at the U.S. Supreme Court this year, voters in Arizona and Nebraska approved measures to protect girls' sports. Arizona's extended those protections to women's private spaces. Nebraska's wrote its women's sports law into the state constitution. You might expect that from Nebraska or even Arizona. Then came Colorado and Washington. In Colorado, two measures are leading: one protecting girls' sports, the other protecting children from dangerous transition surgeries. In my home state of Washington, voters appear to have approved a measure protecting girls' sports. Voters are responding to the stories of girls who paid the price. In Puyallup, Washington, then-15-year-old wrestler Kallie Keeler was sexually assaulted by a male competitor whom state and school policy allowed to compete against her. The state told her it could happen again. Her emergency petition is pending before the U.S. Supreme Court. And in Camas, Washington, a male athlete who switched to the girls' cross-country team midyear took the final qualifying spot from a deserving young woman from Puyallup High School. He will compete in the women's state finals this Saturday. I don't want you to miss this, friend. In 2014, when ADF took on the lie of gender ideology to uphold biological reality, few were with us. Public opinion was at best mixed. This week, the American people crossed political and ideological lines to say otherwise. This tells us the American people aren't ready to abandon truth. Getting here took hard work, alliance-building, and persuasion. Tragically, it also took many young women paying the cost of a lie. If working at ADF has shown me anything, it is that sometimes you have to lose before you can win. But truth always defeats darkness, and lies have a way of producing harms that become impossible to deny. We are not afraid. We walk into the wind, because that is where God has called us. This is not a time for despair. Hebrews 6:18-19 reminds us it is impossible for God to lie, and it calls the hope we have in Him "a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul." That hope is why the Lord has called ADF to keep the door open for the Gospel. You and I contend for His truth so that all might be free to find that hope and spend eternity with Him. The terrain has changed. The calling has not. clean_body: In the wake of the election results, today is a good day to remember why we are here. | Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this | | | | Dear Friend, In the wake of the election results, today is a good day to remember why we are here. First, the ultimate battle isn't about politics or parties. It's about truth, and the freedom to speak it. ADF exists to remove the obstacles between people and the Gospel. We protect the first freedoms that keep the door open so that all might be free. With God's grace, we do that regardless of which party is in power. Second, we play the long game. The terrain changes, but the strategy does not. We anticipated this shift, though we hoped it wouldn't be this big, and that is why--with your partnership--we have pressed so hard in the courts these past few years. We will likely see more hostility toward truth in the days ahead. But we also expect new opportunities to set precedents, especially in states with leaders hostile to human flourishing. Losses at the ballot box in Nevada and Virginia, where voters enshrined a right to abortion in their state constitutions, signal what kinds of policies might soon be attempted elsewhere. We will continue to contend for the sanctity of every woman's life and that of her unborn child. But truth won on Tuesday, too. It can never be erased, only rediscovered or rejected. And in several states, voters rediscovered the truth that men and women are different. Biology isn't red or blue. Building on our major victory at the U.S. Supreme Court this year, voters in Arizona and Nebraska approved measures to protect girls' sports. Arizona's extended those protections to women's private spaces. Nebraska's wrote its women's sports law into the state constitution. You might expect that from Nebraska or even Arizona. Then came Colorado and Washington. In Colorado, two measures are leading: one protecting girls' sports, the other protecting children from dangerous transition surgeries. In my home state of Washington, voters appear to have approved a measure protecting girls' sports. Voters are responding to the stories of girls who paid the price. In Puyallup, Washington, then-15-year-old wrestler Kallie Keeler was sexually assaulted by a male competitor whom state and school policy allowed to compete against her. The state told her it could happen again. Her emergency petition is pending before the U.S. Supreme Court. And in Camas, Washington, a male athlete who switched to the girls' cross-country team midyear took the final qualifying spot from a deserving young woman from Puyallup High School. He will compete in the women's state finals this Saturday. I don't want you to miss this, friend. In 2014, when ADF took on the lie of gender ideology to uphold biological reality, few were with us. Public opinion was at best mixed. This week, the American people crossed political and ideological lines to say otherwise. This tells us the American people aren't ready to abandon truth. Getting here took hard work, alliance-building, and persuasion. Tragically, it also took many young women paying the cost of a lie. If working at ADF has shown me anything, it is that sometimes you have to lose before you can win. But truth always defeats darkness, and lies have a way of producing harms that become impossible to deny. We are not afraid. We walk into the wind, because that is where God has called us. This is not a time for despair. Hebrews 6:18-19 reminds us it is impossible for God to lie, and it calls the hope we have in Him "a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul." That hope is why the Lord has called ADF to keep the door open for the Gospel. You and I contend for His truth so that all might be free to find that hope and spend eternity with Him. The terrain has changed. The calling has not. Let's go. | | In Christ, Kristen Waggoner CEO, President & Chief Counsel Alliance Defending Freedom P.S. Your gift today helps us tackle the new legal threats that will emerge in many states in the wake of the midterm elections. | | Alliance Defending Freedom 15100 N. 90th Street Scottsdale Arizona 85260

**Thursday, November 12, 2026**
Seven adults gathered around our dinner table. Four settled in while three brought the last of the serving plates.
The arroz con gandules made its way around the table as the conversation continued from the living room. The 2026 midterms were over, and the GOP had lost significant ground with Latino voters.
"A word or two in Spanish, a guayabera, and then a chorus of VOTE RED. Ay, yi, yi!"
"I hoped we'd see candidates who practiced what they preached. Too many officials acted like they were doing us a favor. This is the pre-Trump elitism coming back."

"They have Facebook handlers to 'educate' Hispanics. Not one Hispanic administrator in these particular Republican groups, yet the names are Hispanic-this, Latino-that."
"Educate us? We are a conservative, family-oriented, religious culture. They are not teaching us conservatism. We already live it. What are they to teach us?"
"Chess pieces. We are pawns on their chessboard."
"Representation is not a courtesy. It is the law. And loyalty is not organized. It is earned -- at tables like ours."
"At all tables."
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

She leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan by fewer than 4,000 votes, with about 40,000 of the state’s ballots yet to be counted. Mary and her team need the resources to ensure every vote is counted and every voice is heard. But she can't do it alone. = = Thank you for your support, your activism, and all that you do. **** Friend, **We’ve flipped Minnesota’s First Congressional District from red to blue.** I’m still taking it in. This victory belongs to you, Friend. It belongs to the neighbors who knocked doors, chipped in what they could, hosted a living room conversation, put up a yard sign, or told a friend why this race mattered. Two years ago, some would’ve said we stood no chance – _but you gave us this chance, Friend._ I’ll have more to say in the coming days. But unfortunately it’s not quite over yet: With the margin where it is, we might be going to a recount. Here’s why. The recount itself will likely be funded by taxpayers, because Finstad has the ability to request that under state law. **However, that doesn’t cover all the staff and observers we need on our end to ensure that we can advocate for ourselves during the recount process across all 21 counties.** **[We need to raise $20,000 in the next 24 hours to prepare for a potential recount. Doing so could change who wins — allowing politicians to seize power against the will of the people. Election Night results are not final results. Mail-in ballots, provisional ballots, and votes from military and overseas Americans can take additional time to count. Every eligible vote matters, regardless of when it's counted. Politicians don't get to declare themselves the winners by throwing out votes they don't like. That's election sabotage, and it threatens to take the power to choose our leaders away from the people. Congress must monitor federal election counting, investigate interference, and demand enforcement of voting rights protections. And our representatives must prepare to act wherever credible threats to lawful vote counting emerge. After six years of Trump's attacks on election results, we know what's at stake. body:
This is the moment. We can’t waste it.
#
Here's how I see things, Peter:
Republicans have spent the last two years flooding the zone with lawlessness, cruelty, and corruption.
Voters had enough. They elected a majority of Democrats to Congress with a mandate to match that energy — boldly and unapologetically.
We don’t do that by simply just being the adults in the room. We have to prove that we’re FIGHTERS in the room.
So if it were up to me, we’d use our majority to fight for:
* **Saving health care.** Not just reversing Republicans’ cuts — advancing Medicare for ALL. Passing national abortion protections. Not just restoring what was stripped away — expanding reproductive rights.
* **Stopping data centers.** Putting real guardrails and oversight in place over the AI industry.
* **Enacting national voting rights** and economic reparations for Black people.
* **Stop the genocide and end the wars.**
* **Abolishing ICE.** Period.

Republicans showed us how they use their power to advance their agenda of chaos and harm. I have stopped wondering how low they can go — and have been focused on how hard we can fight.
This is the moment. We can’t waste it. We may not win every single fight — but voters fully expect us to take those righteous fights on. And we must.
**[We need to show that an agenda like this has real, public support. So Peter, will you split a donation between Justice Democrats and our campaign so we can fight hard for our new Democratic majority to prioritize an agenda like this? **Thursday, November 12, 2026 - **
_**Palestine:** Israel kills six people in attack on Nasser Hospital in Gaza. Israel kills one person in attack near entrance of Al-Shifa Hospital. Palestinian infant dies of hypothermia in Khan Younis. Five Palestinian fishermen missing after Israeli navy throws them overboard. Israeli settlers, soldiers attack Palestinians across occupied West Bank. Israeli Supreme Court denies request to release Gaza doctors detained without charge or trial._
_**Iran:** IRGC: Two supertankers on fire in Hormuz. Trump says no need for Iran deal. Iran designates Argentina's naval and air forces as "terrorist organizations."_
_**Yemen:** Ansarallah claims attacks on Saudi coalition._
_**Lebanon:** UN: Nearly a quarter of people in Lebanon face acute food shortages._
_**U.S.:** Democrat Scott Colom defeats Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi Senate race. House Republicans derail effort to impeach Hegseth. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after revelations of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate. Incoming House Intelligence chair vows to scrutinize the CIA's "extremely aggressive" use of covert actions under Trump. Marco Rubio's flights to University of Florida football games cost taxpayers more than $1.2 million. White House counsel threatens criminal investigation of congressional Democrats over planned oversight. U.S. military aircraft leave RAF base for the second time in two months. Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop migrant caravan. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved out of his home amid alleged Iranian threats. Chicago-area father died after a 38-hour deportation flight to Pakistan. Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House leader, keep John Thune as Senate minority leader. Senate and House Democrats debate leadership. Federal prosecutors charged former bodyguard for Rep. Ilhan Omar with felony, apparently to obtain incriminating information about her._
_**International:** Egyptian court postpones retrial of Mada Masr editor-in-chief to consider judge recusal request. Imran Khan's political party seeks access to him following hospital visit. Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agents to steal national security documents from Tajikistan. Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi conclude with prisoner-exchange agreement. Millions of workers in Spain protest housing crisis in 24-hour strike. China pledges to "firm support" Cuba against U.S. sanctions. Former member of Italian Red Brigades communist group escapes from Argentina house arrest. UN: Kidnappings in Haiti's capital increased in third quarter of 2026. DRC reports 11,042 Ebola cases, at least 5,387 deaths. UN: In 2026, almost 64,000 people have fled Nigeria for Niger to escape violence._
**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.KiVzWHsgWIwFgC5Ql3ExJOGAC4nB5HAFjKc0Cw_3jyM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=224621419)
* * *
# Palestine
* **Israel kills six people in attack on Nasser Hospital in Gaza:** An Israeli airstrike targeted Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis on Thursday, killing six people, including a doctor and a child, and wounding at least 28 others, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.
* Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed eight Palestinians and injured 29 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,653 killed and 176,007 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,622 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,878, while 850 bodies have been recovered.
* Footage from Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed of Nasser Hospital shows parts of the building badly damaged, and debris covering hospital beds and equipment.
* Among the dead is Dr. Rizq Abu Shuaira, a 52-year-old general surgeon who was killed alongside one of his patients, Dr. Ahmed al-Farra, general director of the hospital, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/a073d802-3bd4-4888-8323-98a30ff41fa7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Nasser Hospital was the last hospital in Gaza that offered specialized surgery, according to Al-Farra, leaving patients in need of such treatment to "face an unknown fate."
* Al-Farra said that the hospital was hit without warning by two missiles, one of which did not explode. The attack "paralyzed" the hospital, he added. A strike hit the main building of the medical complex, and knocked out services in four key departments: surgery, inpatient surgical wards, radiology, and laboratories.
* Nasser Hospital is one of the few medical facilities in Gaza that is even partially functioning, following years of systematic Israeli attacks. Following the latest strike, the Israeli military has attacked Nasser Hospital seven times since the genocide began, according to Al-Farra.
* The Israeli military admitted to the attack, and [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/968b159d-15e0-4390-8851-1c18436e013b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the strike was targeting a Hamas commander. In a statement, Hamas called Israel's claim a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime committed against a civilian medical facility protected under international law."

* **Israel kills one person in attack near entrance of Al-Shifa Hospital:** An Israeli airstrike near the gate of Al-Shifa Hospital killed one Palestinian and wounded several others on Thursday, according to Al Jazeera.
* One Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire east of Bureij camp, in central Gaza, on Thursday.
* **Palestinian infant dies of hypothermia in Khan Younis:** A Palestinian infant died of hypothermia in a tent in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, in southern Gaza on Thursday, Al Jazeera reported.
* Clips [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/2bd00329-f18d-4765-9d52-9ccd800619cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on social media show the body of 9-month-old Raqiq Kanan being carried by his father. "I woke up and found my son as you see him, blue-colored. I brought him to Nasser," his father said. "My son died frozen from the cold."
* Over the past three winters, numerous Palestinians--mostly infants--have died of hypothermia in Gaza, including 11 children last winter.
* **Five Palestinian fishermen missing after Israeli navy throws them overboard:** Five Palestinian fishermen are missing after the Israeli navy interrogated them on a military vessel and then threw them overboard off the coast of Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, WAFA reported.
* Israeli forces opened fire on the fishermen before detaining them and hauling them aboard a military vessel.
* **Israeli settlers, soldiers attack Palestinians across occupied West Bank:** Israeli settlers and soldiers carried out a series of raids and arrests across the occupied West Bank on Thursday, WAFA reported.
* Israeli settlers set fire to more than 100 vehicles, dozens of olive trees, and a warehouse in Al-Lubban Asharqiya, south of Nablus.
* Israeli forces arrested several Palestinians, searched homes, and damaged property in raids in Hebron, Jenin, Nablus, and Qalqilya.
* Israeli forces demolished a Palestinian home in Al-Khader, south of Bethlehem.
* **Israeli Supreme Court denies request to release Gaza doctors detained without charge or trial:** Israel's Supreme Court [refused](https://substack.com/redirect/33eb3253-ad3e-4ddb-9b3b-4352d99a8da2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to order the release of 14 Gaza doctors, including hospital directors and specialists, who are being detained without charge or trial under Israel's Unlawful Combatants Law. Some of the doctors have been in Israeli detention for more than two years.
* The advocacy group Physicians for Human Rights Israel had asked the court to direct the military's chief of staff to revoke their detention orders, citing the ceasefire and Gaza's collapsed health system.
* The court said it had reviewed the cases in light of Gaza's severe shortage of doctors but found no "exceptional grounds" to free them, and the court declined to intervene.

# Iran
* **Two supertankers on fire in Hormuz, IRGC says:** Two supertankers were hit by naval mines while traveling in what the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said was an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz. The tankers were carrying a combined total of more than four million barrels of oil.
* The IRGC said that any vessel in the strait "will meet a similar fate" if it switches off its navigation systems and cooperates with the U.S. military to use the strait's southern route.
* **Trump says no need for Iran deal:** President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the U.S. does not "need a deal with Iran." "Those days have long since passed," he wrote on Truth Social. "We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!"
* Commenting on Vice President JD Vance, Trump said, "I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S." The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Vance was considering face-to-face talks with Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to end the war.
* On Wednesday, Rezai [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/d325e684-823c-44ba-bb3a-ebab0d053709?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reports that Iran was negotiating directly with the U.S., calling reports of talks in Qatar and a planned meeting with Vice President JD Vance "lies" meant to ease economic pressure and lower oil prices. Rezaei said that Iran rejected Washington's first response to its seven conditions for peace as "not sufficient," saying it contained "deception." Iran is now waiting for "a clear and explicit response."
* **Iran designates Argentina 's naval and air forces as "terrorist organizations"**: Iran's Foreign Ministry [designated](https://substack.com/redirect/93950e2f-920c-4ad8-9bb2-a4ab06a06af3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Argentina's naval and air forces as "terrorist organizations" on Wednesday, noting Argentina's March similar designation of the IRGC in March and "the principle of reciprocity." It did not mention Argentina's army in its announcement. Argentina's foreign ministry rejected the move as "completely baseless" and "unacceptable." President Javier Milei's office designated the IRGC a "terrorist organization" on March 31, citing the 1994 AMIA Jewish community center bombing in Buenos Aires, which Argentina blames on Hezbollah.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah claims attacks on Saudi coalition:** Ansarallah [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/8162847a-e3bf-4ea2-b053-9a7cc4113501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several attacks on the Saudi-led coalition on Wednesday, including strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an oil pumping station in Yanbu, and a Saudi military command center in Aden's al-Buraiqa district. The Saudi-led coalition said that it intercepted three cruise missiles heading towards Riyadh, and two drones and two ballistic missiles over western Saudi Arabia.

# Lebanon
* **Nearly a quarter of people in Lebanon face acute food shortages, UN says:** More than a million people, or a quarter of Lebanon's population, [faces](https://substack.com/redirect/830eb71b-6e23-4724-b4f5-f7b48b7e419b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) food shortages as a result of two consecutive conflicts in the country, the UN warned on Wednesday.**** The FAO, World Food Programme and Lebanon's Agriculture Ministry said that the number is expected to rise to 1.15 million by mid-next year. WFP country director Allison Oman Lawi said families are running out of options, noting that "even a small additional shock can push them deeper into crisis." Lebanon estimates that conflicts since 2024 have cost it $27 billion, and that the most recent conflict with Hezbollah, launched by the government in March, has displaced over a million people, about 300,000 of whom remain displaced since violence subsided in June. Israeli troops still illegally occupy land in the country's south, exacerbating the ongoing displacement crisis.

# U.S. News
* **Democrat Scott Colom defeats Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi Senate race:** Democrat **Scott Colom** [defeated](https://substack.com/redirect/5aae2e43-bf46-496d-a42a-19cba432cc2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) incumbent GOP Sen. **Cindy Hyde-Smith** , according to the Associated Press, which called the race Wednesday after officials spent days processing absentee and affidavit ballots. Hyde-Smith conceded in a two-minute video, saying, "I respect the decision of Mississippi voters." Colom, 43, a local prosecutor and son of a onetime Reagan aide, is the first Democrat Mississippi has chosen for the Senate since 1947 and will be the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction. Trump won the state by 23 points in 2024.
* **House Republicans derail effort to impeach Hegseth:** The House [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/609a2efc-753e-4d45-ac75-7132f0ed06bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 211 to 204 to recommend charges against War Secretary Pete Hegseth to a committee, with only Rep. Thomas Massie, who led the effort, joining Democrats against the motion, which lets Republicans slow the process indefinitely. Eleven Democrats and seven Republicans missed the vote. Hegseth faced eight charges that could lead to impeachment, including waging war in Iran and elsewhere without congressional authorization, flouting laws to mitigate civilian casualties, and retaliating against a senator for public statements. Trump called the outcome an "exoneration" while warning that Democrats "must be stopped." Democrats could still move to impeach Hegseth next year, when they assume majorities in both chambers.
* **Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after revelations of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate: Jensen Huang,** Nvidia's CEO and co-founder, [resigned](https://substack.com/redirect/7cf6176c-91e4-4684-ab85-b48626411e55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday morning, according to the company's board of directors. His exit followed reporting from the New York Times that Huang had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate at the company. CFO **Colette Kress** will serve as interim CEO while the board conducts a search for Huang's replacement. Nvidia controls an estimated 90% of the market for advanced AI chips; its shares fell more than 10% in response to the announcement.
* **Incoming House Intelligence chair vows to scrutinize the CIA 's "extremely aggressive" use of covert actions under Trump:** Rep. **Jim Himes**(D-Conn.), the Democrat who will head the House's Intelligence Committee in the next Congress, [vowed](https://substack.com/redirect/aa646645-c3a7-4711-87eb-dae700ced288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday to investigate the CIA's use of covert actions under Trump, including the January abduction of Venezuelan President **Nicol as Maduro**,**** saying "covert action has become much more aggressive worldwide, and the committee would be massively failing at its job if it didn't double down on oversight." Himes also plans to examine donations from defense and intelligence contractors to Trump's "vanity projects," such as the White House ballroom and planned 250-foot triumphal arch.
* **Marco Rubio 's flights to University of Florida football games cost taxpayers more than $1.2 million:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio, whose son Anthony is a walk-on running back at the University of Florida, has [used](https://substack.com/redirect/d37933f0-211a-4963-8e57-6fce6ccd0d62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a government aircraft at least 23 times to get to and from Gainesville, with 15 of these trips designated as "solely personal" by the State Department, the Washington Post reported. The Post estimates these 15 flights cost about $770,600, with seven mixed-use trips adding $443,900. As a secretary barred from commercial flights, he must reimburse only an economy-fare equivalent (which would total $18,000, according to the post). Rubio said he will keep trying to attend events "important to me personally and to my family," and the State Department said his use of military aircraft ensured "secure communications" and "continuity of government."
* **White House counsel threatens criminal investigation of congressional Democrats over planned oversight:** White House counsel **Will Scharf** said the Trump administration is "monitoring the abusive and capricious threats" from Democrats and that their repeated promises to investigate the president and his allies could cross constitutional limits and into "blatant criminality." The threats came in a [letter](https://substack.com/redirect/9d7aaf8d-8065-4616-b2d2-1aa312e57437?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to incoming House Oversight Chair **Robert Garcia** (D-Calif.) Sharf added that the executive branch may respond by investigating Congress. President Trump has repeatedly threatened criminal sanctions against Democrats pledging to investigate his administration.
* **U.S. military aircraft leave RAF base for the second time in two months:** Flight tracking data [verified](https://substack.com/redirect/8ca0fa19-7ac2-4935-bf33-b33d3fd388d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Washington Post shows three Osprey helicopters and 10 KC-135R tankers redeployed on Monday from RAF Mildenhall to other bases in England, Scotland, Spain, and Germany, according to the Washington Post. The Wall Street Journal reported they were moved after an Iranian threat, the nature of which remained unclear. The U.S. previously removed bombers from RAF Fairford over a suspected terrorist plot, for which two men face charges.
* **Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop migrant caravan:** President Trump [threatened](https://substack.com/redirect/1fde2f0d-0d12-4e5a-940a-4bdd6210e0b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to double tariffs on Mexican imports if it does not stop a reported 1,500 migrants from traveling north toward the U.S. He called the migrant caravan an "invasion," and said that there would be "no leniency." Mexican President **Claudia Sheinbaum** pushed back against the threat: Since the start of Trump's second term migrant caravans have not reached the U.S.-Mexico border, she said, emphasizing that Mexican federal authorities manage migration through frameworks that allow people to return to their countries of origin or remain in Mexico.
* **Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved out of his home amid alleged Iranian threats:** Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** has [moved](https://substack.com/redirect/0b67f7a9-d5d7-4ed8-91bf-98ff87c4cf13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) out of his D.C.-area home and onto a military base, the New York Times reported on Tuesday. U.S. officials have reportedly concluded in recent weeks that Iranian plotting against current and former American officials had reached "a more advanced stage," sources told the Times, with intelligence particularly pointing to Bessent, who has led an economic pressure campaign since August to financially isolate Iran through sanctions. At least half a dozen officials moved to protected housing last year, including the presidential adviser (now Chief of Staff) **Stephen Miller** and former Attorney General **Pam Bondi**.
* **Chicago-area father died after a 38-hour deportation flight to Pakistan: Ayaz Ahmed** , a 61-year-old resident of the Chicago suburbs, [died](https://substack.com/redirect/cd2559c1-44a5-4a4c-8770-37364344853a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in August after a 38-hour deportation flight to Pakistan chartered by ICE, according to a Tuesday report from ABC7 Chicago. Ahmed was arrested in June for overstaying a visitor's visa, then held at Indiana's Clay County Justice Center, where his family says his health, including type 2 diabetes, deteriorated despite doctor's letters sent to ICE. In light of his health conditions, his family offered to buy his ticket to speed his removal, an offer declined by ICE. Witnesses deported alongside Ahmed on the flight said no medical aid was given after his condition worsened, he lost control of his bladder, and he fainted after landing. He died four days later.
* **Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House leader, keep John Thune as Senate minority leader:** Rep. **Jim Jordan** (R-Ohio), a founding member of the right-wing Freedom Caucus, will serve as the next House minority leader. He defeated Majority Leader Rep. **Steve Scalise** (R-La.) by 33 votes in Tuesday's secret ballot. Also in Tuesday's House GOP vote, Whip **Tom Emmer**(R-Minn.) beat a challenge from Rep. **August Pfluger**(R-Texas)**** to stay in his post, and **Lisa McClain**(R-Mich.) won conference chair in a three-way race over **Erin Houchin** (R-Ind.) and **Greg Steube** (R-Fla.).
* Senate Republicans reelected Sen. **John Thune** (R-S.D.) to lead their minority on Tuesday after a tense day of private meetings about their midterm losses. Thune ran unopposed and was elected by acclamation after the conference voted 31-15 to proceed rather than delay, a measure pushed for by Sens. **Josh Hawley**(R-Mo.) and **Ron Johnson**(R-Wis.). Thune promised to "make the most of the time we've got" in the final two months of the majority and to "come out swinging."
* **Senate and House Democrats debate leadership:** Rep. **Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez** declined on Tuesday to back **Chuck Schumer** for Senate majority leader: Asked by reporters outside the Capitol about the Senate's Democratic leadership, she said that the desire for new leadership "is seen in a lot of places." Schumer, who turns 76 this month, said that he has secured enough support to become majority leader.
* Ohio Rep.-elect **Don Leonard** said in a social media post on Tuesday that senior House Democrats vowed to make his life "a living hell" if he didn't back Rep. **Hakeem Jeffries** for House speaker. Leonard, who flipped a longstanding Republican district of Ohio, also said that members of Congress told him to vote for Jeffries regardless of whether he commits to issues like a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United and ending U.S. support for Israel and the Iran war. Jeffries can afford at least three dozen defections from House Democrats.
* **Federal prosecutors charged former bodyguard for Rep. Ilhan Omar with felony, apparently to obtain incriminating information about her:** **Abdullahi Mohamed** , a Somali-British citizen who briefly served on **Rep. Ilhan Omar 's **security detail on an overseas trip, was [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/bc39150b-2e0f-4ea3-b1e8-cbf1df867fa3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with lying under oath in a green card interview after answering "no" to nonstandard questions about working for the Somali government and interacting with U.S. officials, according to the New York Times. Prosecutors reportedly offered to block Mohamed's deportation in exchange for derogatory information about Omar, and reportedly told him the probe was "100 percent being run by 1600 Pennsylvania Ave." A spokeswoman for Omar called the attempt to enlist Mohamed "a staggering abuse of presidential power."

# Other International News
* **Egyptian court postpones retrial of Mada Masr editor-in-chief to consider judge recusal request:** On Wednesday, an Egyptian court [postponed](https://substack.com/redirect/a7abe223-7492-47b1-bc79-fc8b8e2ff2c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the trial of Mada Masa editor-in-chief Lina Attalah for November 18, so that the court could consider Attalah's request that the judge be recused. She is charged with publishing "false news" and running an unlicensed website. Attalah's legal team requested the recusal, Mada Masr said, because the judge "had already formed a conviction in mind against the defendant." The judge also convicted her in a separate case last month that human-rights groups characterized as a "sham," saying that it lacked due process.
* **Imran Khan 's political party seeks access to him following hospital visit: **Imran Khan was removed from his imprisonment for a short hospital visit, and returned to prison overnight. The political party he leads, Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI), [demanded](https://substack.com/redirect/2249a2fe-c36c-4c70-8d24-95f4e28d37d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) access to him. The PTI said that his hospital visit raised "deeply troubling questions" about his health, and noted that his family and personal doctors were not told of the hospital visit. They said that they learned of it from news reports. Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on corruption charges that he denies.
* **Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agents to steal national security documents from Tajikistan:** The Singapore-based firm CloudTek [said](https://substack.com/redirect/1176f593-de24-4a72-9670-ec0e071fcf97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a report published Wednesday that a group of Kazakhstan-linked hackers, nicknamed "Silent Lynx," used the open-source Hermes AI framework to steal more than 2,000 national security-related documents from Tajikistan. CloudTek discovered the operation during an investigation of a server that Silent Lynx left unsecured, Reuters reported. According to the CloudTek [report](https://substack.com/redirect/f1076220-3c5b-4e58-beef-5b9c7331ecc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the group also used autonomous AI agents to compromise Tajik railway networks and in operations targeting Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan.
* **Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi conclude with prisoner-exchange agreement:** Two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, [concluded](https://substack.com/redirect/a0ed7a73-3da6-4828-ae78-50b99d73f726?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday. Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed to a "large-scale" prisoner exchange, according to Vladimir Medinsky, Russia's chief negotiator, who said he would travel to Moscow alongside U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to discuss the talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The number of prisoners to be released will be finalized on Thursday, Kushner said. Following their meeting in Moscow, Witkoff and Kushner will meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin, Ireland.
* Separately on Wednesday, the Russian Foreign Ministry [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/f3433a98-3028-4799-ac1f-2cd76dee847e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the sudden and unexpected death of Alexander Darchiev, Russia's ambassador to the United States. No further details were offered about his death. Darchiev was appointed to the ambassador role a year-and-a-half ago. He previously served as ambassador to Canada, from 2014 to 2021.
* **Millions of workers in Spain protest housing crisis in 24-hour strike:** Millions of Spanish workers [participated](https://substack.com/redirect/b3aba259-bd42-49ad-ade8-932ddcb7fc03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a 24-hour walkout that began at midnight on Wednesday. The labor action disrupted public transport and forced businesses, factories, and shops to scale back their operations or close for the day. Spanish trade unions UGT and CCOO reported widespread participation in the action, including 90% of workers in the automotive and port sectors. Protests over the high cost of living became widespread in September, after an 87-year-old woman named Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her Madrid apartment She died just days after the eviction.
* **China pledges to "firm support" Cuba against U.S. sanctions: **On Wednesday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/272f2ab7-ae84-48d5-ba61-d980a70960c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that China would provide "firm support" for Cuba, which is under a U.S. blockade and stifling sanctions. Wang told Cuba's envoy that China would "strengthen communication" and coordination with the island nation, and that it would "jointly oppose power politics and unilateral actions." The U.S. has imposed a fuel embargo on the island since February, causing rolling blackouts and severe supply shortages across the country. The U.S. blockade has crippled Cuba's health care system.
* **Former member of Italian Red Brigades communist group escapes from Argentina house arrest:** A former member of Italy's Red Bridgades, 74-year-old Leonardo Bertulazzi, [escaped](https://substack.com/redirect/8eb43ce5-a27e-47c9-9f19-7121cff59ddc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from his house arrest in Argentina on Tuesday. He used a harness and a rope to climb out of a fifth-story apartment, the Associated Press reported. He remains at large. Bertulazzi faces extradition to Italy for terrorism-related crimes for which he received a 27-year sentence. He was allegedly involved in the 1978 kidnapping and killing of former Prime Minister Aldo Moro. In 2004, Argentina granted him refugee status, which was revoked in 2024 under President Javier Milei. Argentina's Supreme Court approved his extradition to Italy last year.
* **Kidnappings in Haiti 's capital increased in third quarter of 2026, UN says: **Kidnappings in Port-au-Prince, Haiti's capital city, [rose](https://substack.com/redirect/b2675807-5dc7-42f4-a36b-2d440deac7e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with the second quarter, according to the United Nations. Ten percent of kidnapping victims in the third quarter are children. Also in that period, armed gangs and security forces were responsible for almost all of the 1,167 killings and 459 injuries recorded across the country. The UN documented at least 344 victims of sexual violence at the hands of gang members, and 44 cases in which police executed or tried to execute people, compared to 14 case in the previous quarter.
* **DRC reports 11,042 Ebola cases, at least 5,387 deaths:** The Democratic Republic of the Congo [reports](https://substack.com/redirect/8ced1e31-75dc-4401-bfc7-cbf626556bb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 11,042 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,397 deaths, according to government data published on Thursday. It is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in Congo's history, and it is the second-largest and second-deadliest of all time, behind West Africa's 2014-2016 epidemic. Earlier this month, the World Health Organization approved trials of two new vaccines for the disease. Trial results are expected by early 2027.
* **In 2026, almost 64,000 people have fled Nigeria for Niger to escape violence, UN says:** Almost 64,000 people have [fled](https://substack.com/redirect/d469a663-5d14-414b-ac78-b8f276595df3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) northern Nigeria for Niger this year to escape attacks by Islamist militants and armed gangs, according to a new report by the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). Niger already hosts more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, including about 327,500 Nigerians. Most new arrivals settle in the border regions of Diffa and Tahoua. Diffa has received more than 23,000 people, two-thirds of whom are children. Thousands of people in Niger are struggling with limited food, water, shelter, and services, UNHCR spokesperson Dominique Hyde said. Aid agencies have reported increasing cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections, and poor sanitation.
