This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Israel kills six people in attack on Nasser Hospital in Gaza: An Israeli airstrike targeted Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis on Thursday, killing six people, including a doctor and a child, and wounding at least 28 others, according to Gaza's Health Ministry. Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed eight Palestinians and injured 29 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,653 killed and 176,007 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,622 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,878, while 850 bodies have been recovered. Footage from Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed of Nasser Hospital shows parts of the building badly damaged, and debris covering hospital beds and equipment. Among the dead is Dr. Rizq Abu Shuaira, a 52-year-old general surgeon who was killed alongside one of his patients, Dr. Ahmed al-Farra, general director of the hospital, . Nasser Hospital was the last hospital in Gaza that offered specialized surgery, according to Al-Farra, leaving patients in need of such treatment to "face an unknown fate." Al-Farra said that the hospital was hit without warning by two missiles, one of which did not explode. The attack "paralyzed" the hospital, he added. A strike hit the main building of the medical complex, and knocked out services in four key departments: surgery, inpatient surgical wards, radiology, and laboratories. Nasser Hospital is one of the few medical facilities in Gaza that is even partially functioning, following years of systematic Israeli attacks. Following the latest strike, the Israeli military has attacked Nasser Hospital seven times since the genocide began, according to Al-Farra. The Israeli military admitted to the attack, and that the strike was targeting a Hamas commander. In a statement, Hamas called Israel's claim a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime committed against a civilian medical facility protected under international law." Israel kills one person in attack near entrance of Al-Shifa Hospital: An Israeli airstrike near the gate of Al-Shifa Hospital killed one Palestinian and wounded several others on Thursday, according to Al Jazeera. One Palestinian was killed by Israeli gunfire east of Bureij camp, in central Gaza, on Thursday. Palestinian infant dies of hypothermia in Khan Younis: A Palestinian infant died of hypothermia in a tent in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, in southern Gaza on Thursday, Al Jazeera reported. Clips on social media show the body of 9-month-old Raqiq Kanan being carried by his father. "I woke up and found my son as you see him, blue-colored. I brought him to Nasser," his father said. "My son died frozen from the cold." Over the past three winters, numerous Palestinians--mostly infants--have died of hypothermia in Gaza, including 11 children last winter. Five Palestinian fishermen missing after Israeli navy throws them overboard: Five Palestinian fishermen are missing after the Israeli navy interrogated them on a military vessel and then threw them overboard off the coast of Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza, WAFA reported. Israeli forces opened fire on the fishermen before detaining them and hauling them aboard a military vessel. Israeli settlers, soldiers attack Palestinians across occupied West Bank: Israeli settlers and soldiers carried out a series of raids and arrests across the occupied West Bank on Thursday, WAFA reported. Israeli settlers set fire to more than 100 vehicles, dozens of olive trees, and a warehouse in Al-Lubban Asharqiya, south of Nablus. Israeli forces arrested several Palestinians, searched homes, and damaged property in raids in Hebron, Jenin, Nablus, and Qalqilya. Israeli forces demolished a Palestinian home in Al-Khader, south of Bethlehem. Israeli Supreme Court denies request to release Gaza doctors detained without charge or trial: Israel's Supreme Court to order the release of 14 Gaza doctors, including hospital directors and specialists, who are being detained without charge or trial under Israel's Unlawful Combatants Law. Some of the doctors have been in Israeli detention for more than two years. The advocacy group Physicians for Human Rights Israel had asked the court to direct the military's chief of staff to revoke their detention orders, citing the ceasefire and Gaza's collapsed health system. The court said it had reviewed the cases in light of Gaza's severe shortage of doctors but found no "exceptional grounds" to free them, and the court declined to intervene. Iran Two supertankers on fire in Hormuz, IRGC says: Two supertankers were hit by naval mines while traveling in what the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said was an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz. The tankers were carrying a combined total of more than four million barrels of oil. The IRGC said that any vessel in the strait "will meet a similar fate" if it switches off its navigation systems and cooperates with the U.S. military to use the strait's southern route. Trump says no need for Iran deal: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the U.S. does not "need a deal with Iran." "Those days have long since passed," he wrote on Truth Social. "We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!" Commenting on Vice President JD Vance, Trump said, "I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S." The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Vance was considering face-to-face talks with Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to end the war. On Wednesday, Rezai reports that Iran was negotiating directly with the U.S., calling reports of talks in Qatar and a planned meeting with Vice President JD Vance "lies" meant to ease economic pressure and lower oil prices. Rezaei said that Iran rejected Washington's first response to its seven conditions for peace as "not sufficient," saying it contained "deception." Iran is now waiting for "a clear and explicit response." Iran designates Argentina 's naval and air forces as "terrorist organizations": Iran's Foreign Ministry Argentina's naval and air forces as "terrorist organizations" on Wednesday, noting Argentina's March similar designation of the IRGC in March and "the principle of reciprocity." It did not mention Argentina's army in its announcement. Argentina's foreign ministry rejected the move as "completely baseless" and "unacceptable." President Javier Milei's office designated the IRGC a "terrorist organization" on March 31, citing the 1994 AMIA Jewish community center bombing in Buenos Aires, which Argentina blames on Hezbollah. Yemen Ansarallah claims attacks on Saudi coalition: Ansarallah several attacks on the Saudi-led coalition on Wednesday, including strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an oil pumping station in Yanbu, and a Saudi military command center in Aden's al-Buraiqa district. The Saudi-led coalition said that it intercepted three cruise missiles heading towards Riyadh, and two drones and two ballistic missiles over western Saudi Arabia. Lebanon Nearly a quarter of people in Lebanon face acute food shortages, UN says: More than a million people, or a quarter of Lebanon's population, food shortages as a result of two consecutive conflicts in the country, the UN warned on Wednesday. The FAO, World Food Programme and Lebanon's Agriculture Ministry said that the number is expected to rise to 1.15 million by mid-next year. WFP country director Allison Oman Lawi said families are running out of options, noting that "even a small additional shock can push them deeper into crisis." Lebanon estimates that conflicts since 2024 have cost it $27 billion, and that the most recent conflict with Hezbollah, launched by the government in March, has displaced over a million people, about 300,000 of whom remain displaced since violence subsided in June. Israeli troops still illegally occupy land in the country's south, exacerbating the ongoing displacement crisis. U.S. News Democrat Scott Colom defeats Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi Senate race: Democrat Scott Colom incumbent GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith , according to the Associated Press, which called the race Wednesday after officials spent days processing absentee and affidavit ballots. Hyde-Smith conceded in a two-minute video, saying, "I respect the decision of Mississippi voters." Colom, 43, a local prosecutor and son of a onetime Reagan aide, is the first Democrat Mississippi has chosen for the Senate since 1947 and will be the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction. Trump won the state by 23 points in 2024. House Republicans derail effort to impeach Hegseth: The House 211 to 204 to recommend charges against War Secretary Pete Hegseth to a committee, with only Rep. Thomas Massie, who led the effort, joining Democrats against the motion, which lets Republicans slow the process indefinitely. Eleven Democrats and seven Republicans missed the vote. Hegseth faced eight charges that could lead to impeachment, including waging war in Iran and elsewhere without congressional authorization, flouting laws to mitigate civilian casualties, and retaliating against a senator for public statements. Trump called the outcome an "exoneration" while warning that Democrats "must be stopped." Democrats could still move to impeach Hegseth next year, when they assume majorities in both chambers. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after revelations of affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's CEO and co-founder, on Thursday morning, according to the company's board of directors. His exit followed reporting from the New York Times that Huang had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate at the company. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board conducts a search for Huang's replacement. Nvidia controls an estimated 90% of the market for advanced AI chips; its shares fell more than 10% in response to the announcement. Incoming House Intelligence chair vows to scrutinize the CIA 's "extremely aggressive" use of covert actions under Trump: Rep. Jim Himes(D-Conn.), the Democrat who will head the House's Intelligence Committee in the next Congress, on Wednesday to investigate the CIA's use of covert actions under Trump, including the January abduction of Venezuelan President Nicol as Maduro, saying "covert action has become much more aggressive worldwide, and the committee would be massively failing at its job if it didn't double down on oversight." Himes also plans to examine donations from defense and intelligence contractors to Trump's "vanity projects," such as the White House ballroom and planned 250-foot triumphal arch. Marco Rubio 's flights to University of Florida football games cost taxpayers more than $1.2 million: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, whose son Anthony is a walk-on running back at the University of Florida, has a government aircraft at least 23 times to get to and from Gainesville, with 15 of these trips designated as "solely personal" by the State Department, the Washington Post reported. The Post estimates these 15 flights cost about $770,600, with seven mixed-use trips adding $443,900. As a secretary barred from commercial flights, he must reimburse only an economy-fare equivalent (which would total $18,000, according to the post). Rubio said he will keep trying to attend events "important to me personally and to my family," and the State Department said his use of military aircraft ensured "secure communications" and "continuity of government." White House counsel threatens criminal investigation of congressional Democrats over planned oversight: White House counsel Will Scharf said the Trump administration is "monitoring the abusive and capricious threats" from Democrats and that their repeated promises to investigate the president and his allies could cross constitutional limits and into "blatant criminality." The threats came in a to incoming House Oversight Chair Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) Sharf added that the executive branch may respond by investigating Congress. President Trump has repeatedly threatened criminal sanctions against Democrats pledging to investigate his administration. U.S. military aircraft leave RAF base for the second time in two months: Flight tracking data by the Washington Post shows three Osprey helicopters and 10 KC-135R tankers redeployed on Monday from RAF Mildenhall to other bases in England, Scotland, Spain, and Germany, according to the Washington Post. The Wall Street Journal reported they were moved after an Iranian threat, the nature of which remained unclear. The U.S. previously removed bombers from RAF Fairford over a suspected terrorist plot, for which two men face charges. Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it does not stop migrant caravan: President Trump to double tariffs on Mexican imports if it does not stop a reported 1,500 migrants from traveling north toward the U.S. He called the migrant caravan an "invasion," and said that there would be "no leniency." Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum pushed back against the threat: Since the start of Trump's second term migrant caravans have not reached the U.S.-Mexico border, she said, emphasizing that Mexican federal authorities manage migration through frameworks that allow people to return to their countries of origin or remain in Mexico. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved out of his home amid alleged Iranian threats: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has out of his D.C.-area home and onto a military base, the New York Times reported on Tuesday. U.S. officials have reportedly concluded in recent weeks that Iranian plotting against current and former American officials had reached "a more advanced stage," sources told the Times, with intelligence particularly pointing to Bessent, who has led an economic pressure campaign since August to financially isolate Iran through sanctions. At least half a dozen officials moved to protected housing last year, including the presidential adviser (now Chief of Staff) Stephen Miller and former Attorney General Pam Bondi. Chicago-area father died after a 38-hour deportation flight to Pakistan: Ayaz Ahmed , a 61-year-old resident of the Chicago suburbs, in August after a 38-hour deportation flight to Pakistan chartered by ICE, according to a Tuesday report from ABC7 Chicago. Ahmed was arrested in June for overstaying a visitor's visa, then held at Indiana's Clay County Justice Center, where his family says his health, including type 2 diabetes, deteriorated despite doctor's letters sent to ICE. In light of his health conditions, his family offered to buy his ticket to speed his removal, an offer declined by ICE. Witnesses deported alongside Ahmed on the flight said no medical aid was given after his condition worsened, he lost control of his bladder, and he fainted after landing. He died four days later. Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House leader, keep John Thune as Senate minority leader: Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio), a founding member of the right-wing Freedom Caucus, will serve as the next House minority leader. He defeated Majority Leader Rep. Steve Scalise (R-La.) by 33 votes in Tuesday's secret ballot. Also in Tuesday's House GOP vote, Whip Tom Emmer(R-Minn.) beat a challenge from Rep. August Pfluger(R-Texas)** to stay in his post, and Lisa McClain(R-Mich.) won conference chair in a three-way race over Erin Houchin (R-Ind.) and Greg Steube (R-Fla.). Senate Republicans reelected Sen. John Thune (R-S.D.) to lead their minority on Tuesday after a tense day of private meetings about their midterm losses. Thune ran unopposed and was elected by acclamation after the conference voted 31-15 to proceed rather than delay, a measure pushed for by Sens. Josh Hawley(R-Mo.) and Ron Johnson(R-Wis.). Thune promised to "make the most of the time we've got" in the final two months of the majority and to "come out swinging." Senate and House Democrats debate leadership: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez declined on Tuesday to back Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader: Asked by reporters outside the Capitol about the Senate's Democratic leadership, she said that the desire for new leadership "is seen in a lot of places." Schumer, who turns 76 this month, said that he has secured enough support to become majority leader. Ohio Rep.-elect Don Leonard said in a social media post on Tuesday that senior House Democrats vowed to make his life "a living hell" if he didn't back Rep. Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker. Leonard, who flipped a longstanding Republican district of Ohio, also said that members of Congress told him to vote for Jeffries regardless of whether he commits to issues like a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United and ending U.S. support for Israel and the Iran war. Jeffries can afford at least three dozen defections from House Democrats. Federal prosecutors charged former bodyguard for Rep. Ilhan Omar with felony, apparently to obtain incriminating information about her: Abdullahi Mohamed , a Somali-British citizen who briefly served on Rep. Ilhan Omar 's security detail on an overseas trip, was with lying under oath in a green card interview after answering "no" to nonstandard questions about working for the Somali government and interacting with U.S. officials, according to the New York Times. Prosecutors reportedly offered to block Mohamed's deportation in exchange for derogatory information about Omar, and reportedly told him the probe was "100 percent being run by 1600 Pennsylvania Ave." A spokeswoman for Omar called the attempt to enlist Mohamed "a staggering abuse of presidential power." 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Egyptian court postpones retrial of Mada Masr editor-in-chief to consider judge recusal request: On Wednesday, an Egyptian court the trial of Mada Masa editor-in-chief Lina Attalah for November 18, so that the court could consider Attalah's request that the judge be recused. She is charged with publishing "false news" and running an unlicensed website. Attalah's legal team requested the recusal, Mada Masr said, because the judge "had already formed a conviction in mind against the defendant." The judge also convicted her in a separate case last month that human-rights groups characterized as a "sham," saying that it lacked due process. Imran Khan 's political party seeks access to him following hospital visit: Imran Khan was removed from his imprisonment for a short hospital visit, and returned to prison overnight. The political party he leads, Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI), access to him. The PTI said that his hospital visit raised "deeply troubling questions" about his health, and noted that his family and personal doctors were not told of the hospital visit. They said that they learned of it from news reports. Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on corruption charges that he denies. Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agents to steal national security documents from Tajikistan: The Singapore-based firm CloudTek in a report published Wednesday that a group of Kazakhstan-linked hackers, nicknamed "Silent Lynx," used the open-source Hermes AI framework to steal more than 2,000 national security-related documents from Tajikistan. CloudTek discovered the operation during an investigation of a server that Silent Lynx left unsecured, Reuters reported. According to the CloudTek , the group also used autonomous AI agents to compromise Tajik railway networks and in operations targeting Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi conclude with prisoner-exchange agreement: Two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, on Wednesday. Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed to a "large-scale" prisoner exchange, according to Vladimir Medinsky, Russia's chief negotiator, who said he would travel to Moscow alongside U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to discuss the talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The number of prisoners to be released will be finalized on Thursday, Kushner said. Following their meeting in Moscow, Witkoff and Kushner will meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin, Ireland. Separately on Wednesday, the Russian Foreign Ministry the sudden and unexpected death of Alexander Darchiev, Russia's ambassador to the United States. No further details were offered about his death. Darchiev was appointed to the ambassador role a year-and-a-half ago. He previously served as ambassador to Canada, from 2014 to 2021. Millions of workers in Spain protest housing crisis in 24-hour strike: Millions of Spanish workers in a 24-hour walkout that began at midnight on Wednesday. The labor action disrupted public transport and forced businesses, factories, and shops to scale back their operations or close for the day. Spanish trade unions UGT and CCOO reported widespread participation in the action, including 90% of workers in the automotive and port sectors. Protests over the high cost of living became widespread in September, after an 87-year-old woman named Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her Madrid apartment She died just days after the eviction. China pledges to "firm support" Cuba against U.S. sanctions: On Wednesday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi that China would provide "firm support" for Cuba, which is under a U.S. blockade and stifling sanctions. Wang told Cuba's envoy that China would "strengthen communication" and coordination with the island nation, and that it would "jointly oppose power politics and unilateral actions." The U.S. has imposed a fuel embargo on the island since February, causing rolling blackouts and severe supply shortages across the country. The U.S. blockade has crippled Cuba's health care system. Former member of Italian Red Brigades communist group escapes from Argentina house arrest: A former member of Italy's Red Bridgades, 74-year-old Leonardo Bertulazzi, from his house arrest in Argentina on Tuesday. He used a harness and a rope to climb out of a fifth-story apartment, the Associated Press reported. He remains at large. Bertulazzi faces extradition to Italy for terrorism-related crimes for which he received a 27-year sentence. He was allegedly involved in the 1978 kidnapping and killing of former Prime Minister Aldo Moro. In 2004, Argentina granted him refugee status, which was revoked in 2024 under President Javier Milei. Argentina's Supreme Court approved his extradition to Italy last year. Kidnappings in Haiti 's capital increased in third quarter of 2026, UN says: Kidnappings in Port-au-Prince, Haiti's capital city, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with the second quarter, according to the United Nations. Ten percent of kidnapping victims in the third quarter are children. Also in that period, armed gangs and security forces were responsible for almost all of the 1,167 killings and 459 injuries recorded across the country. The UN documented at least 344 victims of sexual violence at the hands of gang members, and 44 cases in which police executed or tried to execute people, compared to 14 case in the previous quarter. DRC reports 11,042 Ebola cases, at least 5,387 deaths: The Democratic Republic of the Congo 11,042 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,397 deaths, according to government data published on Thursday. It is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in Congo's history, and it is the second-largest and second-deadliest of all time, behind West Africa's 2014-2016 epidemic. Earlier this month, the World Health Organization approved trials of two new vaccines for the disease. Trial results are expected by early 2027. In 2026, almost 64,000 people have fled Nigeria for Niger to escape violence, UN says: Almost 64,000 people have northern Nigeria for Niger this year to escape attacks by Islamist militants and armed gangs, according to a new report by the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). Niger already hosts more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, including about 327,500 Nigerians. Most new arrivals settle in the border regions of Diffa and Tahoua. Diffa has received more than 23,000 people, two-thirds of whom are children. Thousands of people in Niger are struggling with limited food, water, shelter, and services, UNHCR spokesperson Dominique Hyde said. name: Courier Newsroom
subject: I could not be more thankful
body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1004&refcode=20261112_TM_T1&akid=316%2E344797%2EupcD-G ]COURIER Newsroom

Peter,

I can’t overstate how big last week's elections were — not only for
Democrats, but for a rising political realignment powered by voters across
the political spectrum.

Millions of people just used their voices and votes to deliver a
thunderous rebuke of the Trump agenda and send a mandate for
transformative economic populism, an end to political corruption, and bold
system change to Washington.

From Michigan and North Carolina to Georgia and Texas and more, COURIER’s
network of newsrooms and on-the-ground reporters played an outsized role
in creating the conditions for last week's outcome — and I could not be
more proud of our team or more thankful for supporters like you.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/14137?t=1002&refcode=20261112_TM_T1&akid=316%2E344797%2EupcD-G ]Before I share more about our impact this cycle, can you take a quick
moment to donate $10 or any amount to help power COURIER’s reporting?
We’ve got big plans to cover the new Democratic majorities next year and
make sure they’re accountable to voters — and we’re counting on donations
from supporters like you in order to do it.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/14137?t=1003&refcode=20261112_TM_T1&akid=316%2E344797%2EupcD-G ]Contribute $10

COURIER’s network of local newsrooms has consistently beat the drum on
issues that voters deeply cared about and which drove them to the polls.

That network now reaches over 120 million Americans each and every week
online with our coverage, and has earned the trust of over 11 million
subscribers network-wide.

From our local reporting on the cost-of-living crisis, ICE terrorism,
stripping of reproductive rights, unprecedented corruption, the Epstein
cover-up, and the rising opposition to AI and data centers, our 20 local
newsrooms reached news-consuming audiences on the issues they cared about.
We proved the importance of local, independent journalism rooted in the
communities it serves — and last Tuesday, our influence was on display all
over the literal map.

Here’s a snapshot of what our team put into the feeds of voters on
Election Day alone:

* Published over 1,100 pieces across social media to keep communities
informed
* Secured over 13.6 million media views across platforms
* Drove 400,000 newsletter opens
* Gained 57,000 new followers across our network
* Spoke to hundreds of voters at polling places to uplift issues that
matter to them

But unlike so many hard-fought campaigns, our work at COURIER doesn’t end
on Election Day.

Our teams are already working to cover the transition of government, and
are preparing to continue holding elected officials accountable for both
the promises they made on the campaign trail and to deliver on voters’
demands — like ending the corruption in Washington and unrigging the
economy that favors the richest Americans at an unbearable cost to
everyone else.

We’ll have more to share on our plans soon, including opportunities to
help us keep building on these tremendous wins and momentum to carry us
into 2028. But for now, Peter, I just wanted to take a moment to
thank you for supporting COURIER over the past year.

Your support has put us in a position to change the playbook — and to
change what’s possible next year and in the years to come.

With gratitude,

Tara McGowan
Founder & Publisher, COURIER Newsroom

COURIER

We’ve got big plans to cover the new Democratic majorities next year and
make sure they are accountable to voters — and we are counting on
donations from supporters like you in order to do it. Make a contribution
to help power COURIER’s reporting:

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20261112_TM_T1&akid=316%2E344797%2EupcD-G ]Donate
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/14138?refcode=email_footer_member_20261112_TM_T1&t=1001&akid=316%2E344797%2EupcD-G ]Become a Member

Email us: [ mailto:info@couriernewsroom.com ]info@couriernewsroom.com

This message was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we
communicate with grassroots supporters like you.

To give by check:

COURIER Newsroom
3229 Greenpoint Ave, PMB 532
Long Island City, New York 11101

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.couriernewsroom.com/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=316%2E344797%2EupcD-G

body:
I’m feeling immense hope for our future.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=4122%2E21716%2EI8OZA9)
I’m feeling immense hope for our future.
**Last week, Delawareans sent me back to Congress, and voters across the country put Democrats in the majority in both the House and Senate.**
With these majorities, we’ll have the power to hold Donald Trump and his entire administration accountable, with real oversight and real consequences.
We’ll also have the opportunity to get to work on an agenda that finally puts working families first: lowering costs, protecting healthcare, and defending the freedoms MAGA Republicans have spent two years attacking.
I keep thinking about the families I’ve sat with over the years. The dad rationing his insulin, the mom choosing between a paycheck and staying home with her sick kid, the seniors watching their grocery bills climb every month.
For two years, this administration answered them with cruelty and corruption. **That ends in January.**
But I learned after my first election to the Delaware State Senate that winning the vote is only the beginning. The real work starts immediately after.
That’s why I’m asking you to stay in this fight with me in the coming months. You know that Trump and his allies will throw everything they have at stopping us, and I’m going to be counting on grassroots supporters like you to stand with me.
[**So, if you can, please consider chipping in $5 or any amount you can to make sure we have what it takes to deliver on every promise we made in this campaign.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261112.XbKGzk&refcode=em20261112-4122&amount=5&t=2&akid=4122%2E21716%2EI8OZA9)

In solidarity,
Sarah McBride

Friend,

Now that the dust has begun to settle, I wanted to reach out directly with the most important words I can say: **Thank you.**

When we started this race, we knew the hill would be steep. We knew special interests and corporate PACs would pour unprecedented amounts of money into protecting the status quo.

And they did. Kelly Ayotte and her allies outspent us by millions of dollars.

Yet because of you—your doors knocked, calls made, dollars chipped in, and unwavering belief in our state—we made this race competitive. _Despite being outspent at historic levels, we came closer to defeating a first-term governor than anyone in New Hampshire has since 2004._

Look at what we accomplished together:
* We cut the margin in half: We shrank the Republican gubernatorial margin from roughly 10 points in 2024 down to about 4 points.
* We gained ground everywhere: We expanded our support across the state, making major inroads in Manchester, Derry, and Nashua, where we even beat Ayotte in her own home ward!

**None of that was possible without you. I truly mean that.** While the final result wasn’t the one we worked so tirelessly for, what we proved this year cannot be erased. We proved that Granite Staters are hungry for honest leadership, lower costs, and a government that works for everyday people, not Donald Trump or corporate special interests.

Because of the work you put in, our state now has Democratic majorities in the State House, State Senate, and on the Executive Council. For the next two years, these will be crucial checks and balances that will defend our values, protect reproductive freedom, and look out for working families every single day.

The fight for a fairer, stronger New Hampshire doesn’t stop here, and I am endlessly proud to stand alongside you in it.

Thank you for everything.

Cinde Warmington

clean_body: | If you’d like to unsubscribe, | Friend, Now that the dust has begun to settle, I wanted to reach out directly with the most important words I can say: Thank you. When we started this race, we knew the hill would be steep. We knew special interests and corporate PACs would pour unprecedented amounts of money into protecting the status quo. And they did. Kelly Ayotte and her allies outspent us by millions of dollars. Yet because of you—your doors knocked, calls made, dollars chipped in, and unwavering belief in our state—we made this race competitive. Despite being outspent at historic levels, we came closer to defeating a first-term governor than anyone in New Hampshire has since 2004. Look at what we accomplished together: We cut the margin in half: We shrank the Republican gubernatorial margin from roughly 10 points in 2024 down to about 4 points. We gained ground everywhere: We expanded our support across the state, making major inroads in Manchester, Derry, and Nashua, where we even beat Ayotte in her own home ward! None of that was possible without you. I truly mean that. While the final result wasn’t the one we worked so tirelessly for, what we proved this year cannot be erased. We proved that Granite Staters are hungry for honest leadership, lower costs, and a government that works for everyday people, not Donald Trump or corporate special interests. Because of the work you put in, our state now has Democratic majorities in the State House, State Senate, and on the Executive Council. For the next two years, these will be crucial checks and balances that will defend our values, protect reproductive freedom, and look out for working families every single day. The fight for a fairer, stronger New Hampshire doesn’t stop here, and I am endlessly proud to stand alongside you in it. Thank you for everything. # Copy & Paste from Text Messages on iPhone
Copying and pasting from text messages on the iPhone has always been a bit of a pain. For so long, the only way to do it was to copy the entire message at once. Well, with the latest version of iOS, you can now select specific parts of a text to copy to your clipboard. This is very useful if you want to share or search a chunk of a longer text message without copying the whole thing or without sharing personal information.
## Why You'll Love This Tip
* **Copy specific parts of text messages without copying the whole message.**
* **Easily look up words or phrases that are texted to you.**

## How to Copy a Text Message on iPhone
### System Requirements
_This tip was tested on an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 26.0.1, but it also works on devices running iOS 27. Find out how to update to the[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-260641-8632208-d3a243fff3-bu10a02c61)._You can now easily highlight and copy a selection of text from your messages on iOS 26. This is super convenient for copying specific information that someone texted you. For more helpful iPhone shortcuts and tricks, check out our free [Tip of the Day](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-260641-8632209-ba03b4ec4a-bu10a02c61) newsletter. Now, here’s how to copy a text message on iPhone:
1. Long-press the text bubble that you want to copy.

|
---
2. Choose **Select** in the menu that appears.

---
3. Highlight the text you want to copy by dragging the blue dots at the start and end of the text.

---
### Enjoying Your Tip of the Day?

4. Tap **Copy**.

---

That’s how to use the new text features on iPhone. Now you’re free to paste your copied text wherever you want! Next, find out the [RCS meaning](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-260641-8632210-6b6eb7d226-bu10a02c61) in your Messages app.

Dear Patriot,

Nearly twenty years in this work has taught me one rule about
Washington:

WHEN A DOOR OPENS, SOMEONE IS ALREADY PUSHING IT SHUT.

Senator Rand Paul opened one for us. Send subpoena requests to his
office . . . the one office in the Senate with sole power to issue
them.

NO REPORTER HAS EVER HELD A KEY LIKE THIS.

Since then, you and I have a responsibility to build something fast: A
small team of researchers and professionals must be funded and put to
work right now.

Threads picked: the ballot cash. The border money. The Pfizer papers.
And one twenty-year theory, at last ready for its test.

Now for the truth about doors . . .

Gavels change hands. Sessions end. And the first time a return comes
back with a big name on it, they will push hard to shut this down.
Harder than we have ever felt.

SENATOR PAUL'S OFFER HAS NO CLOSING DATE PRINTED ON IT. WASHINGTON
WILL PRINT ONE FOR US IF WE MOVE SLOW.

So we will not move slow.

If you have been waiting, THIS IS THE MOMENT. EVERY GIFT, BIG OR
SMALL, GOES THROUGH THAT OPEN DOOR WITH US.

In Truth,[James O'Keefe]

# [CEO Huang resigns over Chinese spy affair as Nvidia crashes](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3dc157-40a7-42cd-b5e7-f5958311e1a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jensen Huang **[stepped down as Nvidia president, CEO and board member effective immediately](https://substack.com/redirect/4b182b48-18dc-4b6c-a3c5-a5227ec81117?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4b182b48-18dc-4b6c-a3c5-a5227ec81117?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Thursday after affairs involving a suspected Chinese spy **[and a subordinate,](https://substack.com/redirect/268a4a93-5b20-4ecf-8461-62364934a82f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** sending shares **[down about 10%](https://substack.com/redirect/cc26073b-b3f9-45b0-929c-247263df76c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and stalling the AI trade after Wednesday's rebound.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3dc157-40a7-42cd-b5e7-f5958311e1a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Kress named interim** : Colette Kress, CFO since 2013,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/24718e78-6d33-4b78-975d-c3c8b231e7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[serves as interim CEO](https://substack.com/redirect/24718e78-6d33-4b78-975d-c3c8b231e7ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while retaining the finance role until a permanent successor is chosen from internal or external candidates.
* **Jones first chair** : Longtime director Harvey C. Jones, a former Synopsys CEO, becomes Nvidia's first-ever board chair as the board begins its search.
* **Stock market hit** : Shares fell roughly 10% in premarket trading to levels not seen since July 2025, erasing hundreds of billions in market value and dragging AI names.
* **CoreWeave contrast** : CoreWeave's strong results had revived the AI trade Wednesday before the Huang news reversed futures and pressured the broader tech rebound.

**[Nasdaq futures slid Thursday](https://substack.com/redirect/f6343400-5b52-4bbe-ac21-64480a23f12e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as Nvidia's leadership crisis pressured the AI trade, **[reversing Wednesday's CoreWeave-fueled rebound](https://substack.com/redirect/b0916a52-b412-4100-928a-4cbf0a2fb7db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that had lifted tech shares after a historic selloff.

---|---|---

* **Thursday drag** : Nvidia's plunge pulled[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf70521-a782-48b3-9bbd-0850dbd5cf2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[major index futures lower,](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf70521-a782-48b3-9bbd-0850dbd5cf2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf70521-a782-48b3-9bbd-0850dbd5cf2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with the Nasdaq futures down sharply as the scandal stalled the rebound.
* **Broader pressure** : Asian markets also felt the weight of the Nvidia news, while oil and yields added secondary pressure to the open.
* **Volatility stretch** : The Nasdaq had already seen some of its widest daily moves in more than a year heading into the latest swing.

# [Lawmakers and China scrutinize Nvidia spy affair](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3dc157-40a7-42cd-b5e7-f5958311e1a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The affair linking Jensen Huang to a woman U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese Ministry of State Security asset has intensified calls for tighter chip controls and congressional scrutiny ahead of any Trump-Xi talks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3dc157-40a7-42cd-b5e7-f5958311e1a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Alice Huang details** : The woman tied to Megaspeed **[visited Taiwan eight times](https://substack.com/redirect/eb186461-9b39-419b-80ed-c6a7b3570e87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in 2024 and 2025; **[her husband Kang Wei introduced her to Huang](https://substack.com/redirect/79b57192-ac89-4f14-a695-2155970b30f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and appeared to accept the relationship.
* **Second affair** : The New York Times reported[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a178a81c-772b-4a5d-8019-f102d60fc040?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[a separate relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's healthcare vice president](https://substack.com/redirect/a178a81c-772b-4a5d-8019-f102d60fc040?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who reported directly to Huang.
* **Lawmaker action** : Sens. Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the administration to preserve records on Nvidia's China chip exports and related security risks.
* **Beijing response** : China accused Washington of using the drama to justify a chip blockade as the scandal unfolded.

Colette Kress **[steps in as Nvidia's interim CEO](https://substack.com/redirect/91def5e9-5862-4acb-bf84-689d4c9e8bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while the board searches for a permanent leader, and **[Elon Musk said](https://substack.com/redirect/928da460-7fd6-4f43-92c9-3ad46b7e6821?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** hiring the departing founder would be "an honor."

Nvidia's board faces calls to[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7e02b195-c204-46af-86a3-b9c276f025a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[treat the company as a large public enterprise](https://substack.com/redirect/7e02b195-c204-46af-86a3-b9c276f025a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7e02b195-c204-46af-86a3-b9c276f025a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)rather than a founder-led private firm as it searches for a permanent CEO with no formal succession plan in place.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3dc157-40a7-42cd-b5e7-f5958311e1a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Board duty** : The board has a responsibility to other shareholders to operate more like a professionally run public company.
* **No succession plan** : Huang's sudden exit left the firm without a named permanent successor, elevating key-person risk.
* **Search underway** : Directors are initiating a process that will consider both internal and external candidates.
* **Key-person shock** : Analysts and market participants **[described the departure as a major governance and concentration risk event.](https://substack.com/redirect/0bb556f3-ef0e-4bf9-afe6-b8b056416ae7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

[ Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/01594d84-f895-47d9-ae1f-23566157bf36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# [Megaspeed network under scrutiny in Nvidia spy probe](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3dc157-40a7-42cd-b5e7-f5958311e1a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Megaspeed sits at the center of a U.S. probe into **[the diversion of billions of restricted Nvidia chips to China,](https://substack.com/redirect/f2de1099-246d-4ec6-b97b-c1b00e2b8679?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f2de1099-246d-4ec6-b97b-c1b00e2b8679?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with its executive linked to the affair involving Jensen Huang.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e3dc157-40a7-42cd-b5e7-f5958311e1a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Probe focus** : The Singapore-based firm **[is under investigation for possibly funneling advanced AI chips past export controls.](https://substack.com/redirect/be05a586-ab5e-41dc-9335-ce936e279781?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Singapore sales** : Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore revenue last year as scrutiny of Megaspeed rose.
* **Executive ties** : Alice Huang's role at the firm has drawn additional attention amid the national-security allegations.
* **Broader network** : Reports describe entities in Singapore and Malaysia used to move hardware toward Chinese customers.

As I set priorities for my third term, I want your voice to be part of the process.

Gabe Vasquez won the most competitive Democratic seat in Congress in 2022. He's running to be a champion for working families and build an economy that benefits everyone. #### _**[I got emotional watching Scott Colom win Mississippi. Not just because of what that victory means, but because of what it proves: no state is hopeless, no community should be written off, and ordinary people can still change this country when we fight for them. That's the mission behind Endless Urgency. We're building independent media that challenges the right-wing propaganda machine, elevates leaders who actually give a damn, and refuses to let cynicism win. If you believe in that mission, become a paid subscriber for just $8/month and help us build something bigger.](https://substack.com/redirect/a71f6e92-0f63-483a-bc96-d8388ca419c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_

* * *
I'm not going to lie to you: I was fighting back tears when they finally called the Mississippi Senate race for Scott Colom.
The first Black senator from Mississippi since Reconstruction. If you can watch something like that happen and not feel it deep in your soul, there's something wrong with you. It's a momentous victory, and it tells you how far this country has come, and where it's headed.
Colom earned every bit of it. You've probably seen the ad by now. Cindy Hyde-Smith, a sitting United States senator, got asked about the price of beef and told people they should just pick another protein. That's how out of touch these people are. Working families in one of the poorest states in the country are getting crushed at the grocery store, and her advice is to eat something cheaper. Let them eat chicken.
Colom's response was perfect: Pick another protein? Pick another senator. And Mississippi did.
You'd think Republicans might take this as a sign. A state as deep red and as suppressed as Mississippi is, just sent a man like Scott Colom to the United States Senate. Any normal political party would stop and reflect on everything it's done to hurt the American people and drive this country toward a cliff.
But they aren't capable of that kind of introspection. So, as I've been writing to you all week, they're doubling down on their very worst instincts.
They promoted Stephen Miller to Chief of Staff, which means more immigration aggression and more corruption. They named Jim Jordan minority leader in the House, a guy whose somehow more conservative than Mike Johnson. And they're going on cable news and repeating the same handful of stupid talking points that lost them the midterms: trans kids, gas prices under Joe Biden, Donald Trump's golden age of America.
I saw it up close yesterday on Newsmax. The MAGA pundit debating me said that every Democrat elected on Tuesday is a communist. Then he went further and claimed Abdul El-Sayed had said he wanted to seize the means of production from the floor of the United States Senate. I asked him to show me where. He couldn't, because it never happened. So I told him to his face, on his own network, that he was lying. He didn't like that. But, I do not care.
That's where the Republican Party is right now. They've learned absolutely fucking nothing from this loss. They're blaming the voters. They think that if they scream about trans kids even louder, and gaslight you into believing Donald Trump knows what the fuck he's doing, that the economy is great for everyone, and that your struggles are your fault instead of the fault of the Republicans stealing from you, they'll win.
It didn't work last Tuesday, and it won't work now. They'll keep nominating candidates who are wildly out of step with their states because Donald Trump likes them, and that will continue to hurt the party.
* * *
#### _**[Here's why these victories matter so much to me. People like Scott Colom, Annie Andrews, James Talarico didn't wait until winning looked easy. They stepped up when things looked hopeless because they believed their communities deserved better. That's what we're committed to elevating at Endless Urgency. We're not here just to dunk on Republicans or celebrate election night. We're here to expose the lies, challenge Democrats to deliver, and keep fighting for a country where working people can afford a decent life. For $8/month, you can help us keep telling the stories that the political establishment too often overlooks.](https://substack.com/redirect/a71f6e92-0f63-483a-bc96-d8388ca419c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/a71f6e92-0f63-483a-bc96-d8388ca419c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
But honestly, I'm a lot less interested in them right now. I'm interested in us. And the thing I'm most excited about from last week isn't just that we won. It's how we won.
Almost every person who won one of these big Senate, House, and governor's races started at a time that looked bleak for the Democratic Party. They ran against the media, the Republican Party and the internet, all telling us Democrats could never be anything.
I never believed that. I could see the destruction the Trump administration was causing, and I knew the pendulum would swing back. These candidates saw it too. They signed up anyway, before anyone knew a wave was coming, and that tells you exactly who they are. They believe in the power of this party.
Scott Colom is a prosecutor who looked at a state Democrats haven't won statewide in a generation and decided to run anyway. You don't make that choice for the career upside. You make it because you believe in an economy that works for everybody, in racial justice in a state that has fought it every step of the way, and in a better life for the people you want to represent.
The same goes for the rest of this class. Annie Andrews is a pediatrician who got into politics because she was tired of watching kids get hurt by policies written by people who'd never treated one. James Talarico is a former teacher who talks about faith and justice in a way that terrifies the Christian nationalists who think they own both. Josh Turek is a Paralympic gold medalist who knows what it means to fight for success. Troy Jackson is a logger from northern Maine who has spent his career taking on the corporations that screw over working people.
These people went through the wringer. They're younger, closer to the issues, and in this for the right reasons. We've elected plenty of Democrats before. I'm not sure we've ever elected this many true believers at once.
Now comes a messy presidential primary with a million candidates, and I'm looking forward to all of it. We'll debate, we'll pick someone, we'll rally behind them, and we'll go fucking win. If we elect another class like this in '28, we'll have an historic chance to make this country work for the working class again, root out the corruption in Washington, and end these stupid forever wars.
But none of this is guaranteed. The ground shifted under Republicans' feet last Tuesday, and it can shift under ours just as fast if we don't deliver. So we roll up our sleeves, we get shit done, and we make people's lives better.
Mississippi picked another senator. Don't let anyone tell you what's impossible ever again.

Neither am I.](https://substack.com/redirect/a71f6e92-0f63-483a-bc96-d8388ca419c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
With urgency,
--Mike

name: Jason Johnson
subject: 9 years because of THIS?

You’ve heard about Erik on the news. He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer.

| | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. **You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does.** And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.**This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood.** It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. clean_body: You’ve heard about Erik on the news. He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer. | | | | Dear Friend,I know you and I have never met. But I’m writing to you today because I’m desperate. | | | This is Erik, me, and our three children in the family photo.I wish I didn’t have to blur our faces. But with the death threats we’ve been getting, I couldn’t afford to take any chances.I should explain...You’ve heard about Erik on the news.He’s the NYPD Sergeant who threw a cooler at a fleeing drug dealer who was speeding a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk. | | | | | That day, my husband was working a drug operation at a park in the Bronx -- what they call a “buy-and-bust.”After an undercover officer “bought” cocaine from a drug dealer -- a known gang member with a mile-long rap sheet -- Erik’s fellow officers moved in.The drug dealer fled, jumping on a motorcycle and taking off down a crowded sidewalk at top speed, without a helmet.When my husband spotted the drug dealer, he was barreling straight toward where two officers were arresting another suspect.Erik knew if he didn’t act quickly, someone was going to be seriously injured -- maybe even killed.So my husband made a split-second decision. He grabbed the closest thing he could find -- a small cooler --and threw it at the motorcycle to stop the drug dealer before it was too late.Erik’s quick thinking that day saved lives -- the lives of his two fellow officers and the innocent bystanders who could have been hit. But sadly, the drug dealer crashed his motorcycle and died from his injuries. When he got home that night, Erik told me he felt terrible that someone died.But I knew he did what he needed to do to keep his fellow officers safe.And I thought it was obvious to anyone with half a brain knew that this drug dealer’s death, while tragic, was no one’s fault but his own. He was the one who joined a violent street gang...He was the one who sold deadly drugs in a park where kids play...He was the one who drove a motorcycle down a crowded sidewalk at top speed with no helmet on, putting himself and others in danger...But none of that mattered to the NY attorney general. You see, Letitia James is bankrolled by George Soros. And she’s filled her office with prosecutors who hate cops as much as she does. And five months after that fateful day......she charged Erik with Manslaughter.She didn’t just charge Erik. She and the other anti-cop activists here in New York turned the case into a media circus.They spent the next two years dragging his name through the mud and calling him a racist even though he is a proud Latino with immigrant parents.What did they expect my husband to do -- stand aside and let a drug dealer plow into the other cops with a motorcycle? Things only got worse at the trial.But not only did the judge find Erik guilty......he sentenced him to NINE YEARS in prison.The judge even told Erik he made the sentence especially tough as a “general deterrent” to other police officers!This is the upside-down world we live in now. A world where the lawyers and judges in our justice system care more about “deterring” cops from doing their jobs than they do about “deterring” criminals from hurting innocent people.It makes you wonder why anyone would want to be a police officer in this day and age.But becoming a police officer in New York City was a childhood dream for Erik. He grew up in the Bronx. His family and friends still live in the area.Erik always told me how proud he was that he got to go to work every day and help get the drugs, guns and crime out of his neighborhood.And when we were getting ready for the trial, we got a flood of letters from people who lived there. Letter after letter talked about how Erik is a man with a heart for the community.But most importantly, he’s a wonderful husband and an incredible dad to our three children.Telling them their father was going to prison was the hardest thing I’ve ever done.Our five-year-old couldn’t understand.Daddy was a police officer. He was one of the good guys. Why would he go to jail?After he was sentenced, Erik was locked up in Riker’s Island in awful conditions.He spent his days in solitary confinement in a dark, filthy cell with blood all over the walls.This is how Letitia James and Judge Guy Mitchell repaid my husband for 15 years of protecting his neighborhood. It’s disgusting.It’s unjust.And it’s just plain wrong.Thankfully, Erik’s lawyers told us he has a good chance at an appeal. And after we filed the appeal, the court set Erik free on bond.But as you know, the appeals process is incredibly expensive.I had almost given up hope.But thank the Lord, Erik is a godly man. Through it all, his faith has never wavered -- not once.On his way home from prison, he stopped at our local church to pray and ask God for help. You know that LELDF helps innocent law enforcement officers -- and their families -- fight for justice when there’s nowhere else to turn. Thanks to kind-hearted people like you, they get these officers the lawyers and expert witnesses they need to fight back against activist prosecutors and judges......and win.Friend, you’ve already read my email this far, so I’m going to come right out and ask: I know it’s strange to ask for your support in the very first email I’ve ever written you.But we have nowhere else to turn.Erik and I come from working-class families.We’re not wealthy.And with Erik being found guilty, we lost his salary and our medical benefits. We’re barely getting by as it is. because LELDF is a nonprofit, your gift is tax-deductible too.But whatever God is prompting you to give, please act quickly.Erik’s legal team needs to be working around the clock on this appeal.Because if we don’t fight this injustice, Erik will be imprisoned. And you know how police officers are treated in prison. And when you access the secure donation page, you’ll see there is a box where you can type a message— If you’re a believer like Erik, maybe you could write a short prayer. I know it will mean the world to him. Friend, for the past three years Erik told me something over and over again: “It’s not about the hardships. It’s about the people God sends into your life during difficult times to help you.” I pray that today you’ll be one of those people God uses to help our family.Thank you, and God bless you.Sincerely, Cynthia Duran P.S. My husband doesn’t deserve this. He’s a decorated police officer who spent his entire career serving and protecting his city. That day in the park, he saved lives. And for that, Letitia James wants him locked up for NINE YEARS.Please don’t let the cop-haters destroy another good man. | | | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. House Whip Katherine Clark, Elect Democratic Women chair Rep. Lois Frankel, and EDW executive board member Rep. Julia Brownley attend the GRAMMYs on the Hill Advocacy Day Awards Dinner on April 8, 2025 in Washington, D.C. Photo by Leigh Vogel/Getty Images for The Recording Academy.
Maybe they waited too long for the cake pops to come back around.
After 11 Democrats missed the vote to impeach War Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday, an ill-timed Tuesday reception hosted by the political action committee Elect Democratic Women (EDW) has become the focus of increasing attention. According to an RSVP list of the event obtained by Drop Site News, the party was studded with representatives of the country's top weapons makers and the city's most powerful defense contractor lobbying firms.
A motion from Republicans to effectively kill the impeachment resolution [passed 211-204](https://substack.com/redirect/99bca0c3-103b-468b-8107-abf71ef674d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Three of the missing Democrats blamed their tardiness on traffic getting back to the Capitol from an event.
The unexcused absences have sent an angry Democratic base, which was already clamoring for leadership changes in the House and Senate and an end to the war with Iran, all the way up the wall. The complete list of EDW partygoers is unlikely to calm anyone down.
The event, billed as a "New Member Reception," was expected to be attended by a slew of lobbyists for weapons makers, AI companies, crypto firms, insurance companies, Big Pharma, and others looking to press their case for federal largesse, according to the event RSVP list. EDW, chaired by Rep. **Lois Frankel**(D-Fl.), served as a major pass-through for **AIPAC** cash in the 2026 cycle. AIPAC's super PAC **United Democracy Project** [funneled at least ](https://substack.com/redirect/3662f1c8-0870-4640-b926-92844902f4b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)$2.35 million into EDW Action this year, according to federal campaign finance records.
The event was to be attended, according to the list, by 132 lobbyists, The defense industry was represented by at least two people from **Lockheed Martin** , as well as representatives from top defense lobbying firms like **Cornerstone Public Affairs** , **Invariant** , **Akin Gump** , **Porter Group** , **Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck** , **K &L Gates**, and **BGR Group**. AI and Big Tech were represented by lobbyists from **Anthropic** , **Google** , **Dell** , **Salesforce** , **Airbnb** , and **Intel**. Big Pharma had people from **PhRMA** , **Genentech** , **AstraZeneca** , **Blue Cross Blue Shield** , **CVS** , and **Elevance Health**. Prediction markets were championed by a **Kalshi** lobbyist while cryptocurrencies were advocated for by someone from **Coinbase**. And, for good measure, two lobbyists from **Bayer-Monsanto** , the company responsible for releasing the cancer-causing weed killer RoundUp, attended the bash. Major firms like **Walmart** , **Comcast** , and **Delta** were in attendance, as were a handful of major unions.
The event ran from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. House leadership scheduled the vote to impeach Hegseth at 5:30 p.m., and the vote closed at 6:05.
The "run of show" had Frankel giving remarks at 5:00, cutting it close to the vote time, given rush hour traffic down Pennsylvania Avenue from the venue, Goldfinch Social.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e17dad-f6db-4391-92ba-254a99796808?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Reps. **[Julia Brownley](https://substack.com/redirect/18833e7e-c47b-46ad-81b0-6949abf88e0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **(D-Calif.), **Melanie Stansbury**(D-N.M.), and **Brittany Pettersen**(D-Colo.) missed the vote and attended the event. Brownley is an executive board member of EDW and Stansbury is a board member. Eight others missed the vote-Reps. **Laura Gillen** , **Nancy Pelosi** , **Haley Stevens** , **Marilyn Strickland** , **Frederica Wilson** , **Jonathan Jackson** , **Steven Horsford** , and **Lou Correa**. Pelosi said she was attending a Veteran's Day event; Horsford cited a "personal emergency." Jackson made it to the steps of the Capitol on time and was seen filming a social media video before the vote was gaveled to a close, but inexplicably missed the vote. He said he is taking "full accountability." Stevens was endorsed by EDW but was thrown out of the Michigan Democratic Party for endorsing the Republican in the Michigan Senate race. She has been hanging out in the Republican cloakroom during votes.
"I am so sorry," Stansbury posted to social media Wednesday morning. "There is no one who is more disappointed in myself than me that I was not here the moment that that gavel dropped."
Pettersen has been less forthcoming. Drop Site reported Tuesday night that some members had been at an EDW event, and the local Colorado media [pressed Pettersen](https://substack.com/redirect/a1ef6336-c2a8-4c92-a08a-ec58415a2689?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as to whether she was one of them, but she initially declined to say, allowing only she had been "denied the ability to vote."
"Her team twice refused to tell us where she was. Our Marshall Zelinger found that Pettersen was at a Super PAC party," [Local9 News in Colorado](https://substack.com/redirect/8a1c8d9c-7aae-47ee-9dc8-7f05492a774e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reported.
"Last night I was late to the floor and there is no excuse for that," she said in a follow-up statement. "I was an Electing Democratic Women [sic] event celebrating the record-breaking number of new women members who were just elected, and unfortunately was significantly delayed with the blockade on Independence Avenue."

The Colorado [local news anchor went on](https://substack.com/redirect/8a1c8d9c-7aae-47ee-9dc8-7f05492a774e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "So why the hesitancy about being at an EDW event?" he asked, before explaining: "EDW Action is the Super PAC for EDW. It took in more than $2.3 million this year from a Super PAC affiliated with AIPAC, the group that helps elect congressmembers who support a strong relationship between the U.S. and Israel. Critics describe EDW Action as a conduit for AIPAC money."
The rest of EDW's executive board includes Reps. **Joyce Beatty** , **Debbie Dingell** , and **Norma Torres**. Board members include Reps. **Nikki Budzinski** , **Laura Friedman** , **Julie Johnson** , **Jennifer McClellan** , and **Jill Tokuda**. (Johnson lost a primary to Justice Democrat **Frederick Douglass Haynes** in Texas and is not returning to office.)
Frankel [quit the Congressional Progressive Caucus in November 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/ba82b6d8-18c9-45c6-b510-a4f28466f228?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over complaints that the caucus was too critical of Israel; she had previously been one of just six CPC members to vote to censure Rep. **Rashida Tlaib** for using the slogan, "From the river to the sea." Earlier this year, [according to Democratic candidate ](https://substack.com/redirect/e0ab372e-479a-4e61-bca3-b9005806516e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Jamie Belsito](https://substack.com/redirect/e0ab372e-479a-4e61-bca3-b9005806516e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[,](https://substack.com/redirect/e0ab372e-479a-4e61-bca3-b9005806516e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Frankel told Belsito that EDW could back her in a Massachusetts primary and funnel money from AIPAC, AI interests, and crypto companies into her race. When Belsito objected, saying she didn't want the money whether it was direct or through a pass-through, EDW endorsed a rival candidate (who lost to incoming freshman **Dan Koh**).
After the effort to impeach Hegseth failed, Democratic Whip **Katherine Clark** released a statement claiming, "Republicans just blocked the House from impeaching Pete Hegseth," calling the GOP "a disgrace" for "protecting an unqualified, incompetent man over our servicemembers."
Clark, during a meeting of her deputy whips Wednesday,[ told her colleagues](https://substack.com/redirect/723f3d01-4b40-4854-87ee-0466e857b32b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they had let the American people down.
She also reportedly noted that seven Republicans also missed the vote, so that even if Democrats had arrived in time, the GOP had votes to spare they could add to the board. It's not obvious that her claim is true. Only two of the seven Republicans who missed the vote won re-election last Tuesday, making it unlikely they would have been trying to abstain, as members sometimes do, so as not to face backlash in their districts.

subject: I can’t believe we need to talk about this

body:
The Secretary of Defense, the man trusted with the lives of every single American in uniform, was verbally reprimanded by a young, enlisted Tomb Guard for conduct unbecoming.
#
Peter —
Yesterday, Secretary Hegseth went for a Veterans Day photo-op at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington.
The Secretary of Defense, the man trusted with the lives of every single American in uniform, was verbally reprimanded by a young, enlisted Tomb Guard for conduct unbecoming.
They were talking, carrying on... even laughing, at that place of solemnity, dignity, and honor.
Frankly, I can’t believe it. I can’t believe we even need to talk about this. There has never been a Secretary of Defense, a White House, or a President like this. They disrespect us at every turn.
Donald Trump himself called the fallen “suckers” and “losers,” he has attacked Gold Star families, he trampled graves at Arlington, and now wants to overshadow those graves with a 250 foot tall arch dedicated entirely to himself.
This level of disrespect and disregard, at the place of highest honor in Arlington National Cemetery, should enrage every single American.
This is the attitude with which they approach the construction of the Arc de Trump. They laugh at us as they push ahead with their plans for the arch, even as Veterans, mayors, governors, and even the Kennedy family have taken them to court to stop it.
Peter, we cannot let them get away with this. We simply cannot let this go. And that is why I am asking you to make a donation today.
[**Donate $5, or anything you can afford, because every Veteran in the country needs to know about this. That’s how we’ll spread the word, and it’s how we’ll stop further dishonor of the fallen buried at Arlington.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov26.ldComW&refcode=em261112-1-misc&t=1&akid=35803%2E3013755%2EL5kZ1Y)

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: For the ones who believed early
body:
They wrote us off over and over again. Here’s something to remember it by.
# [](https://governorhinojosa.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
_Do you remember where you were the night Texas shocked the world?_
I do. I was in a room full of people who believed in this campaign back when it was still only familiar faces at our events. Hundreds of millions of dollars in attack ads. Written off over and over again. And there we were, hearing the results come in from McAllen and Lubbock, from Dallas and Corpus Christi, all the way out to Big Bend.
I want you to remember that night forever, so I asked my team to make something for you.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261112_1_remembersticker.DLbHwG&refcode=em20261112-2653&t=1&akid=2653%2E299639%2EWPt94A)
**[Chip in anything you can, even just $1, to help cover printing and shipping, and we’ll send you this limited-edition “I Remember Where I Was When We Took Back Texas” bumper sticker.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261112_1_remembersticker.DLbHwG&refcode=em20261112-2653&t=2&akid=2653%2E299639%2EWPt94A)**
Here’s what the national pundits still don’t understand about this race:**it was never about “flipping Texas blue.”**
We didn’t end one era of single-party rule just to usher in another. This was a fight for every Texan, whatever their party. It was about whether this state belongs to the people who built it, or to the billionaires and lobbyists who’ve gotten very comfortable running it.
When I decided to run, people told me Greg Abbott couldn’t be beaten. He had more than a hundred million dollars in the bank and one of the most entrenched political machines in the country.
But Texans have never minded being doubted. We ran with a Texas chip on our shoulder, and on Election Day, we answered loud enough for every lobbyist in Austin to hear: **Texas belongs to us.**
Well, team, we did it. We took Texas back.
This sticker is my thank-you to the people who were with us before the rest of the country woke up to what was happening here. Put it on your bumper, your laptop, your fridge, wherever you’ll see it. Because this was never just about one election. Taking back Texas means building a government that works for and belongs to its people, and that work starts now.
[**Chip in $1 or more and claim your limited-edition sticker before they’re gone.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261112_1_remembersticker.DLbHwG&refcode=em20261112-2653&t=3&akid=2653%2E299639%2EWPt94A)
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261112_1_remembersticker.DLbHwG&refcode=em20261112-2653&t=22&akid=2653%2E299639%2EWPt94A)
I’ll always remember where I was when we took back Texas. I hope you will too.
Gina Hinojosa

movement — lost overwhelmingly here in Pennsylvania and all across the
country.

ridiculous conspiracy theories about the safety and security of our

Donald Trump and his movement lost last week. And no amount of lies or
conspiracy theories will change that indisputable, undeniable fact.

united

Hi friends!

🎥 _ JOIN US: AFTER THE ELECTION_

The votes are in. Now let’s talk about what they mean. Join Rocky
Mountain Voice for a special post-election Zoom call, “After the
Election: A Midterm Analysis & Look Ahead,” on Friday, November 13
at 9:00 a.m. MT.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

We’ll break down the midterm results, discuss Colorado’s place in
the nation and what happens next, and share an update on the Road to
Red 2034, now in year three of a ten-year plan. We’ll also cover
growth plans for Rocky Mountain Voice. _RSVP HERE!

here

or watch on YouTube
