🏔️ HERE IN COLORADO... Democrats are set to hold two-thirds of
both legislative chambers
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and Senate Republican Lisa Frizell says blocking bills now takes seven
crossover Democrats instead of six; backers of Props 133, 134 and 135
launched a petition urging lawmakers to implement them as approved
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
Jeffco Schools and the U.S. Department of Education agreed to
“indefinitely pause” their Title IX litigation
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
and the state treasurer says 18 military decorations, including five
Purple Hearts, await veterans and their families
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Steve Scalise (R-LA) 106-73 to lead House Republicans into the
minority
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
telling colleagues that “offense, not defense, wins elections.”

graduated income tax will eventually collect less than expected
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
citing Montana’s experience; and Greg Walcher writes that the
American chestnut is returning
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
after USDA deregulated Darling 54.

This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, November 12, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

COLORADO’S NEW SUPERMAJORITY: SIX LEGISLATORS SAY NEITHER PARTY IS
UNITED
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Democrats hold two-thirds of both chambers of the Colorado
legislature, enough to put constitutional amendments on the ballot and
override a governor’s veto without a single Republican vote.

Asked what they intend to do with it, two of the three Democrats who
answered RMV said the caucus is not going to vote as one. Asked the
same questions, two Republicans said the same thing about theirs.

RMV sent the same questions to every returning legislator and to the
incoming members who already have legislative email addresses. Rep.
Naquetta Ricks, Sen. Tom Sullivan and Rep. Lisa Feret answered by
email or written statement. House Minority Leader Jarvis Caldwell
answered through his communications director. Sen. Lisa Frizell and
Rep. Brandi Bradley sat for phone interviews.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

THE SILVER LININGS IN AMENDMENT 87: COLORADO’S NEW TAX WILL
EVENTUALLY COLLECT LESS
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

INDEPENDENCE INSTITUTE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Independence Institute senior fellow Rob Natelson argues Colorado’s
new graduated income tax will backfire economically, driving investors
and businesses to neighboring states with far lower rates._

*
A TAX HE SAYS WILL SHRINK REVENUE, NOT GROW IT: Natelson argues
progressive income taxes drive out investors, discourage new
residents, and deter entrepreneurs from expanding businesses, pointing
to Montana’s past experience with a similar tax as a cautionary
precedent.

*
A COMPETITIVE DISADVANTAGE AGAINST NEIGHBORING STATES: The piece lists
several competing states that have cut or eliminated income taxes,
including Nevada, Wyoming and South Dakota with none at all, and
Arizona, Montana and Oklahoma all cutting top rates well below
Colorado’s new structure.

*
A “SILVER LINING” FRAMED AS FORCED RESTRAINT: Natelson contends
that because the tax will ultimately generate less revenue than
advertised, it may force the legislature to cut spending on programs
he criticizes, including state dollars he says go to underperforming
schools and health programs.

COLORADO VETERANS: FROM DACHAU TO CAMP HALE, 13 RESOLUTIONS AND A
MEMORIAL’S UNFINISHED LIST
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | NOVEMBER 11

_On the morning of April 29, 1945, soldiers of the 157th Infantry
Regiment set foot inside Dachau. The 157th had Colorado National Guard
roots and fought as part of the U.S. Army’s 45th Infantry Division.
House Joint Resolution 26-1011 calls it the Colorado National
Guard’s 157th._
__

COLORADO IS BUILDING HOMES AGAIN: JUST NOT THE SINGLE-FAMILY KIND
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | NOVEMBER 10

_Colorado builders pulled permits for 33,754 new housing units in
2025, according to the U.S. Census Bureau’s Building Permits Survey.
That beat 2024 by almost 5 percent. Permits authorize construction, so
they measure what builders intend to put up rather than what gets
finished._
__
__

__

A REPUBLIC, IF YOU CAN KEEP IT: THE DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE IS THE
TEST

| | | Peter, Last week’s historic blue wave was a mandate from the people. Democrats everywhere won by running on a Working Families agenda to lower costs, curb corporate corruption, tax the billionaires, and end the war in Iran. But already, we’re seeing some party leaders and pundits try to downplay this momentum shift, or saying that now isn’t the time to make too many demands. **That’s a load of crap.** 84% of Democrats want Medicare for All.1 74% oppose US military and economic aid to Israel.2 And 67% support a moratorium on data centers.3 Voters have made it clear what their demands are this year. And thanks to the 16 WFP champions we’re sending to the U.S. House and the 2 to the U.S. Senate, we have a rare opportunity to actually _enact_ those demands. **[Now we need to put all of our pressure on the naysaying Democratic establishment, and fight to pass a true Working Families agenda. clean_body: | | | Peter, Last week’s historic blue wave was a mandate from the people. Democrats everywhere won by running on a Working Families agenda to lower costs, curb corporate corruption, tax the billionaires, and end the war in Iran. But already, we’re seeing some party leaders and pundits try to downplay this momentum shift, or saying that now isn’t the time to make too many demands. That’s a load of crap. 84% of Democrats want Medicare for All.1 74% oppose US military and economic aid to Israel.2 And 67% support a moratorium on data centers.3 Voters have made it clear what their demands are this year. And thanks to the 16 WFP champions we’re sending to the U.S. House and the 2 to the U.S. Senate, we have a rare opportunity to actually enact those demands. Here’s the bottom line: our goal isn’t just to win elections; it’s to pass policies that make people’s lives better. And Democratic leaders will be judged on whether or not they deliver on their promises to make life more affordable, take on corporations and the billionaire class, and stop Big Tech from running roughshod over our communities. We have been handed the power; now we must use it. In solidarity, Team WFP Sources: 1\. , KFF , October 6, 2026 2\. , Al Jazeera , May 21, 2026 3\. , Data For Progress , June 23, 2026 Thoughts? _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3991%2E259176%2EIzZj4h) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3991%2E259176%2EIzZj4h)_

**In the final hours, when the provisional ballots were counted, we won the race for North Carolina’s 3rd Congressional District.**

It is the honor of my life to be chosen to serve in the place where I was born and raised.

From the beginning, folks across the country wrote us off – from the media to our own Republican opponent. On Election Night, we were neck-and-neck. Greg Murphy declared victory late that night, but after every voice was heard, we pulled ahead. We will win this election when it’s certified.

**Republicans gerrymandered this district to try to keep control of their power. But working families down east had a different plan: Together, John, we beat them and added another critical seat to our new Democratic House Majority.**

I heard the concerns of the people of this district, and I’m ready to work to lower costs, provide affordable healthcare, and make sure everyone here can get ahead and build a good life right here at home.

I’ll go to Washington every day remembering who sent me and who I work for. Thank you to every voter, volunteer, and neighbor who powered our grassroots campaign.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you – **Dr. Raymond E. Smith, Jr.**

### [Maine's $1 billion budget problem: How does Hannah Pingree react?](https://substack.com/redirect/0b620b24-7d19-45b0-97e8-477fcf0c5e15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Maine's next governor starts January facing a projected gap in the state budget. The Bureau of the Budget's [revised forecast](https://substack.com/redirect/75d91862-c440-4610-8e4f-b7744a6eeda7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) projects a General Fund gap of about $1.096 billion for the 2028-2029 biennium, plus a $256.7 million Highway Fund gap. The deficit is driven, per the forecast, primarily by Medicaid welfare ($345 million) and maintaining the 55% school funding mandate ($280.7 million).
The new far-left majorities in Augusta will inevitably want to "tax the millionaires" to keep the spending going, but here's the thing: This gap already includes the Democrat millionaire's tax, the 2% surcharge on high-earners' incomes. Based on testimony submitted by Mills Administration officials when that "millionaires' tax" was up for debate, Maine only has roughly $5 billion of taxable income above the $1 million per year threshold. That means if Democratic lawmakers want to tax their way out of this welfare fraud black hole -- and it very obviously is a _**welfare**_ _**fraud**_ black hole -- then they'll have to increase the millionaire's surcharge tax to 17.5% -- which would give Maine nearly double the highest top marginal tax rate in the country.
How did Maine's budget crisis explode to such a staggering degree? Comparing FY2018 spending to FY2026 spending is illustrative: Health & Human Services spending increased by $1 billion -- 44% of all spending growth during the eight-year period. Cutting spending to erase the looming budget deficit will require about a 24% cut in spending at DHHS, or 12-13% cuts at both DHHS and the Department of Education (or some other more creative combination of cuts). My prediction, however, is that the far-left Democrats will instead look not only to increase the "millionaire's tax" but to also lower the threshold so it applies to far more than just those making more than $1 million per year. As a bonus prediction: These tax increases will actually end up _decreasing_ state revenue because of behavioral changes, i.e., high earners leaving the state to avoid paying for free needles, Somali welfare fraud, and some of the worst schools in the nation.

### [Maine Awarded $190 Million in Second-Year Federal Funding to Support Rural Health Care](https://substack.com/redirect/5a6f9dd7-d375-4eaf-98a2-4f20f0f02777?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Maine has been awarded more than $190 million for the second year of the Rural Health Transformation Program, a $50 billion, five-year federal program ($10 billion a year nationwide) that the Maine Wire says Sen. Susan Collins (R) proposed during negotiations over amendments to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Collins said Maine will receive $190 million "plus additional funds to reflect the progress the State has made in implementing the program." She said earlier money from the program has already been used to protect Penobscot Community Health Center from bankruptcy. Gov. Janet Mills (D) welcomed the award and thanked Collins, Sen. Angus King and Reps. Jared Golden and Chellie Pingree.
### [MaineHousing Proposes $1.1 Million Contract for Preble Street to Coordinate Maine's Homeless Service Hubs](https://substack.com/redirect/6656d0e4-7208-4eea-b118-6e90f94318a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you're wondering who will run the state's homeless response, MaineHousing wants it to be Preble Street... the same people who've been involved in the state's homelessness response. The agency proposed a contract of about $1.1 million (proposed, not yet paid) that would put the infamous Portland nonprofit in charge of hiring and supervising the coordinators for all nine regional hubs. Eight agencies shared that job until now. MaineHousing says it reviewed three proposals, and the contract is set to start Dec. 1. MaineHousing Director Dan Brennan said the change "will let the hubs keep doing their good work in a focused and efficient way." The announcement didn't say how the money gets divided or how anyone will measure whether it works, and it didn't mention Portland's Aug. 28 inspection of Preble Street's Elena's Way shelter, which rated the safety-monitoring requirement "Not Met" because required evening patrols still weren't happening. Preble Street has said the report didn't accurately reflect its work.
Jon Fetherston went to Preble Street on Wednesday to ask whether this is a good idea and was apparently assaulted by a Preble Street ally. In the video Fetherston says he's standing on a public sidewalk and says he's going to get a police officer. Preble Street is one of Maine's largest left-wing, taxpayer-funded NGOs, and its income has grown as homelessness, drug addiction, and vagrancy have spiraled out of control.

Maine's stalwart commitment to rejecting economic growth in favor of poverty and government jobs has continued with the new Chinese Communist-backed crusades against data centers. Eight Maine towns have adopted restrictions on AI data centers. Most chose temporary moratoriums, and North Berwick adopted a permanent ban with 78% of the vote. Wells voters backed their moratorium with 82%, and Eliot and Peru each passed theirs with more than 76%.
Gov. Janet Mills (D) vetoed a statewide pause earlier this year because the bill had no exemption for a proposed project at the former Androscoggin Mill in Jay. Lawmakers fell short of the two-thirds needed to override. The Maine Wire says paperwork reportedly filed with the Department of Environmental Protection shows discussions about the Jay site have been reopened. In Thursday's update, Fetherston says the developer claims the project would create as many as 1,000 construction jobs and about 150 permanent positions, and that Gov.-elect Pingree has expressed reservations. He says Maine needs jobs and that the numbers, the environmental requirements and the economic benefits should be examined before anyone decides. Libby Palanza has the story.
### [Pests Persist at Solterra Weeks After City of Portland Documented Building-Wide Cockroach Infestation](https://substack.com/redirect/35582622-556a-4e54-baeb-39b9959c1bf0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Residents of the Solterra Apartments in Portland are still living with pests weeks after the city documented them. The Maine Wire says it visited the building Nov. 9 and quickly gathered dozens of bedbugs. City records show an Oct. 16 inspection marked the property "In Violation" for a "roach infestation throughout the entire building," with a reinspection set for Oct. 23. The version of the record the Maine Wire got doesn't say what that reinspection found. A lobby notice says pesticides may be applied Friday, Nov. 13. Resident Allison Decato's emails show a city employee said he had asked an inspector to issue a plumbing violation notice when he's back in the office Nov. 12, and the email gave no inspection date.

Rep. Benjamin Hymes says a property tax break that covers all Maine veterans is now law and takes effect April 1, 2027. In the Maine Wire's Veterans Day video, Hymes says he passed the idea in two earlier Legislatures, where it died on the Appropriations table without funding. This year he asked the governor's office to put it in the supplemental budget, and he says it passed. He says his bill, LD 888, was the framework and was "basically carbon copied" into the budget, with an April 1, 2027, start instead of April 1, 2026. He says the size of the benefit depends on a veteran's age, disability status and a few other things. The post doesn't give a dollar amount.

Eight towns vote to restrict data centers; MaineHousing proposes about $1.1 million for Preble Street -- Fetherston gets their response on the street. Plus, the math problem facing the Pingree Admin. Nov 12 | | | | | | | | | | | Paul LePage won the 2nd Congressional District on Election Day. On Thursday, it was confirmed that Secretary of State Shenna Bellows would not be able to use the magic of Ranked Choice Voting (RCV) to deprive the GOP candidate of a victory, as happened in 2018. "The Maine Ranked Choice Voting process only confirmed what we already knew, Paul LePage is the Congressman-Elect for Maine's 2nd Congressional District," said Brent Littlefield, senior advisor to Rep. LePage. "As Paul said, he will work with anyone, regardless of Party, to put Maine first," said Littlefield. Sadly, LePage will arrive in Washington, D.C., just in time to have a front-row seat to the end of the Trump Era. With Democrats controlling the U.S. House of Representatives by a comfortable 40+ seats, the only orders of business will be investigations, retribution, and impeachment attempts. Maine's next governor starts January facing a projected gap in the state budget. The Bureau of the Budget's projects a General Fund gap of about $1.096 billion for the 2028-2029 biennium, plus a $256.7 million Highway Fund gap. The deficit is driven, per the forecast, primarily by Medicaid welfare ($345 million) and maintaining the 55% school funding mandate ($280.7 million). The new far-left majorities in Augusta will inevitably want to "tax the millionaires" to keep the spending going, but here's the thing: This gap already includes the Democrat millionaire's tax, the 2% surcharge on high-earners' incomes. Based on testimony submitted by Mills Administration officials when that "millionaires' tax" was up for debate, Maine only has roughly $5 billion of taxable income above the $1 million per year threshold. That means if Democratic lawmakers want to tax their way out of this welfare fraud black hole -- and it very obviously is a welfare fraud black hole -- then they'll have to increase the millionaire's surcharge tax to 17.5% -- which would give Maine nearly double the highest top marginal tax rate in the country. How did Maine's budget crisis explode to such a staggering degree? Comparing FY2018 spending to FY2026 spending is illustrative: Health & Human Services spending increased by $1 billion -- 44% of all spending growth during the eight-year period. Cutting spending to erase the looming budget deficit will require about a 24% cut in spending at DHHS, or 12-13% cuts at both DHHS and the Department of Education (or some other more creative combination of cuts). My prediction, however, is that the far-left Democrats will instead look not only to increase the "millionaire's tax" but to also lower the threshold so it applies to far more than just those making more than $1 million per year. As a bonus prediction: These tax increases will actually end up decreasing state revenue because of behavioral changes, i.e., high earners leaving the state to avoid paying for free needles, Somali welfare fraud, and some of the worst schools in the nation. We read the fine print so you don 't have to. Maine has been awarded more than $190 million for the second year of the Rural Health Transformation Program, a $50 billion, five-year federal program ($10 billion a year nationwide) that the Maine Wire says Sen. Susan Collins (R) proposed during negotiations over amendments to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Collins said Maine will receive $190 million "plus additional funds to reflect the progress the State has made in implementing the program." She said earlier money from the program has already been used to protect Penobscot Community Health Center from bankruptcy. Gov. Janet Mills (D) welcomed the award and thanked Collins, Sen. Angus King and Reps. Jared Golden and Chellie Pingree. If you're wondering who will run the state's homeless response, MaineHousing wants it to be Preble Street... the same people who've been involved in the state's homelessness response. The agency proposed a contract of about $1.1 million (proposed, not yet paid) that would put the infamous Portland nonprofit in charge of hiring and supervising the coordinators for all nine regional hubs. Eight agencies shared that job until now. MaineHousing says it reviewed three proposals, and the contract is set to start Dec. 1. MaineHousing Director Dan Brennan said the change "will let the hubs keep doing their good work in a focused and efficient way." The announcement didn't say how the money gets divided or how anyone will measure whether it works, and it didn't mention Portland's Aug. 28 inspection of Preble Street's Elena's Way shelter, which rated the safety-monitoring requirement "Not Met" because required evening patrols still weren't happening. Preble Street has said the report didn't accurately reflect its work. Jon Fetherston went to Preble Street on Wednesday to ask whether this is a good idea and was apparently assaulted by a Preble Street ally. In the video Fetherston says he's standing on a public sidewalk and says he's going to get a police officer. Preble Street is one of Maine's largest left-wing, taxpayer-funded NGOs, and its income has grown as homelessness, drug addiction, and vagrancy have spiraled out of control. Maine's stalwart commitment to rejecting economic growth in favor of poverty and government jobs has continued with the new Chinese Communist-backed crusades against data centers. Eight Maine towns have adopted restrictions on AI data centers. Most chose temporary moratoriums, and North Berwick adopted a permanent ban with 78% of the vote. Wells voters backed their moratorium with 82%, and Eliot and Peru each passed theirs with more than 76%. Gov. Janet Mills (D) vetoed a statewide pause earlier this year because the bill had no exemption for a proposed project at the former Androscoggin Mill in Jay. Lawmakers fell short of the two-thirds needed to override. The Maine Wire says paperwork reportedly filed with the Department of Environmental Protection shows discussions about the Jay site have been reopened. In Thursday's update, Fetherston says the developer claims the project would create as many as 1,000 construction jobs and about 150 permanent positions, and that Gov.-elect Pingree has expressed reservations. He says Maine needs jobs and that the numbers, the environmental requirements and the economic benefits should be examined before anyone decides. Libby Palanza has the story. Residents of the Solterra Apartments in Portland are still living with pests weeks after the city documented them. The Maine Wire says it visited the building Nov. 9 and quickly gathered dozens of bedbugs. City records show an Oct. 16 inspection marked the property "In Violation" for a "roach infestation throughout the entire building," with a reinspection set for Oct. 23. The version of the record the Maine Wire got doesn't say what that reinspection found. A lobby notice says pesticides may be applied Friday, Nov. 13. Resident Allison Decato's emails show a city employee said he had asked an inspector to issue a plumbing violation notice when he's back in the office Nov. 12, and the email gave no inspection date. Rep. Benjamin Hymes says a property tax break that covers all Maine veterans is now law and takes effect April 1, 2027. In the Maine Wire's Veterans Day video, Hymes says he passed the idea in two earlier Legislatures, where it died on the Appropriations table without funding. This year he asked the governor's office to put it in the supplemental budget, and he says it passed. He says his bill, LD 888, was the framework and was "basically carbon copied" into the budget, with an April 1, 2027, start instead of April 1, 2026. He says the size of the benefit depends on a veteran's age, disability status and a few other things. The post doesn't give a dollar amount. Rep. Barbara Bagshaw (R-Windham) lost to Democrat Bradley Youngs by 139 votes, 2,637 to 2,498 (unofficial), and has asked for a recount. On WVOM on Nov. 6, she said same-day registration lines in Windham were filled with people she described as "foreign-looking," and she said she asked the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to check everyone who voted that day against its SAVE citizenship database. Maine allows registration until the polls close. Windham Town Clerk Anthony Blasi told the Portland newspaper the town didn't see an unusual number of registrations for a statewide election and that a rush in the final hours is common. At 2.7% of the vote, Bagshaw's margin means a $500 deposit applies. Secretary of State Shenna Bellows has previously admitted that noncitizens are registered to vote in Maine; however, she has also refused to provide Maine's Central Voter Registration (CVR) file to the federal government so noncitizens can be removed from the rolls. Rockland police arrested Crystal Parmenter, 41, of Waldoboro, on Monday while investigating a report of suspected drug trafficking at a local hotel. Officers say she was the subject of an active warrant charging her with being a felon in possession of a firearm, and they arrested her on it. A search warrant on the hotel room allegedly turned up suspected narcotics. Police say the drug investigation is ongoing and more charges are pending. The Penobscot County Sheriff's Office asked the public Tuesday for help finding Brittany Wood, 36, of Eddington. A deputy stopped her Sunday, seized suspected drugs and, the Maine Wire reports, says he had to prevent her from destroying evidence. She wasn't arrested on scene, for unspecified reasons. Deputies say testing later confirmed the drugs, and she refused repeated requests to surrender, so they got a warrant charging her with unlawful possession of scheduled drugs, falsifying physical evidence and violating conditions of release. She was out on bail after the May 31 overdose of an infant, whose life was saved by an officer using Narcan, and was charged then with felony domestic violence aggravated assault and endangering the welfare of a child. A Sagadahoc deputy stopped a car on I-295 in Bowdoinham at 12:05 a.m. Tuesday after clocking it at 90 mph, according to the sheriff's department. Police say the driver, Lawz R. Lepenn, 44, of Auburn, who is on probation for an aggravated drug trafficking conviction, ran. The chase reached 120 mph before state troopers put down spikes near Exit 109 in Augusta. Police say he then ran into the woods and a State Police drone spotted him near the Augusta airport. They say he dropped a sports bag on the highway that held more than three pounds of cocaine. He's charged with aggravated trafficking and eluding and is held without bail at Two Bridges Regional Jail because of the probation violation. The Information reported Tuesday that Alice Huang, the former CEO of the Singaporean company Megaspeed, used her ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the company's distributors to help move at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips to Chinese tech firms since 2023, according to the Daily Caller News Foundation. The two are not related. An Nvidia spokesperson told the DCNF the company sells its data-center GPUs "primarily to well-known partners" who "work with us to ensure that all sales comply with U.S. export control rules," and Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." Jensen Huang confessed to the affair in a Sunday company email. Drones can find a generator by its noise and heat, and the Army is shopping for hybrid battery systems so small teams can shut the generators off. Chariot Defense CEO Adam Warmoth, whose company sells hybrid power systems, told the Daily Caller News Foundation the choice is to "turn off the generator, but then lose all of my communications, all of my sensors" or "leave it on and be a target." Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-N.C.), an Army veteran on the House Armed Services Committee, said, "You've just given away your position." Videos from @TheMaineWire on X Anti-ICE protesters across from a Veterans Day event. The Maine Wire's Wednesday post calls it a "shocking lack of respect" and says anti-ICE protesters showed up across from a Veterans Day event. In the clip, someone off camera asks the protesters whether they're protesting a Veterans Day event and whether that's disrespectful to veterans. Freedom isn 't free. The Maine Wire's post calls it "some inspiring perspectives this Veterans Day," with veterans talking about what the day means to them. " This park is high school." No reporter in Maine has spent more time engaging with Maine's homeless community than Joe Sokol (except for maybe Jon Fetherston), and he shares a look at what life was like for those living in Davenport Park over the summer. Here's Wednesday's episode... Today's Political Events Legislative recount schedule : The Secretary of State's office said it would post a schedule after the Nov. 10 request deadline and hasn't announced a date. name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: Your input matters, friend.
body:
|
#
Friend, Last week, mid-Michigan sent me back to Congress – and this time, I’ll be serving in a new Democratic majority. Thank you, truly, for placing your trust in me. Now, it’s time to get to work. Too many families are being squeezed by rising costs while the wealthy and well-connected rig the system in their favor. I’ve heard it again and again from folks across mid-Michigan. People are playing by the rules, working hard, and doing everything right – and it’s still not enough to get ahead. With a Democratic majority, we finally have the chance to change that – rooting out corruption at every level, protecting essential programs like SNAP and Medicaid, and fighting for real solutions that lower costs for everyone. **But you know better than anyone what you need us to get done. clean_body: | Friend, Last week, mid-Michigan sent me back to Congress – and this time, I’ll be serving in a new Democratic majority. Thank you, truly, for placing your trust in me. Now, it’s time to get to work. Too many families are being squeezed by rising costs while the wealthy and well-connected rig the system in their favor. I’ve heard it again and again from folks across mid-Michigan. People are playing by the rules, working hard, and doing everything right – and it’s still not enough to get ahead. With a Democratic majority, we finally have the chance to change that – rooting out corruption at every level, protecting essential programs like SNAP and Medicaid, and fighting for real solutions that lower costs for everyone. But you know better than anyone what you need us to get done. As my team and I build our priorities for the new term, I want your voice in the room. | I look forward to reading your responses. More soon, Kristen | We'd hate to see you go, but you can click here if you'd like to . Thank you for supporting Kristen McDonald Rivet for Congress! Kristen for Michigan P.O. name: Pennsylvania Working Families Party
subject: A huge win for working families in Allegheny County!💜
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pennsylvania Working Families Party
body:
12 weeks of paid parental leave, and a historic victory for working parents! | | | Peter, We've got some pretty exciting news to share from Western Pennsylvania! 💜 **Last month, Allegheny County made history, becoming the first county in the country to pass a law guaranteeing _12 weeks_ of paid parental leave for eligible working parents!** That's a _huge_ deal. For too long, working parents have been forced to choose between taking time to care for their newborns and bringing home a paycheck. This new policy, which will begin rolling out next year, is a major step toward making sure more families have the time and support they need during one of the most important moments of their lives. **And what makes this victory even more exciting is how it happened.** For months, parents, nurses, union members, and community organizers came together to make this possible. They knocked on doors, made calls, organized rallies, and shared their stories with County Council, all to make sure the voices of working families were heard. And all that hard work paid off! The PA Working Families Party was proud to stand alongside Pennsylvania United, SEIU Healthcare PA, and so many other incredible organizations as part of the Parental Leave to Help Families Thrive coalition. We're also grateful to County Executive Sara Innamorato and the County Council members who helped turn this campaign into a real victory for working families. This is exactly the kind of change we’re fighting for: **policies that make a real difference in people’s everyday lives and give working families the support they deserve.** We’re so proud of everyone who helped make this happen. But we’re not stopping here. Millions of working people across Pennsylvania still don’t have guaranteed paid parental leave. Allegheny County just showed what’s possible when we organize together, and we’re going to keep fighting until every working family has the support they deserve. **[Wll you chip in $10 today to help I didn’t write this note quickly.

I typed it, stepped away from it, came back to it, and kept asking myself if I was saying this the right way.

Because what I’m asking of you is not small.

Dear Peter,

A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana.

Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her.

Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were:

_" I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana. **Not now, not ever.** "_

The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don't count.

**That 's what abortionist "shield laws" do. **They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label!

Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm President of Students for Life of America. I've spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I've never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen.

The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back.

Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down.

**I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America.**

For years, we've been told abortion is now "a state issue."

_If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,_one mailbox at a time__.

Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I've carried with me for most of my adult life:

_" I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?"_

I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today.

[Will you make a generous tax-deductible gift right away to help us stand with the pro-life states in this fight](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=60515d8367914e269489df5e4d568b95&_e=cXdOzelZe3jAkEThAht6ZTAusY6tbmTK5xa3JxkdRh9hWyvMTEXlB2FhD7E9oUGzYCc0n3uNIQBC81qY__QGanrxdSpa1vlu9tNrgqY1k_pvaHspPB5eVo3Fpcv2T4HH4yF5ckRzsH8nZ8dGaIsbU8D4kM4GsbWylY53XtcpwCVtfdNi7R74-PRp1N54qIkNCQ_SDhXsR0XDPIrH4bxyhGosmYSmcMOiP1CwihX7dEEdGyou1RBmqNy-_nvIAJBUpQMAiuQtotT38y1l_zuiNeOu5W2cB1p1XIU7E0M6M9ObtrBKlP4ErVDtBhueuCDWIuTK92WggdHXVX0BBEWLCEtd-T0tHlE-Y7TmQfyj0CfiCLe1c1ienx4ClMLIcq9fwSNxR-rCCZVUZVWXGYdpgr10mE2ZeTMPPCoCDt8PvwjyuROMx96B_Gdx4F4uA7uT7Eu294-gkAC-OSC5Ym_eDxl7MJxBrt4D7OXAgOWT8JMcRG2fwcdn9bcgrLGFqmio6oQPaQI_ajaEAlPcixDhNthm14HlUyHdn9bgrqOmqB6AeLp12YihKkAN5eHEx23Sfw9ubDkuF_atoelQl5S39nfpn6LJBy2SMhGxwp-GP7lgDmJdg7LESAHuLlmn1SlHwwbLYSL613afXo1EvJDic4v9BnsEl8AwhOhbN3PXQLgK8mTiLvghncMsrZWFm0KNHXJQgqXX7hq-tyuk0gU8DJzvqW0JNcWonLrx2f3Fr22hEm_DkTSz-jwjBTIh5ZfpPq4D17ceqWz5uJrl01T-LuAMdoytShA-UqTsJW5oP8KXbwvJ_pxReB8qgIEd9xCbalIL4i60gg-KlDJkHn6M7L8D-GVyo1fUwOcHO5sxbCvTrbsW9qGK9xREoNwohid3)**?**

The Solicitor General is the federal government's lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that's John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands.

That means the Trump Administration's voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation.

President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. **If that 's true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government's help protecting the laws their people passed.**

And right now, they aren't getting enough of it.

The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills.

That's why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what's being shipped through the mail.

Louisiana's attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn't list the prescriber or a single risk.

Louisiana's attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: _**" It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes."**_

And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state's pro-life laws.

Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year.

_And the women who take these deadly pills?_

A study from the _Ethics & Public Policy Center _recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. **That 's at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug's own label!**

Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . .

Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years.

When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations.

Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation's water and the endangered species that live in it.

And now, we're preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We've also done this before and seen the impact.

On the opening day of the Supreme Court's term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up.

_Roe v. Wade_ had been called "settled law" for 48 years.

Eight months later, it was gone.

I won't tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. **But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible.**

This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand.

But I can't get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills.

clean_body: Dear Peter, A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana. Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her. Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges. New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were: " I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana. Not now, not ever. " The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don't count. That 's what abortionist "shield laws" do. They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label! Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this. My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm President of Students for Life of America. I've spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I've never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen. The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back. Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down. I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America. For years, we've been told abortion is now "a state issue." If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,one mailbox at a time. Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I've carried with me for most of my adult life: " I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?" I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today. ? The Solicitor General is the federal government's lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that's John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands. That means the Trump Administration's voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation. President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. If that 's true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government's help protecting the laws their people passed. And right now, they aren't getting enough of it. The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills. That's why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what's being shipped through the mail. Louisiana's attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn't list the prescriber or a single risk. Louisiana's attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: " It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes." And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state's pro-life laws. Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year. And the women who take these deadly pills? A study from the Ethics & Public Policy Center recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. That 's at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug's own label! Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . . Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years. When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations. Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation's water and the endangered species that live in it. And now, we're preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We've also done this before and seen the impact. On the opening day of the Supreme Court's term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up. Roe v. Wade had been called "settled law" for 48 years. Eight months later, it was gone. I won't tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible. This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand. But I can't get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills. : >> $25 puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop. >> $50 covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits. >> $100 launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials. >> $250 helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out. >> $500 helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event. Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind. Governor Hochul defiantly said "not now, not ever." I'd like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I'd like you standing with me when we do. Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her. For Life, Kristan Hawkins President, Students for Life P.S. - Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. subject: About the midterms
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY POWERED BY PEOPLE
body:
[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1001&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Powered by People[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1002&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Powered by People

Take a look at this spreadsheet showing the impact we had in 12 Texas
State House races.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261112.No2-AK&refcode=ema20261112-241175&t=1004&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Spreadsheet showing the numbers of Powered by People voters who were
contacted, confirmed voted/turned out, the Democratic victory margin, and
the percentage of PxP voters versus those margins

While we met, verified registration and personally stayed in touch with
more than 113,000 primarily young Texas voters statewide, it was in these
key districts where our organizers and volunteers made the critical
difference.

It’s how Powered by People helped Democrats win control of the State House
for the first time in 24 years.

Our organizing philosophy is that people connecting with people — human to
human — is the most powerful political force in a democracy. Money,
technology and media all play a role, but none can match what we can do
when we meet our fellow Texans where they are, have real conversations
with them about what’s most important in their lives and then help them to
register and vote so that they can change what’s possible in our country.

Thousands of volunteers, supported by a dozen organizers and a highly
focused support staff, spent hundreds of thousands of hours on college
campuses, in clubs, at concerts, coffee shops, community centers —
everywhere we could think to find young Texans — to do the work that
works.

When it was 108-degrees in Tarrant County this August, we were outside on
the campus of UT Arlington meeting the 18 and 19-year old freshmen to give
them a chance to register and vote. When it was 40-degrees and windy this
past January, a cold rain pelting our faces, we were on the UT Austin
campus doing the same.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261112.No2-AK&refcode=ema20261112-241175&t=1005&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Two Powered by People volunteers in high-visibility vests holding
clipboards standing with university students

We worked at Community Colleges, Historically Black Colleges and
Universities, flagship public universities like A&M, UT and Tech, and
private colleges like Rice and Paul Quinn.

We posted up at Kacey Musgraves’ concerts, Alyssa Edwards’ shows, and at
smaller venues with local artists. We showed up at Sparta’s Texas shows
and registered fans there too.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261112.No2-AK&refcode=ema20261112-241175&t=1006&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Two people working on their voter registration, one writing on a
clipboard and the other holding their phone

Our volunteers stood outside of churches and mosques, greeting
parishioners and offering to check and update their voter registrations.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261112.No2-AK&refcode=ema20261112-241175&t=1007&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]A Powered by People volunteer sitting with someone in a mosque

We helped recruit the down-ballot candidates that won key Congressional
and state legislative seats, and we ran innovative vote-by-mail programs
that personally followed up with eligible voters in key contests, like
Taylor Rehmet’s special State Senate election in Tarrant County earlier
this year.

And most importantly, we personally stayed in touch with each one of the
113,000+ voters that we met, answering their questions about voting,
sending them important information about polling locations and personally
encouraging them to vote until we could confirm they’d cast their ballot.

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261112.No2-AK&refcode=ema20261112-241175&t=1008&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Gray message: "Hey, Claudia! I did vote a few hours ago! First time
voting 🎉🎉" ; Blue message: "You're awesome!! 💙 Democracy thanks you!"

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261112.No2-AK&refcode=ema20261112-241175&t=1009&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Grey message: "Hey Mary!! 🥹💙 Thank you so much!! I appreciate you
reaching out and keeping me informed! I'll definitely keep you in my
contacts for the next time. Thank you for everything you do! 🥳 💙" ; Blue
text: "Dang! You made my day, week, etc! Enjoy your weekend and hope we
get great results next week!!"

At the end of the day, 73.3% of the new and young Texans that we met,
registered and stayed in touch with voted. By comparison, the overall
turnout statewide was 51.6% and for young people not in our program it was
35%.

That’s how we made the difference in close elections and it’s how we
contributed to the gigantic victories won by Gina Hinojosa and James
Talarico.

And we did this all in a state that has no online voter registration, no
same-day registration and no automatic registration; a state where, in one
of the most competitive counties, 92 polling locations were closed,
including at the University of Texas at Arlington campus with 42,000
students; a state where the Attorney General, Ken Paxton, sued to stop us
from doing this work and cost our organization more than $600,000 in
attorneys’ fees; a state that passed laws in the last legislative session
targeting Powered by People in an effort to keep us from organizing on
college campuses.

I started Powered by People because I believed that if more young people
voted, we would have a better state. Better leaders making better laws. An
end to the corruption, cruelty and incompetence that has defined our state
government under Abbott, Paxton and Patrick. I knew that in a state that
makes it tougher than any other for young people to vote, we have to work
that much harder to make sure that they do.

You supported this vision and our program and together we ran one of the
most effective and successful organizing efforts in the country. I look
forward to building upon these victories by scaling the size of our
program, investing in the systems and people that can help us reach more
young voters, and recruiting even more volunteers to ensure that we are
ready to win in 2028, 2030 and beyond.

Thank you for your contributions, your encouragement and your faith in
people-centered grassroots organizing. It has been an honor to work with
you and our Powered by People team and I look forward to what we can do
together in the days and years to come.

Beto

[ https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261112.No2-AK&refcode=ema20261112-241175&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1010&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu ]Donate

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to act. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe: https://act.betoorourke.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=1011&akid=241175%2E444211%2E3ubWbu

subject: Schumer: Step aside
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Our Revolution click here to unsubscribe
body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

The calls for Schumer to step aside as Senate leader are growing — and
they're coming from everywhere.

The Machinists union, which has 600,000 members, sent Schumer a letter
saying it's time for "a new generation" to lead Senate Democrats. Everyone
from Abdul El-Sayed to Troy Jackson to more centrist senators like Elissa
Slotkin are now joining the call, saying it's time for new leadership.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40039?source=email-20261112&t=1011&akid=11587%2E5885482%2EGyhGVI ]Headline: Machinists union calls on Schumer to step aside as leader

Our Revolution members agree, with 73% saying Chuck Schumer is NOT the
right person to lead Senate Democrats in our recent survey. That's the
message from the grassroots, and it's the one every single Senate Democrat
needs to hear loud and clear before they choose the next leader.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40039?source=email-20261112&t=1012&akid=11587%2E5885482%2EGyhGVI ]ADD YOUR NAME: Tell Democrats that it's time for Schumer to step aside
— it's time for new Senate leadership.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40039?source=email-20261112&t=1013&akid=11587%2E5885482%2EGyhGVI ]ADD YOUR NAME

The day after the polls closed, Schumer announced: "I'll be reelected as
Majority Leader."

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40039?source=email-20261112&t=1014&akid=11587%2E5885482%2EGyhGVI ]Headline: ‘I’ll be reelected as majority leader,’ Schumer says

It's not his call to make.

This is about whether the people who built this victory get to shape what
comes next, or whether it goes to leaders who expect to keep their jobs
out of habit.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40039?source=email-20261112&t=1015&akid=11587%2E5885482%2EGyhGVI ]Graphic reading: TIME’S UP, CHUCK. A quote from Our Revolution’s Joseph
Geevarghese in USA Today reads: Chuck Schumer should step down as Senate
Minority Leader. The graphic shows Chuck Schumer looking down at his
wristwatch.

We need leaders willing to fight: for working people, against corporate
power, and against an administration that spent two years attacking our
rights. We need leaders who understand that this majority exists because
voters wanted change, not more of the same.

Schumer has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade. This is the moment
to turn the page. But it won't happen unless senators hear from us, and
fast. Every signature adds to the pressure, and every message from a
constituent makes it harder for a senator to wave this off as noise.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40039?source=email-20261112&t=1016&akid=11587%2E5885482%2EGyhGVI ]Add your name now: Tell Senate Democrats, no on Schumer. We need new
leadership.

Millions of us organized, volunteered, knocked doors, made calls, and
fought to win back the House and Senate and elect a new generation of
progressives. WE did the work to win — delivering a clear mandate for
change. WE should have a say in who leads the party.

When we organize, we win.

name: David Reid
subject: I have to tell you something
body:
It’s important

| |
---
Peter, Election season is over. We’ve all exhaled. Now I want to tell you what I’m thinking about next. In January, I’ll head back to Richmond for another General Assembly session, and I have to tell you, I’m excited. A long list of work lies ahead: affordability bills that pick up where last session left off, education policy that keeps delivering for Virginia students, child welfare conversations that I’ve started building toward with the Foster Care Special Interest Group, voting rights work that will matter more than ever heading into 2027, and more. I’m ready to do all of it. But before I can get there, I need to ask you for one more push. Virginia law bars state legislators from fundraising during the General Assembly session. That means the window between now and the second Wednesday in January is the only time I can raise what my campaign needs to carry us through the first half of 2027—the organizing, staffing, and communications infrastructure that keeps me connected to HD-28 while I’m working in Richmond. **Lea el boletín en español abajo**

**Receiving a shout-out for our years of engaging voters across Texas** ** ** Organizing isn't just how we win policies to improve lives, it's how we build political power in our communities and win elections. This is central to TOP's theory of change. Expanding the electorate and engaging Black and Latino Texans year-round for now over 16 years contributed to this historic midterm result in our state. We helped flip Texas, and we're proud to have worked alongside our members, supporters, and allies to have gotten to this watershed moment! TOP is honored to be included as a nominee by D.D. Guttenplan of The Nation for PVP (Particularly Valuable Player) in last Tuesday’s election victories. 🏆 [Read the article here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143355153/659937521/-614545101?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNVE8vMS80NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMjkxZGFjMy1kYmRlLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vqRTumzC3Th91I0LwwSYIcb-wOXEBOb7-aC1Q0C0rXM=&emci=5cf6b85a-c8de-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&emdi=c291dac3-dbde-f111-91f0-000d3a18e244&ceid=227997)
**Celebrating the midterm results and charting next steps for our communities** We’re hosting dinners this week to celebrate with our communities and share how we reached this point this election, as well as how we use our collective power to now win meaningful change with new leaders elected into office. Bring your family, friends, and neighbors! We held our Houston dinner Tuesday, and we have two more dinners tonight in Fort Worth and San Antonio. For more information, email David at [dvillalobos@organizetexas.org](mailto:dvillalobos@organizetexas.org). Fort Worth:
Thursday, Nov. 12
6 - 8 p.m.

1819 Nevada St. **Recognizing Veterans Day** TOP is proud to recognize the invaluable contributions of our veterans — particularly Black and Latino veterans across Texas — for the role they play everyday in moving our state and nation forward. Veterans of all walks are integral parts of our families and communities, and we are honored to build power alongside TOP staff and members who have served.

**Español** **Recibimos elogios por nuestros años de trabajo con votantes a través de Texas** Organizarnos no solo nos permite lograr políticas que mejoren vidas, sino también construir poder político en nuestras comunidades y ganar elecciones. Esto es fundamental para la teoría del cambio de TOP. Ampliar el electorado e involucrar a los texanos negros y latinos durante todo el año, por más de 16 años, contribuyó al histórico resultado de las elecciones de medio término en nuestro estado. Ayudamos a que Texas cambiara de rumbo, ¡y nos enorgullece haber trabajado junto a nuestros miembros, simpatizantes y aliados para llegar a este momento crucial! Celebramos nuestra cena en Houston el martes, y esta noche tendremos dos cenas más en Fort Worth y San Antonio. Para más información, envíen un correo electrónico a David a [dvillalobos@organizetexas.org](mailto:dvillalobos@organizetexas.org). Los veteranos de todos los ámbitos son parte esencial de nuestras familias y comunidades, y nos honra construir fortaleza junto al personal y los miembros de TOP que han servido a nuestro país.

body:
The Democrat AG targeting me just won in a landslide. Now she’s emboldened like never before to pursue her sham charges against yours truly!
| Peter,
---
Unfortunately, I have some devastating news.
---
The vindictive Democrat Attorney General who is targeting me just won her reelection in a _landslide_.
---
When my lawyers had informed me that any day now, this AG could call a NEW grand jury to RESTART her sham case against me, I immediately knew what was on the line for me in the midterms.
---
Sadly, the shocking election results only make my situation that much more dire.
---
**_This Democrat AG is now more emboldened than ever to come after me with her false charges and phony _state-level_ case in which she knows President Trump cannot save me with a federal pardon! _**
---
While every word in this letter is the honest-to-God truth of where things stand for me – and it may currently look bleak – please rest assured that I will _NEVER_ _SURRENDER_ to the lunatic Left’s final witch hunt against me.
---
I’ve been to hell and back defending myself against the Democrats and their Deep State goons...
---
_They raided my home at dawn.
Arrested me alongside President Trump as innocent men.
Froze my bank accounts.
Seized my assets.
And forced me to the point of bankruptcy.

subject: America needs to remember
body:
The legacies of our veterans are too important to forget

| | | |
---
Friend,
---
During World War II, when I passed another Black soldier, we didn't need to say a word. We just held up two fingers in a V.It stood for "Double Victory." Victory over fascism overseas, and victory over racism here at home.My name is Enoch "Woody" Woodhouse. I'm 99 years old, and I'm one of the last of the Tuskegee Airmen.I grew up in Roxbury, in Boston, in a family of preachers. After Pearl Harbor, my mother encouraged me to serve. So, in 1944, I graduated from English High School and enlisted at 17, along with about 20 of my classmates. My brother became one of the first Black Marines trained at Montford Point.
---
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2u2zAMRp9G3q5h_dhWBw0FggAdblGgQ0eBoRiHqGW5opy8fpE23TrdleR3Dgn-eI_vwCtvy1fIFFgkVomQqTLCRpSklUqZ8oVqNIOZ3rR-0yYCNr5TdNClMBrtr76joOdPbtTezHN3C6MBBzjNaA360WoHo794e8WrNR6vQ8fhydNaG6P1PE794AdM82Rd0v7iHCo3HHuCRj1vwokES9n3snJjlL7UpVvDrbVdlP2szFmZsxAelfp_69-pUYVNkLZG9ZlQ5gx3jMtB0qLwslGVP2fFRynpVg4hZc9SjooUsSRS9vTl-zc9mdFbZaaj5Zgp8ZGVPVEGXl_FvxFlTzeoCeRnBPz1aiHkHXjZlD393_2aa1Sf1K6GtD94XVmmWblheVp6LLlrH3nPPZjfAQAA___E4aLy)
---
I passed the exams for flight training. Then the Army ended the program before I could start. I went to officer school instead, and at 19, I was commissioned as a second lieutenant.**Friend, some of the hardest moments of my service had nothing to do with the enemy.** Once, traveling by train, a porter told me, "We don't ride that train," and I had to wait for the next one.At officer school in Texas, I waited 40 minutes for a table in the dining hall. When they finally seated me, it was behind a screen that walled me off from everyone else.I couldn't eat that steak. I just couldn't. For eight weeks, I lived on hot dogs, hamburgers, and milkshakes from the snack bar. But I didn't quit. I became a finance officer with the Tuskegee Airmen, which meant I was the paymaster. Back then, you didn't write checks. You paid in cash._I had the most important job on base. Everybody knew me._**And I served with the finest men I've known in my life, no matter their race.**
---
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2u2zAMRp9G3q5h_dhWBw0FggAdblGgQ0eBoRiHqGW5opy8fpE23TrdleR3Dgn-eI_vwCtvy1fIFFgkVomQqTLCRpSklUqZ8oVqNIOZ3rR-0yYCNr5TdNClMBrtr76joOdPbtTezHN3C6MBBzjNaA360WoHo794e8WrNR6vQ8fhydNaG6P1PE794AdM82Rd0v7iHCo3HHuCRj1vwokES9n3snJjlL7UpVvDrbVdlP2szFmZsxAelfp_69-pUYVNkLZG9ZlQ5gx3jMtB0qLwslGVP2fFRynpVg4hZc9SjooUsSRS9vTl-zc9mdFbZaaj5Zgp8ZGVPVEGXl_FvxFlTzeoCeRnBPz1aiHkHXjZlD393_2aa1Sf1K6GtD94XVmmWblheVp6LLlrH3nPPZjfAQAA___E4aLy)
---
After the service, I went to Yale and then Boston University law school, and I practiced law for more than 40 years.In 2007, the Tuskegee Airmen received the Congressional Gold Medal, and the President of the United States saluted us to make up for all the salutes we never got. People sometimes call my story Black history. To me, it isn't. _It's American history. Our history._ And I've lived long enough to believe that somehow, somewhere, we Americans get our act together and do the right thing.**But only if we remember, Friend.** That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. This November, I joined AVC in Washington and shared my story with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen, the young men and women who will lead our military next.
---
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2u2zAMRp9G3q5h_dhWBw0FggAdblGgQ0eBoRiHqGW5opy8fpE23TrdleR3Dgn-eI_vwCtvy1fIFFgkVomQqTLCRpSklUqZ8oVqNIOZ3rR-0yYCNr5TdNClMBrtr76joOdPbtTezHN3C6MBBzjNaA360WoHo794e8WrNR6vQ8fhydNaG6P1PE794AdM82Rd0v7iHCo3HHuCRj1vwokES9n3snJjlL7UpVvDrbVdlP2szFmZsxAelfp_69-pUYVNkLZG9ZlQ5gx3jMtB0qLwslGVP2fFRynpVg4hZc9SjooUsSRS9vTl-zc9mdFbZaaj5Zgp8ZGVPVEGXl_FvxFlTzeoCeRnBPz1aiHkHXjZlD393_2aa1Sf1K6GtD94XVmmWblheVp6LLlrH3nPPZjfAQAA___E4aLy)
---
AVC recorded it, so it will be there long after I'm gone - and that's why I'm so passionate about AVC's work. _They make sure America never forgets the service and sacrifice of our veterans._ AVC is a nonprofit educational organization. Its mission is to preserve and promote the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes:
---
* **The National Memorial Day Parade** in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event
* **The Annual Veterans Conference** every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen
* **AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes,** a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide
* **Oral histories and documentaries** that record veterans' stories in their own words, so they're never forgotten

---
AVC is funded entirely by people like you, and every gift is tax-deductible. _**[Friend, will you join me with a gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can give today, so the stories of every American who served are remembered and passed on to the next generation?](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2u2zAMRp9G3q5h_dhWBw0FggAdblGgQ0eBoRiHqGW5opy8fpE23TrdleR3Dgn-eI_vwCtvy1fIFFgkVomQqTLCRpSklUqZ8oVqNIOZ3rR-0yYCNr5TdNClMBrtr76joOdPbtTezHN3C6MBBzjNaA360WoHo794e8WrNR6vQ8fhydNaG6P1PE794AdM82Rd0v7iHCo3HHuCRj1vwokES9n3snJjlL7UpVvDrbVdlP2szFmZsxAelfp_69-pUYVNkLZG9ZlQ5gx3jMtB0qLwslGVP2fFRynpVg4hZc9SjooUsSRS9vTl-zc9mdFbZaaj5Zgp8ZGVPVEGXl_FvxFlTzeoCeRnBPz1aiHkHXjZlD393_2aa1Sf1K6GtD94XVmmWblheVp6LLlrH3nPPZjfAQAA___E4aLy)**_
---
[ **Yes, I'll Help America Remember the**
**Legacies of Our Veterans**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2u2zAMRp9G3q5h_dhWBw0FggAdblGgQ0eBoRiHqGW5opy8fpE23TrdleR3Dgn-eI_vwCtvy1fIFFgkVomQqTLCRpSklUqZ8oVqNIOZ3rR-0yYCNr5TdNClMBrtr76joOdPbtTezHN3C6MBBzjNaA360WoHo794e8WrNR6vQ8fhydNaG6P1PE794AdM82Rd0v7iHCo3HHuCRj1vwokES9n3snJjlL7UpVvDrbVdlP2szFmZsxAelfp_69-pUYVNkLZG9ZlQ5gx3jMtB0qLwslGVP2fFRynpVg4hZc9SjooUsSRS9vTl-zc9mdFbZaaj5Zgp8ZGVPVEGXl_FvxFlTzeoCeRnBPz1aiHkHXjZlD393_2aa1Sf1K6GtD94XVmmWblheVp6LLlrH3nPPZjfAQAA___E4aLy)
---
I still hold up two fingers in a V now and then. These days, the victory I'm after is making sure America never forgets the men and women who served. _**[I hope you'll join me and AVC in securing that victory with your most generous gift today.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckb2u2zAMRp9G3q5h_dhWBw0FggAdblGgQ0eBoRiHqGW5opy8fpE23TrdleR3Dgn-eI_vwCtvy1fIFFgkVomQqTLCRpSklUqZ8oVqNIOZ3rR-0yYCNr5TdNClMBrtr76joOdPbtTezHN3C6MBBzjNaA360WoHo794e8WrNR6vQ8fhydNaG6P1PE794AdM82Rd0v7iHCo3HHuCRj1vwokES9n3snJjlL7UpVvDrbVdlP2szFmZsxAelfp_69-pUYVNkLZG9ZlQ5gx3jMtB0qLwslGVP2fFRynpVg4hZc9SjooUsSRS9vTl-zc9mdFbZaaj5Zgp8ZGVPVEGXl_FvxFlTzeoCeRnBPz1aiHkHXjZlD393_2aa1Sf1K6GtD94XVmmWblheVp6LLlrH3nPPZjfAQAA___E4aLy)**_

clean_body: The legacies of our veterans are too important to forget | | | | Friend, During World War II, when I passed another Black soldier, we didn't need to say a word. We just held up two fingers in a V.It stood for "Double Victory." Victory over fascism overseas, and victory over racism here at home.My name is Enoch "Woody" Woodhouse. I'm 99 years old, and I'm one of the last of the Tuskegee Airmen.I grew up in Roxbury, in Boston, in a family of preachers. After Pearl Harbor, my mother encouraged me to serve. So, in 1944, I graduated from English High School and enlisted at 17, along with about 20 of my classmates. My brother became one of the first Black Marines trained at Montford Point. I passed the exams for flight training. Then the Army ended the program before I could start. I went to officer school instead, and at 19, I was commissioned as a second lieutenant.Friend, some of the hardest moments of my service had nothing to do with the enemy. Once, traveling by train, a porter told me, "We don't ride that train," and I had to wait for the next one.At officer school in Texas, I waited 40 minutes for a table in the dining hall. When they finally seated me, it was behind a screen that walled me off from everyone else.I couldn't eat that steak. I just couldn't. For eight weeks, I lived on hot dogs, hamburgers, and milkshakes from the snack bar. But I didn't quit. I became a finance officer with the Tuskegee Airmen, which meant I was the paymaster. Back then, you didn't write checks. You paid in cash.I had the most important job on base. Everybody knew me.And I served with the finest men I've known in my life, no matter their race. After the service, I went to Yale and then Boston University law school, and I practiced law for more than 40 years.In 2007, the Tuskegee Airmen received the Congressional Gold Medal, and the President of the United States saluted us to make up for all the salutes we never got. People sometimes call my story Black history. To me, it isn't. It's American history. Our history. And I've lived long enough to believe that somehow, somewhere, we Americans get our act together and do the right thing.But only if we remember, Friend. That's why I'm writing to you on behalf of the American Veterans Center. This November, I joined AVC in Washington and shared my story with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen, the young men and women who will lead our military next. AVC recorded it, so it will be there long after I'm gone - and that's why I'm so passionate about AVC's work. They make sure America never forgets the service and sacrifice of our veterans. AVC is a nonprofit educational organization. Its mission is to preserve and promote the legacy of America's veterans and active-duty service members, from World War II through today. Its work includes: The National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C., the nation's largest Memorial Day event The Annual Veterans Conference every Veterans Day weekend, where veterans of every generation share their stories with hundreds of cadets and midshipmen AMERICAN VALOR: A Salute to Our Heroes, a two-time Emmy-winning special broadcast nationwide Oral histories and documentaries that record veterans' stories in their own words, so they're never forgotten AVC is funded entirely by people like you, and every gift is tax-deductible. I still hold up two fingers in a V now and then. These days, the victory I'm after is making sure America never forgets the men and women who served. With gratitude, Enoch "Woody" Woodhouse II Lt. Colonel & original Tuskegee Airman On behalf of American Veterans Center | | | The mission of the American Veterans Center and the World War II Veterans Committee is to preserve and promote the legacy and experiences of America's veterans and active duty service personnel from World War II through today. A non-profit educational organization, the AVC and WWIIVC are funded solely through generous contributions from people like you. All contributions are tax-deductible. body:
Thinking ahead.
#
Peter,
**This election cycle might be over, but Voto Latino doesn’t take a break.**
In fact, right now, our team is mapping out our game plan for reaching Latino voters in 2027 and 2028.
We’re doing this because the victories we won in 2026 aren’t guaranteed to last — we have to continue working with our community year-round to ensure we’re keeping Latino voters engaged.
Every year, hundreds of thousands of young Latinos turn 18 and become eligible to vote, and if we want to protect what we built this year and win even bigger in 2028, we can’t wait until the next election to reach them. We have to keep our foot on the gas right now.
Your support right now is what keeps Voto Latino organizing, registering new voters, and showing up for Latino communities heading into 2027 and 2028.
